docs.text: Why do some terms differ from what I'm used to? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select uses a consistent set of terms to describe assets , locations , work, and inventory . These might differ from the terms you use today or in other systems. If you're not sure what a term means, click any underlined term in this help center to see its definition and related terms. This list brings those definitions and common alternatives together in one place. Assets and equipment ¤ Asset ¤ Any piece of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure that your organization maintains. You might know this as: equipment, machine, or unit Want to know more? What is an asset ? · How do I classify assets ? · How do I track asset history? Work and maintenance ¤ Work order ¤ A request or instruction to perform maintenance work. It records what needs to be done, where, who did it, what parts were used, and how long it took. This record stays with the asset as part of its maintenance history. You might know this as: maintenance order, job, ticket , or work request Want to know more? What is a work order ? · How do I complete a work order ? Plan tab ¤ The Plan section of a work order is where you record what is expected before work starts: the tasks to perform, materials to request, and labor needed. When actual work happens, those details are recorded separately in the Actuals section. Comparing plan to actuals lets you see whether jobs came in on time and on budget. You might know this as: planned work, work plan, or expected materials Work log ¤ A record of notes and updates added directly inside a work order . Use the work log to describe what you found, what you did, and anything else the next person needs to know. Entries are time-stamped and show who wrote them. You might know this as: job notes, maintenance notes, or technician notes Communications log ¤ A record of emails, notifications, and messages sent or received in connection with a work order . The communications log captures the conversation around the work, such as approval requests, status updates, and alerts. It is separate from the work log, which is for internal notes. You might know this as: message history, notification log, or email log Preventive maintenance ¤ Scheduled routine maintenance performed to prevent equipment failures. You might know this as: maintenance plan, planned maintenance, or PM Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance? Corrective maintenance ¤ Maintenance performed to fix equipment that has broken down. You might know this as: breakdown maintenance, repair work, or reactive maintenance Want to know more? How do I decide what work should be done? · What happens when an asset fails? Job plan ¤ A template that defines standard tasks, materials, and labor for recurring maintenance work. You might know this as: standard job, task template, or maintenance procedure Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance? Status ¤ The lifecycle state of a work order or record. You might know this as: lifecycle state, order state, or workflow stage Want to know more? How do I complete a work order ? Locations and sites ¤ Location ¤ A functional location or operating area where assets are installed or work is performed. You might know this as: functional location , area, or site area Want to know more? What is a location ? Site ¤ A data partitioning concept that represents a plant, facility, or business unit. You might know this as: plant, facility, or business unit Want to know more? What are the basic concepts? People, roles, and access ¤ Person and role ¤ A person record holds an individual's contact details and is used across the system to identify who owns, supervises, or reports on work. A role, also called a security group , determines what applications and actions that person can access. When you add a user, you assign them to a security group . The security group defines the role. The person record and the user account are separate, though they are linked. You might know this as: user type, access level, or permission group Want to know more? How do I add users? · How do I assign the correct people? Security group ¤ A collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. You might know this as: permission group, access group, user group, or role Want to know more? How do I add users? Authorized users ¤ The number of authorized users defines how many people are entitled to access the product under your subscription. When you add a new user account, it counts against this limit. If you reach the limit, you cannot add more users until entitlement is increased. Contact your IBM account representative to adjust your authorized user count. You might know this as: licensed users, named users, or seat count People and skills ¤ Labor ¤ Work time and effort assigned to a work order . You might know this as: technician time, work hours, or crew time Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Craft ¤ A trade or skill type required for maintenance work. You might know this as: trade, skill type, or discipline Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people? Inventory and materials ¤ Inventory ¤ Materials and spare parts stored for maintenance work. You might know this as: stock, stores, or warehouse Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job? Item and material ¤ An item is the master record for a part or material in the catalog, such as a filter or a seal. Material is the same thing in the context of a work order : materials are items requested or used for a specific job. The word changes depending on where you are in the system, but they refer to the same physical thing. You might know this as: spare part, stock item , or consumable Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job? Material request, reservation, and issue ¤ These three terms describe the sequence of getting parts to a job: Material request : You ask for the parts, tools, or services that a job needs. A request can be linked to a work order or made without one. Reservation : When materials are specified on an approved work order or task, the system can reserve the items in the storeroom automatically. A submitted material request can also create a reservation. A reservation holds the stock so it is not allocated to another job before yours. Issue : When you physically take the parts and use them, you issue them against the work order . This deducts the quantity from inventory and records the cost. You might know this as: pick list, parts request, stock allocation, or materials withdrawal Rotating item ¤ A repairable spare part that can be tracked individually by serial number. You might know this as: repairable spare, rotable, or serialized spare Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? Tracking and monitoring ¤ Meter ¤ A counter that tracks equipment usage, such as hours, cycles, or miles. You might know this as: counter, runtime meter , or odometer Want to know more? How do I detect issues early? Failure code ¤ A standardized code used to categorize and track equipment failures. You might know this as: failure classification, breakdown code, or fault code Want to know more? What happens when an asset fails? Downtime ¤ The period when equipment is not operational or available for use. You might know this as: outage, production loss, or equipment unavailable Want to know more? How do I reduce downtime ? · How do I detect issues early? Service requests ¤ Ticket ¤ A service request or incident report. You might know this as: service request, incident, or request Want to know more? What are the basic concepts? Configuration and data ¤ Object structure ¤ Defines the records and related fields that are available for importing, exporting, or exchanging data. You might know this as: data structure, import template, or record definition Want to know more? Which object structure do I use for each data type? · How do I get data into the system? Domain ¤ A list of valid values attached to a field that controls what users can select in a dropdown. You might know this as: value list, lookup list, or picklist Want to know more? How do I customize dropdown values? Communication template ¤ A reusable email template that can be triggered automatically by a workflow or escalation , or manually from a record. You might know this as: email template, notification template, or message template Want to know more? How do I automate communication? Escalation ¤ An automated rule that monitors the system for a condition and performs an action or sends a notification when that condition is met. You might know this as: alert rule, automated notification, or trigger Want to know more? How do I automate communication? · How do I act on alerts? People and teams ¤ Crew ¤ A named group of workers assembled to complete a job together, assigned as a team to a work order . You might know this as: work crew , team, or work gang Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people? Data sync ¤ The process of transferring record, lookup, and map data between the server and a mobile device. You might know this as: synchronization, offline sync, or data refresh Want to know more? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? User interface ¤ Default application ¤ The application that opens when a user logs in. Users can set their own default application in their profile preferences. Administrators can also set defaults for a security group . Choosing the correct default means users land on the most relevant application for their role without extra navigation. You might know this as: home screen, landing page, or startup application Start Workflow ¤ A workflow is an automated sequence of steps that routes a record through an approval or review process. "Start Workflow" is the action that begins this process for a specific record. Once started, the record follows a defined path, such as routing a work order to a supervisor for approval, and the system handles the routing automatically. You might know this as: submit for approval, begin approval process, or route for review Share with admin ¤ The "Share with admin" action sends a copy of information or a report to a system administrator. Administrators receive the information and can act on it, such as reviewing a configuration issue or adjusting access. The exact content and outcome depends on where in the system you use the action. You might know this as: send to admin, notify administrator, or escalate to admin API calls ¤ An API call is a request your system makes to Maximo Application Suite Select to exchange data automatically. For example, sending a new work order from an external system counts as one API call. Subscription plans include a defined number of API calls per period. If you integrate other systems with Maximo Application Suite Select, each data exchange uses some of this allowance. You might know this as: system integrations, data requests, or integration transactions Upgrade ¤ In Maximo Application Suite Select, Upgrade refers to moving to a higher subscription tier or adding capacity to your account. This gives you access to additional features, more users, or higher usage limits. You might know this as: subscription upgrade, plan upgrade, or adding capacity Basemap ¤ The background map layer that shows geography, streets, or satellite imagery. You might know this as: background map, base layer, or map tile Want to know more? How do I set up maps? Operational dashboard ¤ A landing page to monitor KPIs, manage upcoming assignments, complete tasks, or access related applications. You might know this as: command center, control panel, or operations console Want to know more? What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is an asset ? What is a work order ? What is a location ?

docs.text: Administrator: Add users ¤ Get started quickly with a task designed for administrators like you. Learn the basics while accomplishing something useful. Add a new user to the system and assign them appropriate access, for example, add users for Ice cream plant A. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Use consistent naming conventions for user IDs Follow principle of least privilege, that is, minimum access needed Keep security group assignments organized What to do ¤ Add a user ¤ Open the Users application. Click Create user . Specify a login email . Specify a user ID . Optionally, add a note in the memo . Example: Temporary access for contractor at ice cream plant A Provide a display name . This is the full name of the user or a recognizable preferred name. Click Select groups and add the user to at least one security group . An email is sent to the login email address. Table 1: Security groups ¤ A security group is a collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. A role determines what a person can see and do in Maximo Application Suite Select. Assign each user to the security group that matches their role: Security group What they can do System admin Manages system configuration and user access. System administrators can configure domains , communication templates , AI settings, create users, and set up security groups , but typically do not perform day-to-day operational work. Example tasks: Set up notification templates, manage user roles, set up security groups , configure system settings, and maintain data structures. Supervisor Oversees operations and team activities. Supervisors can plan and approve work, review technician work, monitor assets and performance, and access analytics to track progress. Example tasks: Assign and approve work orders , review KPIs, review inspection results, manage job plans , and monitor asset condition and maintenance schedules. Technician Performs maintenance and operational work. Technicians can view and update assigned work, complete inspections, record labor hours, report materials used, and record asset data such as meter readings and condition details. Example tasks: Complete work orders , enter inspection results, update asset condition, record labor hours, report materials used, and report meter readings. Requester Submits and tracks service requests. Requesters have limited access and cannot perform operational or administrative tasks. This role is focused on initiating and monitoring work requests. Example tasks: Create a service request for a broken asset and track its status until it is resolved. Inventory clerk Manages inventory and storeroom operations. Inventory clerks can maintain stock, process item movements, adjust inventory balances, and ensure accurate inventory records. Example tasks: Receive items into inventory , issue materials to work orders , perform inventory counts, adjust inventory balances, and manage storerooms. Note You must assign at least one security group . The user cannot access applications until a security group is assigned. User preferences ¤ Users update their preferences in their profile. They open the profile menu from the top right of the header and can select preferences, such as a default application , storeroom, locale, and language. What success looks like ¤ You've successfully added your first user when: User can log in successfully User sees appropriate applications and menus Security group permissions work as expected User can perform tasks for their role No error messages or access issues You'll know you're ready to move on when you can create users efficiently, assign appropriate permissions, and troubleshoot access issues independently. Once you've added your first user, setting up the rest of your team follows the same steps, just repeated at scale. Continue building your skills ¤ Set up your workforce ¤ After adding users, create the craft and labor records that let you assign work to the correct people. How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Customize your dropdown values ¤ Add your organization's terminology to status fields and dropdowns so the system speaks your team's language. How do I customize dropdown values? Set up maps ¤ Let your team see assets , work orders , and service addresses on a map inside the application. How do I set up maps? Automate your notifications ¤ Set up communication templates and push notifications so people hear about assignments and status changes without being told. How do I automate communication? Configure Maximo Mobile for field teams ¤ Set the defaults that control how mobile devices sync data and which map app your team uses. How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? Load your existing data ¤ Bring in your locations , assets , and inventory . Start by learning the order that avoids import errors. Then plan your location hierarchy and asset hierarchy . What is the correct load order? Need help? ¤ If you get stuck on your first task: Check Starting out for answers to common questions Review the basics in What are the basic concepts? docs.text: How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile lets you view assigned work, complete work orders , assign and approve work, issue parts, and update records from your phone or tablet. Technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks all use IBM Maximo Mobile. Note IBM Maximo Mobile is also used with IBM Maximo Manage. If you see references to Maximo Manage, you can ignore them. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Download the app before your first shift, not during it. Sign in with the same credentials you use on the desktop. docs.text: Inventory clerk: Issue a part ¤ Get started quickly with a task designed for inventory clerks like you. Learn the basics while accomplishing something useful. Issue a part from the storeroom to a work order , for example, issue parts from Main storeroom. Guided steps available: Prefer to learn in the application? Log in and open your Operational dashboard to follow guided steps for issuing a part. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Always verify item numbers before issuing Keep storeroom organized and labeled Issue parts promptly to avoid work delays Record transactions immediately Check for reorder needs after issuing What to do ¤ Check for work orders needing parts. Review the parts list. Note the work order number. Go to Inventory application. Search by item number or description. Check the storeroom location . Verify quantity available. Go to the storeroom. Find the correct bin location . Verify the item number matches. Check the part condition. In Maximo, open the inventory record. Click Issue Current Item . Enter the work order number. Specify quantity to issue. Confirm the transaction. Check that inventory balance decreased. Verify work order shows the material. Confirm cost was recorded. Hand over the physical part to technician. What success looks like ¤ You've successfully issued your first part when: Inventory balance decreased by the correct quantity Work order shows the material issued with cost Transaction recorded with work order number Physical part delivered to technician Storeroom bin location updated if needed System and physical inventory match No errors or warnings in the transaction You'll know you're ready to move on when you can issue parts quickly and accurately, verify inventory balances, and handle multiple requests efficiently. Check what needs attention ¤ Your Operational Dashboard shows work queues for inventory . For example, you can see parts needed today, low stock, stagnant inventory , open material requests, and cycle counts that are due. Use them to decide what to work on first. Find and complete an assigned work order , for example, complete work on Filler FL-02. Guided steps available: Prefer to learn in the application? Log in and open your Operational dashboard to follow guided steps for completing a work order . 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with a simple preventive maintenance task Ask your supervisor if you're unsure about anything Take photos to document your work Record information as you go, not at the end What to do ¤ Log into Maximo Application Suite Select. Open the Work Orders application, or open the Technician app and select Assigned work . The Technician app is also available in IBM Maximo Mobile. Learn Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? Choose a simple work order to start. Look for status "Assigned" or "In Progress". New to work orders ? Learn What is a work order ? to understand the basics. Click to open the work order details. Change status to "In Progress". Review what needs to be done. Check if you need any parts or tools. Perform the maintenance task. Add notes about what you did. Record time spent as labor hours. You need a labor record to track time. If you cannot start work, ask your administrator to check that you have one. Add any parts you used. Need to request parts? See How do I issue parts to a job? Update meter readings if applicable. Change status to "Completed". Verify all information is recorded. Submit for approval if required. What success looks like ¤ You've successfully completed your first work order when: Work order status changed from "Assigned" to "Completed" All required fields are completed such as notes, labor hours, or parts used Your supervisor can see what you did and why Equipment history now shows your work Parts inventory updated automatically Time and costs are recorded for planning You'll know you're ready to move on when you can complete a simple work order from start to finish without help, and your notes clearly explain what you found and fixed. For more detail on recording notes, parts, and time accurately, see How do I complete a work order ? What can I do in the Technician app? ¤ The Technician app is built around the work that you do every day. It is the same app on the desktop and in IBM Maximo Mobile. In the Technician app, you can: View the work orders that are assigned to you, and filter them by priority, status , or due date. View work orders on a map to plan routes and reduce travel time. See work details such as job plans , instructions, and safety requirements. Record labor hours, tool use, and material use. Update the work order status as you work. Attach photos, notes, and documents to work orders . Report failures and update failure class information. Request materials, tools, or services. View details of the related asset and location . Add to the work log and review earlier entries. Create a work order with the add button, for example when you find a problem on site . You can link the work order to an asset . Create follow-up work orders . Record meter readings, such as energy use, run time, or fuel level. Get IBM Maximo Mobile ¤ Take your work with you. IBM Maximo Mobile lets you view assigned work, complete work orders , and update records from your phone or tablet. How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? docs.text: How can AI improve maintenance? ¤ Artificial intelligence features in maintenance management accelerate work order processing, assist with failure classification, and generate executive summaries of historical equipment performance. By extracting patterns from historical maintenance records, AI reduces manual administrative tasks and helps teams identify recurring failure modes. In Maximo Application Suite Select, AI capabilities focus on data enrichment, intelligent classification, and automated work summaries configured through the AI Configuration application. Looking to verify your AI readiness right away? Skip to AI configuration checklist ↓ AI maintenance capabilities ¤ Integrating AI models with maintenance workflows provides several key operational improvements: Automated work order summarization: Summarize extensive technician logs, status changes, and repair remarks into concise executive digests for shift handovers. Failure mode recommendations: Suggest relevant Problem, Cause, and Remedy failure codes based on free-form technician text entered on work orders . Asset classification assistance: Analyze asset specification attributes and recommend standardized classification hierarchies. docs.text: What can I automate? ¤ Automating routine maintenance workflows eliminates repetitive manual scheduling, ensures preventive maintenance triggers on time, and delivers instant notifications when critical equipment anomalies occur. Instead of relying on planners to generate work orders or send status updates manually, automated background tasks handle routine administration. In Maximo Application Suite Select, automation is driven by scheduled background tasks in Cron Task lite, condition monitoring triggers, communication templates , and mobile push notifications. Looking to verify your automation readiness right away? Skip to automation readiness checklist ↓ Key automation capabilities in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Automation in Maximo Application Suite Select addresses four major operational maintenance areas: Preventive maintenance generation: Automatically creates scheduled work orders ahead of due dates based on elapsed calendar time or accumulated run hours. Condition-based work triggers: Generates corrective work orders when the gauge readings that you enter exceed defined action thresholds. Automated inventory reordering: Flags storeroom parts that drop below their minimum reorder point and creates restock requests. Instant stakeholder alerts: Dispatches email and push notifications when work orders are approved, delayed, or completed. Table 1: Automation mechanisms and operational applications ¤ Automation type Primary application How it works Operational example Scheduled PM generation Cron Task lite, PM Background process scans active PM schedules and generates work orders within a defined look-ahead window Generating weekly lubrication work orders 3 days before their due date for Filler FL-02 Condition-based triggers Condition Monitoring, Cron Task lite Monitors gauge readings and automatically issues corrective work orders upon action limit breaches Generating an urgent inspection work order when drive motor bearing temperature exceeds 80 degrees Celsius Inventory reorder calculation Inventory , Cron Task lite Calculates current balances against minimum thresholds and economic order quantities Creating restock requisitions when food-grade lubricant stock drops below 5 drums Mobile push alerts Push Notifications Administration Dispatches immediate notifications directly to technician mobile devices Alerting on-call technicians to emergency breakdowns in the Cold Storage Room Figure 1: Automated background processing architecture in Cron Task lite As shown in Figure 1, the Cron Task lite background engine automates maintenance scheduling and inventory replenishment across three core tasks and two operational dispatch channels: Background Engine (Cron Task lite) : Executes automated background processing on configured schedules without manual user intervention. Automated tasks : PMWOGENCRONTASK : Evaluates active preventive maintenance intervals and automatically generates scheduled PM work orders within configured lead times. MEASUREPOINTWOGENCRONTASK : Evaluates condition monitoring meter logs and triggers corrective work orders when action limits are breached. REORDERCRONTASK : Scans current storeroom balances and automatically creates restock requisitions for low-stock items . Dispatch outcomes : Work dispatch : Routes generated PM and condition-based work orders directly to technician mobile push alerts and supervisor Work Queue cards. Inventory dispatch : Routes generated material requisitions directly to the storeroom restock queue. Scheduled background tasks in Cron Task lite ¤ Cron tasks run on configured background schedules without requiring user intervention. System administrators manage execution intervals and parameters in the desktop application. Table 2: Essential background tasks in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Task name Frequency Function PMWoGenCronTask Nightly Evaluates preventive maintenance frequencies and generates open work orders MeasurePointWoGenCronTask Every 15 minutes Evaluates condition monitoring meter points against defined action limits ReorderCronTask Daily Analyzes storeroom balances and initiates replenishment for low-stock items Configuring PM work order generation in Cron Task lite ¤ To ensure work orders generate automatically before their maintenance due date, configure the automated generation schedule: In the Find navigation item field, search for Cron Task Setup and open it. In the Cron Task field, search for PMWOGENCRONTASK . In the Cron Task Instances table, select the active instance for your site . In the Schedule field, verify the execution frequency, such as running daily at 01:00 AM. In the Parameters table, set the LEADTIME value to 3 to generate work orders three days ahead of target start dates. Check the Active box to ensure the background task is running. In the Select Action menu, click Save Properties , then click Reload Request . 💡 Tip: Use lead time to prevent last-minute scheduling chaos ¤ Always configure a lead time on your PM generation cron task. Generating work orders 3 to 7 days before their scheduled date gives maintenance supervisors time to pre-assign technicians, confirm parts availability in the storeroom, and coordinate equipment downtime with production managers. Mobile push notifications for urgent work ¤ When equipment breaks down unexpectedly, supervisors must alert field technicians immediately. The Push Notifications Administration application routes urgent work alerts directly to technician tablets and mobile devices. Enabling mobile push alerts for emergency work ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Push Notifications Administration and open it. Select the notification event configuration for Emergency Work Orders . Verify that the trigger condition is mapped to work orders with Priority 1 or Emergency work types. Set the recipient rule to target the assigned technician and maintenance lead for the active shift. Set status to Active and click Save . docs.text: How do I turn data into decisions? ¤ Collecting thousands of work orders , meter logs, and parts transactions provides no operational value unless maintenance leaders can synthesize that information into strategic decisions. Without structured reporting, management reacts to emergencies rather than proactively addressing chronic failures. Turning maintenance data into actionable decisions in Maximo Application Suite Select involves monitoring performance indicators in KPI Manager and KPI Viewer, analyzing equipment failure trends, and leveraging role-based operational dashboards. Looking to verify your decision analytics right away? Skip to decision-making analytics checklist ↓ Framework for data-driven maintenance decisions ¤ To transition from reactive firefighting to strategic asset management, connect operational metrics directly to business outcomes. Table 1: Strategic maintenance decisions and supporting metrics ¤ Decision category Core question to answer Key metrics Analytics tool Repair versus replace Has the cumulative repair cost of an asset exceeded its economic replacement value? Total Maintenance Cost, Year-to-Date Cost vs Replacement Value Assets , KPI Viewer PM optimization Are preventive maintenance routines preventing breakdowns or causing intrusive infant mortality? PM Compliance Rate, Emergency Work Ratio, MTBF KPI Manager, PM Staffing & craft planning Do we have sufficient mechanical and electrical staffing to handle the scheduled backlog? Labor Utilization, Overdue Backlog Hours by Craft Work Queue Manager, Supervisor Operational Dashboard Inventory stocking Are we holding excess capital in slow-moving stock while stocking out of critical spares? Inventory Turnover Ratio, Stockout Incidence Rate Inventory , Inventory Clerk Operational Dashboard Figure 1: Maintenance data aggregation and decision pipeline As shown in Figure 1, operational maintenance data moves through a four-stage decision pipeline from raw logging to strategic actions: Data ingestion : Field technicians and clerks log raw work logs, labor hours, and parts actuals. Aggregation engines : Data feeds in parallel into two core analytical modules: KPI Manager : Calculates compliance rates and measures performance against targets. Failure Codes : Tracks chronic root causes and failure trends. Dashboards : Operational dashboards aggregate these analytical streams into unified review screens. Strategic actions : Specific performance thresholds trigger targeted operational decisions: PM Compliance below 85 percent : Reallocate craft labor to clear maintenance backlogs. Chronic failures : Refine job plan instructions and maintenance tasks. Repair cost exceeding 60 percent of asset value : Initiate capital replacement planning. Monitoring metrics with KPI Manager and KPI Viewer ¤ KPI Manager allows reliability managers to configure mathematical metrics, set performance targets, and define Green, Yellow, and Red alert thresholds. Key performance indicator benchmarks ¤ Targeting established industry benchmarks ensures your maintenance strategy drives plant profitability. Table 2: Recommended operational KPI target thresholds ¤ Key performance indicator Benchmark target Warning threshold Critical action threshold PM Compliance Rate with 10 percent grace rule Greater than 90 percent 80 to 89 percent Below 80 percent Emergency Work Ratio Below 10 percent of total labor hours 11 to 20 percent Above 20 percent Mean Time Between Failures, MTBF Increasing month-over-month Flat Declining trend Schedule Compliance Greater than 85 percent 70 to 84 percent Below 70 percent Creating a KPI in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for KPI Manager and open it. Click New KPI . In the KPI field, enter a unique code, such as KPI_PM_COMPLIANCE . In the Description field, enter Preventive Maintenance Compliance Rate . In the Calculation field, enter the SQL select statement calculating completed PMs within allowable grace windows against total scheduled PMs. In the Target field, enter 90.00 . In the Caution at field, enter 85.00 to establish the yellow warning boundary. In the Alert at field, enter 80.00 to establish the red critical boundary. Click Save , then click Run KPI to calculate the initial value. 💡 Tip: Review KPI trends weekly rather than single-day spikes ¤ A single day drop in PM compliance often reflects a scheduled plant-wide cleaning or minor power outage. Look for four-week rolling trends in KPI Viewer before making permanent adjustments to craft staffing or job plans . Real-world decision: Filler FL-02 repair versus replace analysis ¤ At the Ice Cream Main Plant, Filler FL-02 experienced four mechanical seal failures over six months. By analyzing the asset history: Total Maintenance Cost: The Assets application showed $42,000 in combined parts and overtime labor over the trailing twelve months. Replacement Cost: A new modular filling station costs $65,000. Failure Trend: Failure Codes indicated all four breakdowns originated from drive shaft misalignment causing seal wear. Decision: Rather than approving a fifth seal replacement or spending $65,000 on a complete machine replacement, engineering scheduled a targeted drive shaft realignment and bearing housing overhaul for $6,500, permanently resolving the root cause. Decision-making analytics checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure your reporting framework supports sound management decisions. docs.text: How do I optimize performance? ¤ Continuous maintenance optimization transforms a routine preventive maintenance program into a high-efficiency reliability strategy. Over time, maintenance programs accumulate outdated tasks, excessive inspection frequencies, and inaccurate time estimates that consume valuable craft labor without preventing breakdowns. Optimizing maintenance performance in Maximo Application Suite Select involves conducting PM optimization reviews, fine-tuning condition monitoring limits, refining job plan labor estimates, and eliminating chronic failure modes. Looking to verify your optimization program right away? Skip to performance optimization checklist ↓ The continuous optimization cycle ¤ Effective maintenance programs follow a closed-loop refinement cycle: Figure 1: Continuous maintenance performance optimization cycle As shown in Figure 1, continuous maintenance optimization operates as a closed-loop cycle across four progressive steps and an ongoing refinement loop: Step 1: Execute work : Technicians perform preventive, corrective, and inspection tasks in the field. Step 2: Log actuals : Technicians record accurate actual labor hours, materials used, and failure codes . Step 3: Analyze KPIs : Reliability engineers and supervisors evaluate key performance metrics, such as PM compliance and equipment availability. Step 4: Identify changes : The maintenance team pinpoints operational bottlenecks and formulates targeted process revisions. Refinement actions : Adjustments such as extending PM intervals, refining job plan torque specifications, and pre-staging replacement parts feed directly back into Step 1 for ongoing execution. Table 1: Maintenance optimization stages and techniques ¤ Optimization stage Operational focus Data analyzed Desired outcome PM frequency tuning Adjusting service intervals based on actual operating run hours Continuous meter history, PM generation counts, historical failure dates Eliminating unnecessary PMs on idle equipment Condition threshold calibration Setting realistic warning and action limits Gauge meter readings, historical reading logs Preventing alarm fatigue while ensuring early anomaly detection Job plan refinement Comparing estimated labor and parts against actual logged values Work order actuals, wrench time delays, parts issue logs Reducing job duration and eliminating missing parts delays Failure elimination Identifying chronic root causes across equipment families Failure Codes Problem, Cause, and Remedy trends Modifying operating parameters to design out recurring failures Identifying candidates for PM optimization ¤ Not all preventive maintenance tasks deliver equal value. Reviewing maintenance records often reveals tasks that can be streamlined or eliminated entirely. Table 2: Indicators that a PM routine requires optimization ¤ Observed symptom Operational diagnosis Optimization action Zero failures found over 20 consecutive PM cycles The inspection frequency is too tight or the asset operates in low-stress conditions Extend the PM frequency interval or switch to a usage-based meter trigger Failures occur immediately after scheduled PM service Intrusive teardown inspections are introducing human assembly errors Replace intrusive mechanical inspections with non-destructive condition monitoring Actual hours consistently exceed estimated hours by 50 percent Job plan instructions are missing setup steps or required tooling Revise the Job Plan to reflect realistic task durations and stage specialized tools PM work orders closed without completing tasks Technicians face time constraints or perceive the task as non-value-added Simplify the checklist in Inspection Forms to focus only on critical failure modes Refining PM intervals in the desktop application ¤ When an asset runs intermittently, calendar-based maintenance schedules generate premature work orders . Converting calendar PMs to meter -based schedules ensures servicing occurs only after true operating wear. Updating a PM schedule to usage-based triggers ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for PM and open it. Open the preventive maintenance record for the target asset , such as PM_FILLER02_SVC . In the Frequency tab, navigate to the Meter Based Frequency sub-tab. Click New Row to link a continuous meter : In the Meter field, select the run-hour meter , such as RUNHOURS . docs.text: Continuous maintenance optimization transforms a routine preventive maintenance program into a high-efficiency reliability strategy. Over time, maintenance programs accumulate outdated tasks, excessive inspection frequencies, and inaccurate time estimates that consume valuable craft labor without preventing breakdowns. Optimizing maintenance performance in Maximo Application Suite Select involves conducting PM optimization reviews, fine-tuning condition monitoring limits, refining job plan labor estimates, and eliminating chronic failure modes. Looking to verify your optimization program right away? Skip to performance optimization checklist ↓
docs.title: How do I optimize performance?

docs.text: Effective maintenance programs follow a closed-loop refinement cycle: Figure 1: Continuous maintenance performance optimization cycle As shown in Figure 1, continuous maintenance optimization operates as a closed-loop cycle across four progressive steps and an ongoing refinement loop: Step 1: Execute work : Technicians perform preventive, corrective, and inspection tasks in the field. Step 2: Log actuals : Technicians record accurate actual labor hours, materials used, and failure codes . Step 3: Analyze KPIs : Reliability engineers and supervisors evaluate key performance metrics, such as PM compliance and equipment availability. Step 4: Identify changes : The maintenance team pinpoints operational bottlenecks and formulates targeted process revisions. Refinement actions : Adjustments such as extending PM intervals, refining job plan torque specifications, and pre-staging replacement parts feed directly back into Step 1 for ongoing execution.

docs.text: How do I manage more assets ? ¤ As manufacturing plants expand and new production lines are commissioned, maintenance teams must manage hundreds of additional pieces of equipment. Trying to manage growing asset registries using individual, disconnected preventive maintenance records creates administrative overload and leads to missed service intervals. Scaling maintenance operations efficiently in Maximo Application Suite Select relies on Master PM templates, multi- asset Routes, parent and child equipment hierarchies, and bulk data onboarding via Data Management. Looking to verify your scaling readiness right away? Skip to scaling verification checklist ↓ Core tools for scaling asset management ¤ To scale equipment coverage without increasing administrative headcount, use four core features: Master PM templates: Maintain a single master maintenance schedule that automatically updates individual PM records across hundreds of identical machines. Multi-stop routes: Combine repetitive inspections across multiple assets or locations into a single consolidated work order . Asset hierarchies: Organize equipment into parent and child relationships to track sub-assemblies. Data Management tool: Bulk load newly commissioned assets , locations , and initial meter configurations using validated spreadsheet templates. Table 1: Scaling mechanisms and operational applications ¤ Scaling mechanism Application Operational function Plant scaling example Master PM Master PM Centralizes maintenance intervals, job plans , and seasonal triggers across equipment models Managing identical 500-hour service schedules for 30 homogenizer pumps Routes Routes Bundles multiple physical assets or locations into a single sequential work order Inspecting 45 cold storage temperature valves on a single daily shift route Parent-child trees Assets Establishes sub-assembly structures for components that move between machines Tracking drive motors and gearboxes installed on Filler FL-02 Bulk onboarding Data Management Ingests large asset registries with classifications and specifications in batches Commissioning 200 new assets for the Ice Cream Plant expansion Figure 1: Operational scaling through Master PMs and multi-stop routes As shown in Figure 1, operational scaling relies on two complementary consolidation mechanisms: Master PM cascading : A single master template, such as the 50 HP Motor Template, links to and automatically updates individual maintenance schedules across the plant, including PM 1001 for Filler FL-01 Drive Motor, PM 1002 for Filler FL-02 Drive Motor, and PM 1003 for Filler FL-03 Drive Motor. Route consolidation : A single route definition, such as the Cold Storage Daily Route, bundles multiple physical inspections into one unified work order with sequential stops, covering Stop 1: Production Room Compressor Valve, Stop 2: Cold Storage Evaporator Valve, and Stop 3: Filling Line Room Bypass Valve. Standardizing schedules with Master PMs ¤ When your facility operates dozens of identical assets , such as motors, pumps, or conveyors, creating separate PM schedules for each machine causes maintenance drift. If the manufacturer updates the recommended lubrication interval, updating each PM manually is time-consuming and error-prone. A Master PM establishes the master frequency and attached Job Plan. When you modify the Master PM, Maximo Application Suite Select cascades the update to all linked individual asset PM records. Creating a Master PM in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Master PM and open it. Click New Master PM . In the Master PM field, enter a unique identifier, such as MPM_50HP_MOTOR . In the Description field, enter Standard 50 HP Motor Quarterly Service . In the Frequency tab, set the maintenance interval, such as every 90 days or every 1,500 run hours. In the Job Plan field, select the standardized maintenance procedure. In the Select Action menu, click Create Associated PMs to link existing equipment records that match this equipment model. Click Save . Consolidating repetitive tasks with Routes ¤ Creating individual work orders for every light fixture, fire extinguisher, or conveyor bearing generates overwhelming work order volume that clutters technician task lists. The Routes application groups multiple assets or locations into a single route. When Maximo Application Suite Select generates work from a routed PM, it creates one parent work order with child tasks or multiple entries on the Multi Asset and Location table. Table 2: Comparing individual PMs versus routed maintenance ¤ Metric Individual PM approach Routed maintenance approach Work order volume 50 separate work orders generated weekly 1 consolidated work order with 50 asset stops Technician time logging Technician opens and closes 50 individual records Technician logs time once on the parent route work order Scheduling overhead Supervisor assigns 50 distinct work orders Supervisor assigns 1 route work order to the shift team Audit trail Fragmented across dozens of disconnected records Consolidated in one chronological route history Creating an asset route in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Routes and open it. Click New Route . In the Route field, enter an identifier, such as RT_COLD_INSPECT . In the Description field, enter Cold Storage Daily Temperature and Valve Inspection . In the Route Stops table, click New Row to add equipment locations in sequential walking order: In the Location field, enter COLD_ROOM_A . In the Asset field, enter the specific refrigeration valve or sensor. Repeat step 5 for all remaining stops along the inspection path. Click Save . 💡 Tip: Order route stops by physical layout ¤ When building routes, list stops in the exact physical sequence a technician walks through the facility. Sequencing stops by floor and room eliminates backtrack travel time and ensures inspectors do not overlook remote equipment. docs.text: How do I standardize across teams? ¤ When different maintenance shifts or plant areas follow disparate procedures, equipment reliability varies widely. One shift might lubricate pump bearings using detailed manufacturer steps while another applies grease without cleaning grease fittings or checking seals. Standardizing maintenance across teams ensures uniform safety compliance, predictable job durations, consistent failure analysis, and accurate labor cost tracking. In Maximo Application Suite Select, standardization is achieved through shared Job Plans, uniform Craft definitions, standardized Failure Codes, and structured Inspection Forms. Looking to verify standardization readiness right away? Skip to cross-team standardization checklist ↓ Core standardization pillars in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ To establish consistent operational practices across all shifts and plant zones, standardize four primary elements: Standard Job Plans: Provide unambiguous, numbered task instructions, safety lockout requirements, estimated labor hours, and required spare parts. Uniform Craft and Labor structures: Define enterprise-wide craft codes, skill levels, and hourly billing rates. Structured Failure Hierarchies: Enforce a common three-tier Problem, Cause, and Remedy taxonomy across all equipment classes. Digital Inspection Forms: Replace informal walk-through checklists with version-controlled inspection templates. Table 1: Cross-team standardization pillars in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Standardization pillar Application Operational purpose Cross-team benefit Standard procedures Job Plans Specifies exact mechanical steps and required tools Eliminates variation between day, night, and weekend shift execution Craft definitions Crafts Standardizes skill levels, certifications, and loaded hourly rates Ensures accurate labor cost estimation across departments Failure classification Failure Codes Defines uniform Problem, Cause, and Remedy failure paths Enables plant-wide reliability engineering and root cause comparison Digital inspections Inspection Forms Standardizes quality, sanitation, and safety audit sheets Guarantees compliance records match regulatory audit requirements Figure 1: Cross-shift standardization structure and unified reporting As shown in Figure 1, the cross-shift standardization architecture connects central standards to operational execution and executive reporting: Enterprise Standards : Central definitions establish baseline consistency: Standard Crafts : Enforce uniform labor billing rates and skill progressions. Standard Job Plans : Mandate identical procedural steps, safety controls, and required parts. Standard Failure Codes : Define uniform Problem, Cause, and Remedy failure options. Shift Execution : Both Day Maintenance and Night Maintenance follow the identical procedures and log data using the same failure codes . Unified Reporting : Operational execution feeds clean, structured data into KPI Viewer, enabling true benchmark comparisons across shifts and departments. Creating standardized Job Plans ¤ A well-constructed Job Plan removes guesswork for technicians. When a work order generates for Filler FL-02, the attached job plan details exact torque specifications, required seal replacement kits, and food safety sanitation steps. Creating a Job Plan in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Job Plans and open it. Click New Job Plan . In the Job Plan field, enter an identifier, such as JP_FILLER_SEAL_SVC . In the Description field, enter Filler FL-02 Mechanical Seal Service and Inspection . In the Tasks table, click New Row to add numbered operational steps: Task 10: Isolate power and apply lockout and tagout locks to main disconnect. Task 20: Drain product lines and flush pump housing with clean water. Task 30: Remove mechanical seal housing and inspect drive shaft for pitting. Task 40: Install new food-grade mechanical seal kit and torque bolts to 25 Nm. Task 50: Remove lockout tags, restore power, and conduct 15-minute leak check. In the Labor tab, add required craft hours, such as 2 hours of Mechanical Technician, MECH . In the Materials tab, specify required storeroom items , such as the replacement seal kit and food-grade lubricant. In the Select Action menu, change status to Active , then click Save . 💡 Tip: Version job plans rather than overwriting active procedures ¤ When updating standard operating procedures, use the Revision feature in Job Plans. Revising a job plan preserves historical records on completed work orders while ensuring new work orders automatically adopt the latest approved safety standards. Configuring uniform Crafts and Labor rates ¤ Standardizing craft codes ensures that work plans accurately predict job costs regardless of which specific technician is assigned. Table 2: Example craft hierarchy for manufacturing facilities ¤ Craft code Description Skill levels Standard hourly rate MECH Mechanical Technician Apprentice, Journeyman, Master $45.00 to $65.00 ELEC Electrical Technician Journeyman, Master $55.00 to $75.00 HVAC Refrigeration Specialist Journeyman, Master $60.00 to $80.00 LUBE Lubrication Technician Standard $35.00 to $45.00 Creating a Craft in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Crafts and open it. Click New Craft . In the Craft field, enter the code, such as MECH . In the Description field, enter Mechanical Maintenance Technician . In the Standard Rate field, enter the default loaded hourly labor cost. In the Skill Levels table, click New Row to define progression levels, such as JOURNEY and MASTER . Change status to Active and click Save . Cross-team standardization checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure all maintenance teams operate under unified standards. Quels sont les concepts de base ? ¤ Découvrez les éléments de base que vous utiliserez chaque jour : Qu'est-ce qu'un emplacement ? - Lieux physiques où le travail est effectué Qu'est-ce qu'un actif ? - Équipements, machines et infrastructures que vous entretenez Qu'est-ce qu'un ordre de travail ? - Instructions pour effectuer un travail de maintenance Comment les emplacements , les actifs et les ordres de travail fonctionnent-ils ensemble ? - Découvrez comment ces concepts s'articulent dans des scénarios réels Qu'est-ce que Maximo Application Suite Select ? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select est une solution SaaS (Software as a Service) prête à l'emploi. Aucune installation. Aucune configuration. Aucune personnalisation nécessaire. Il vous suffit de vous connecter et de commencer à travailler : Suivre les actifs Créer et terminer des ordres de travail Planifier la maintenance préventive Gérer l'inventaire des pièces Surveiller les performances À qui s'adresse-t-il ? ¤ Les techniciens peuvent rechercher et terminer des ordres de travail, par exemple terminer le travail sur Filler FL-02. Les superviseurs peuvent planifier, affecter et suivre le travail de maintenance, par exemple affecter la maintenance préventive de Spiral freezer SF-01. Les magasiniers peuvent gérer les pièces et les fournitures, par exemple sortir des pièces de Main storeroom. docs.text: Ajouter un utilisateur ¤ Ouvrez l'application Users. Cliquez sur Create user . Indiquez une adresse e-mail de connexion . Indiquez un ID utilisateur . Si vous le souhaitez, ajoutez une note dans le champ mémo . Exemple : accès temporaire pour un sous-traitant de l'usine de crèmes glacées A Indiquez un nom d'affichage . Il s'agit du nom complet de l'utilisateur ou d'un nom d'usage facilement reconnaissable. Cliquez sur Select groups et ajoutez l'utilisateur à au moins un groupe de sécurité. Un e-mail est envoyé à l'adresse e-mail de connexion. Tableau 1. Groupes de sécurité ¤ Un groupe de sécurité est un ensemble d'utilisateurs qui disposent des mêmes accès. Les droits d'un groupe de sécurité déterminent les applications, les actions et les données auxquelles ses membres peuvent accéder. Un rôle détermine ce qu'une personne peut voir et faire dans Maximo Application Suite Select. Affectez chaque utilisateur au groupe de sécurité qui correspond à son rôle : Groupe de sécurité Ce qu'ils peuvent faire System admin Gère la configuration du système et les accès des utilisateurs. Les administrateurs système peuvent configurer les domaines, les modèles de communication et les paramètres d'IA, créer des utilisateurs et définir des groupes de sécurité, mais ils n'effectuent généralement pas de travail opérationnel au quotidien. Exemples de tâches : configurer des modèles de notification, gérer les rôles des utilisateurs, définir des groupes de sécurité, configurer les paramètres système et gérer les structures de données. Supervisor Supervise les opérations et les activités de l'équipe. Les superviseurs peuvent planifier et approuver le travail, examiner le travail des techniciens, surveiller les actifs et les performances, et accéder aux analyses pour suivre l'avancement. Exemples de tâches : affecter et approuver des ordres de travail, examiner les indicateurs clés de performance, examiner les résultats d'inspection, gérer les plans de travail, et surveiller l'état des actifs et les calendriers de maintenance. Technician Effectue le travail de maintenance et le travail opérationnel. Les techniciens peuvent consulter et mettre à jour le travail qui leur est affecté, effectuer des inspections, enregistrer les heures de main-d'œuvre, déclarer les matériaux utilisés et enregistrer des données sur les actifs, comme les relevés de compteur et les détails sur l'état. Exemples de tâches : terminer des ordres de travail, saisir les résultats d'inspection, mettre à jour l'état des actifs, enregistrer les heures de main-d'œuvre, déclarer les matériaux utilisés et saisir les relevés de compteur. Requester Soumet et suit des demandes de service. Les demandeurs disposent d'un accès limité et ne peuvent pas effectuer de tâches opérationnelles ou administratives. Ce rôle consiste à lancer et à suivre des demandes de travail. Exemples de tâches : créer une demande de service pour un actif en panne et suivre son statut jusqu'à sa résolution. Inventory clerk Gère l'inventaire et les opérations du magasin. Les magasiniers peuvent tenir à jour les stocks, traiter les mouvements d'articles, ajuster les soldes d'inventaire et garantir l'exactitude des enregistrements d'inventaire. Exemples de tâches : réceptionner des articles en stock, sortir des matériaux pour des ordres de travail, effectuer des comptages d'inventaire, ajuster les soldes d'inventaire et gérer les magasins. Note Vous devez affecter au moins un groupe de sécurité. L'utilisateur ne peut pas accéder aux applications tant qu'aucun groupe de sécurité n'est affecté.

docs.text: Getting work done ¤ Find quick answers to common questions about planning, completing, and managing work. Planning work ¤ How do I plan recurring maintenance? ¤ Set up preventive maintenance (PM) schedules that automatically generate work orders based on time intervals or meter readings. This ensures routine maintenance happens consistently without manual tracking. I want to know more about planning recurring maintenance Why isn't my PM generating work orders ? ¤ Check that the PM is active, that the asset or location is operating, and that a floating schedule is not waiting on an open work order . A PM might also not be due yet, or you might be generating from a child PM instead of the top level PM. I want to know more about why a PM does not generate work orders How do I decide what work should be done? ¤ Prioritize work based on asset criticality, safety requirements, and operational impact. Use work order status and priority codes to manage what gets done first. I want to know more about deciding what work to do How do I schedule work? ¤ Assign work orders to specific dates and technicians based on availability, skills, and workload. Scheduling helps balance resources and ensures work happens when needed. I want to know more about scheduling work What is the difference between items , service items , and tools? ¤ Items represent physical materials or spare parts that are stored and consumed. Service items represent work or services that are delivered but not held in inventory . Tools represent reusable resources used to perform work rather than being consumed. These categories allow Maximo Application Suite Select to track usage, availability, and cost in different ways. How should inventory concepts such as ABC types and balances be understood? ¤ Inventory represents the system's record of physical stock and its associated value. Balances reflect what the system believes is on hand. ABC types are used to prioritize items based on importance, usage, or value, recognizing that not all inventory needs the same level of control. What is a count book? ¤ A count book defines a structured approach to validating inventory accuracy. It identifies which items should be physically counted and reconciled with system balances. Conceptually, it supports ongoing alignment between system data and real-world stock. I want to know more about tracking stock levels What is the difference between rotating and non- rotating items ? ¤ Rotating items are interchangeable assets that are tracked individually over their lifecycle. Non- rotating items are tracked only by quantity and are consumed when used. This distinction reflects whether individual history and movement are important to manage. I want to know more about storeroom and inventory strategy Completing work ¤ How do I find my work? ¤ View assigned work orders in your work list or on the Operational dashboard . Filter by status , priority, or due date to focus on what needs attention now. I want to know more about finding my work How do I complete a job? ¤ Open the work order , perform the tasks, record time and materials used, add notes about what you did, then change the status to complete. I want to know more about completing a job What if I can't complete a task? ¤ Document why the work can't be completed, update the work order status , and notify your supervisor. This keeps everyone informed and helps resolve blockers quickly. I want to know more about handling incomplete tasks How do PMs, Master PMs, and routes relate to maintenance strategy? ¤ Preventive maintenance (PMs) defines recurring maintenance activities. Master PMs provide a way to standardize and manage multiple related PMs. Routes organize how work is carried out across multiple assets , improving efficiency and consistency. I want to know more about planning recurring maintenance What are job plans ? ¤ Job plans define the standard approach to completing a task. They capture steps, resources, and expectations. Conceptually, job plans convert individual knowledge into shared organizational knowledge. Managing assets ¤ How do I track asset history? ¤ View all work orders , meter readings, and maintenance activities performed on an asset . This history helps you understand patterns, predict issues, and make informed maintenance decisions. I want to know more about tracking asset history How do I classify assets ? ¤ Assign classification codes that define what type of asset it is and what attributes apply. Classifications ensure consistent data capture and support better reporting and analysis. I want to know more about classifying assets What happens when an asset fails? ¤ Create a corrective work order , document the failure with failure codes , perform repairs, and update the asset record. This captures valuable data for reliability analysis. I want to know more about handling asset failures What are classifications? ¤ Classifications are used to structure and standardize how assets , items , and related records are described. They define which attributes apply to different types of records and ensure consistent data capture across the system. Conceptually, classifications establish a shared data model and vocabulary that supports reporting, maintenance strategies, and scalability. How do I classify assets ? What are systems in the context of locations ? ¤ Systems provide a functional grouping of locations based on how assets work together. While locations describe physical placement, systems describe operational or functional relationships. This allows organizations to manage assets from both a physical and functional perspective. What are meters , meter groups, and condition monitoring? ¤ Meters capture usage or condition data from assets . Meter groups organize related measurements. Condition monitoring evaluates those measurements to identify potential issues and support maintenance decisions based on actual asset behavior. I want to know more about detecting issues early What role do inspections play? ¤ Inspections standardize how asset condition is assessed. They convert observations into structured, consistent data. This supports early issue detection and more reliable maintenance decisions. I want to know more about inspections What are failure codes ? ¤ Failure codes provide a structured way to describe what went wrong, why it happened, and how it was resolved. They transform maintenance history into analyzable data. This supports reliability analysis and continuous improvement. I want to know more about failure codes and asset failures Managing inventory ¤ How do I issue parts to a job? ¤ Select the work order , add the items needed, specify quantities, and issue them from inventory . This tracks what materials were used and updates stock levels automatically. I want to know more about issuing parts How do I track stock levels? ¤ View current balances, reorder points, and usage history for each item . Set up alerts to notify you when stock runs low so you can reorder before running out. I want to know more about tracking stock levels What happens if stock is incorrect? ¤ Perform a physical count, compare it to system balances, and adjust the records to match reality. Document why the discrepancy occurred to prevent future issues. I want to know more about correcting stock How do labor , crafts , crews , and calendars work together? ¤ Labor represents individual workers. Crafts represent skills. Crews group labor for coordinated work, and calendars define availability. Together, these concepts model how work is resourced and scheduled. I want to know more about assigning the correct people Monitoring and responding ¤ How do I detect issues early? ¤ Monitor meter readings, set up condition-based alerts, and track asset performance trends. Early detection helps you address problems before they cause failures. I want to know more about detecting issues early What metrics matter? ¤ Track work order completion rates, mean time between failures, maintenance costs, and asset availability. These metrics show how well your maintenance program is performing. I want to know more about metrics How do I act on alerts? ¤ Review the alert details, assess the severity, create a work order if needed, and assign it to the appropriate technician. Quick response prevents small issues from becoming big problems. I want to know more about acting on alerts Organizing people and work ¤ How do I assign the correct people? ¤ Match work orders to technicians based on their craft skills, availability, and current workload. This ensures work gets done efficiently by qualified people. I want to know more about assigning the correct people How do I standardize data? ¤ Use consistent naming conventions, classification codes, and data entry practices across your organization. Standardization makes data reliable and supports better reporting. I want to know more about standardizing data Setting up and controlling ¤ How do I get data into the system? ¤ Import data using templates, integrate with other systems, or enter it manually. Clean, accurate data from the start saves time and prevents problems later. I want to know more about getting data into the system How do I automate communication? ¤ Set up email notifications for work order assignments, status changes, and alerts. Automation keeps everyone informed without manual effort. I want to know more about automating communication How do I add users? ¤ Before people can work in Maximo Application Suite Select, they need a user account with the correct security group assigned. I want to know more about adding users How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? ¤ Crafts define the skills in your organization. Labor records represent the people. Crews group people together so you can assign a whole team to a job in one step. I want to know more about setting up labor , crafts , and crews How do I decide whether something is a location , an asset , or a spare part? ¤ Every physical entity in your plant or facility must be classified as one of three primary record types: a location , an asset , or a spare part. Making the right classification before importing data ensures accurate maintenance history. I want to know more about deciding between a location , an asset , and a spare part How do I plan my location and asset hierarchies? ¤ A location hierarchy is the physical map of your facility. An asset hierarchy is the equipment breakdown structure that operates within those locations . Plan locations first, then assets . How do I plan my location hierarchy? How do I plan my asset hierarchy? What is the correct load order for my data? ¤ Import order matters. Referenced records must exist before records that use them, and parent records must exist before child records. I want to know more about load order How do I prepare data for import? ¤ Proper data preparation prevents import failures and ensures data quality. I want to know more about preparing data for import How do I fix import errors? ¤ Import errors can occur with locations or assets . A troubleshooting guide helps you fix common import problems. I want to know more about fixing import errors Which object structure do I use for each data type? ¤ An object structure defines what you are loading, much like a spreadsheet template defines the columns available for a type of data. You pick the one that matches the data you are loading. I want to know more about object structures How do I set up meters , failure codes , and inspection forms? ¤ Meter readings can drive preventive maintenance schedules and trigger corrective work orders . Failure codes convert technician remarks into standardized reliability data. Digital inspection forms replace paper clipboards with structured checklists on mobile devices. How do I set up meters and meter groups? How do I set up failure codes ? How do I create inspection forms? How do I plan my preventive maintenance and storeroom strategies? ¤ A preventive maintenance strategy prevents equipment breakdowns, stabilizes labor schedules, and ensures replacement parts are staged before work begins. A storeroom strategy ensures critical spare parts are on hand and prevents stockouts. How do I plan my preventive maintenance strategy? How do I plan my storeroom and inventory strategy? How do I set up maps? ¤ Map Manager lets you configure a map so that users can see the location of assets , work orders , and service addresses on a visual map inside the application. I want to know more about setting up maps How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? ¤ As an administrator, you configure the defaults that control how mobile devices sync data, which map app your team uses for navigation, and how service requests and work orders are created. I want to know more about configuring IBM Maximo Mobile Common troubleshooting ¤ Why can't I complete a work order ? Why is inventory showing negative stock? Why can't I issue materials to a work order ? Why don't technicians see their assigned work? Why can't I see new work in IBM Maximo Mobile? Why does my data look wrong? Why aren't technicians using the system? Still need help? ¤ In the product : Click the help icon (?) in the top right For a specific field : Click the field name or press Alt+F1 Submit feedback : Use the feedback option in the help menu

docs.text: Improving results ¤ Find quick answers to common questions about improving work quality, data quality, and system adoption. Improving work ¤ How do I reduce downtime ? ¤ Implement preventive maintenance , respond quickly to failures, keep critical spare parts in stock, and analyze failure patterns to address root causes. Proactive maintenance prevents unplanned outages. I want to know more about reducing downtime How do I improve completion rates? ¤ Ensure work orders have clear instructions, assign them to qualified technicians, provide necessary parts and tools, and remove obstacles that prevent completion. Track completion metrics to identify patterns. I want to know more about improving completion rates Improving data quality ¤ Why does my data look wrong? ¤ Data issues often stem from inconsistent entry practices, missing required fields, duplicate records, or integration problems. Identifying the root cause helps you fix it systematically. I want to know more about data issues How do I make data reliable? ¤ Establish data standards, train users on proper entry, validate data at entry, clean up existing issues, and monitor data quality regularly. Reliable data supports better decisions. I want to know more about making data reliable Improving adoption ¤ Why aren't technicians using the system? ¤ Common barriers include complex workflows, lack of training, poor mobile experience, or unclear value. Understanding why helps you address the real obstacles to adoption. docs.text: Security ¤ Find quick answers to common questions about security, access control, and data protection. Questions ¤ How do I control who can access the system? ¤ Administrators create user accounts and assign security groups in the Users application and suite administration. Each user receives login credentials or accesses the suite through enterprise single sign-on. I want to know more about adding users How do I manage user permissions? ¤ Permissions are controlled through role-based security groups , such as Administrator, Supervisor, Technician, and Inventory Clerk. Security groups determine which desktop applications, role-based apps, and actions each user can access. Following the principle of least privilege, users are granted only the access required for their specific role. I want to know more about user permissions and security groups How is my data protected? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select protects data through role-based access control, encrypted network transmission, and complete audit logging. Critical transactions, such as status changes, inventory balance adjustments, and work order actuals, record the user identifier and timestamp to maintain accountability. How do I set up single sign-on? ¤ Enterprise single sign-on is configured at the suite administration level with standard identity providers, such as SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect. Once single sign-on is enabled, users authenticate with their corporate credentials across both web browser sessions and IBM Maximo Mobile. What security features are available? ¤ Security capabilities include role-based permissions, site -level data segregation, audit tracking, electronic signatures, secure session timeouts, and encrypted local data storage on mobile devices. docs.text: Starting out ¤ Find quick answers to common questions about getting started with Maximo Application Suite Select. Questions ¤ What can I do in my role? ¤ Technicians complete work orders and record work, supervisors assign and track maintenance, inventory clerks manage parts and stock, and administrators configure data, access, and system settings. Each role focuses on key tasks to keep work moving. I want to know more about what I can do in my role What is an asset ? ¤ An asset is any piece of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure that your organization maintains. Assets are tracked in the system with details such as location , maintenance history, and current condition to help you manage their lifecycle. I want to know more about assets What is a work order ? ¤ A work order is a request or instruction to perform maintenance work. It tracks everything about a maintenance job including what needs to be done, who does it, what parts are used, and when it's completed. I want to know more about work orders What is a location ? ¤ A location is a functional area or operating space where assets are installed or work is performed. Locations help you organize assets by where they're physically placed and track maintenance by area. I want to know more about locations Why do some terms differ from what I'm used to? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select uses a consistent set of terms to describe assets , locations , work, and inventory . These might differ from the terms you use today or in other systems. I want to know more about terminology What are classifications? ¤ Classifications are used to structure and standardize how assets , items , and related records are described. They define which attributes apply to different types of records and ensure consistent data capture across the system. Conceptually, classifications establish a shared data model and vocabulary that supports reporting, maintenance strategies, and scalability. How do I classify assets ? What are systems in the context of locations ? ¤ Systems provide a functional grouping of locations based on how assets work together. While locations describe physical placement, systems describe operational or functional relationships. This allows organizations to manage assets from both a physical and functional perspective. Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? ¤ You can work with work orders in the Work Orders application, in the Technician app on the desktop, and in the Technician app in IBM Maximo Mobile. All three work with the same work orders . I want to know more about where to manage work orders How do inspections work? ¤ An inspection is a set of questions that you answer about an asset or a location . Inspections use two apps: Inspection Forms, to define the forms, and Inspections, to conduct inspections and record the results. I want to know more about inspections What happens when I'm offline in IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile keeps working when your device loses its connection. The app stores your data on the device, so you can keep working and sync your changes later. I want to know more about working offline How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile lets technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks view assigned work, complete work orders , and update records from a phone or tablet. I want to know more about getting IBM Maximo Mobile How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? ¤ A location tells you where work happens. An asset tells you what equipment is maintained. A work order records the maintenance done on that equipment. I want to know more about how these concepts connect What keyboard shortcuts can I use? ¤ Keyboard shortcuts let you save, move between records, change status , and navigate without switching between your keyboard and mouse.
