docs.text: How do I act on alerts? ¤ Operational dashboards in Maximo Application Suite Select consolidate critical operational signals into a single view. When a key performance indicator breaches an alert threshold, or when urgent maintenance enters a work queue, supervisors and administrators can review the situation and take immediate corrective action directly from the dashboard. Acting on alerts promptly prevents small anomalies, such as an overdue preventive maintenance inspection or a rising emergency backlog, from escalating into unplanned production downtime . Looking to verify your alert response workflow right away? Skip to alert and work queue checklist ↓ When you first sign in, Select shows the Operational Dashboard that matches your security group . Your administrator assigns the group. Select includes some dashboard content, and an administrator can edit the dashboard to add cards such as KPIs and work queues. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Check your Operational Dashboard at the start of each shift. Review red threshold breaches first, followed by yellow caution indicators. Use work queue cards to take direct action. You can assign labor , update work order status , or open the full record without navigating through the main menu. Ensure newly created work queues are activated. In Work Queue Manager, new queues default to inactive until an administrator explicitly sets their status to active. Customize work queue queries so they capture only actionable records. Queues containing thousands of general records dilute focus and cause alert fatigue. Where alerts appear on your dashboard ¤ Your Operational Dashboard organizes alerts and work items into distinct visual cards. Table 1: Alert indicators on the Operational Dashboard ¤ Card type What it displays Alert condition Immediate action KPI trend cards Single performance indicator with historical trend line Card turns red when value breaches the alert threshold; turns yellow at caution level Use the card menu to open the KPI in KPI Viewer and analyze the underlying historical records Work queues card Table of urgent work categories, such as overdue work or emergency requests Badge count increases when new records match the queue query Select a queue to inspect records, assign technicians, or update status directly Condition monitoring alerts Assets exceeding measurement action limits Corrective work orders appear in unassigned or emergency work queues Review the asset condition history and dispatch qualified personnel Responding to KPI threshold breaches ¤ When a KPI card changes to yellow or red, investigate the underlying cause before adjusting operational priorities. Table 2: Common KPI alert triggers and corrective responses ¤ KPI alert What the breach indicates Immediate corrective response PM compliance below 85% Routine inspections and servicing are falling behind schedule Open the Overdue PMs work queue and reschedule delayed maintenance to available shifts Emergency work order spike Unplanned equipment breakdowns are consuming maintenance capacity Review recent failure codes in the Work Orders application to identify repeat defect patterns Overdue work order accumulation Team capacity is mismatched with incoming work demand Reassign low priority backlog work and focus available crafts on critical production assets Stock-out frequency increase Essential spare parts were unavailable when requested Coordinate with the inventory clerk to expedite reorders and adjust reorder points in the Storeroom Processing work items from a work queue card ¤ The Work queues card on the supervisor dashboard allows you to triage and process work without opening multiple menu screens. Table 3: Actions available within the work queue card ¤ Action How to perform it Operational outcome Assign labor Select the work order row, click Assign, and select a qualified technician Assigns the work order and sends it directly to the technician mobile work list Update status Select the record and choose a new status , such as Approved or Canceled Advances the work order lifecycle and removes it from unapproved queues Open record Click the work order number link Launches the full Work Orders application for detailed planning and job plan adjustments Filter table Enter criteria in the column filter boxes Narrows the active queue to specific assets , locations , or priority levels Real-world example: Responding to a packaging line alert ¤ Consider how a supervisor at the ice cream main plant responds to morning dashboard alerts. Scenario: Morning shift review ¤ The supervisor opens Operational Dashboard : Supervisor . KPI Card 1, PM Compliance: Displays 78%, highlighted in red alert status because the threshold is 85%. Work Queues Card: Displays Overdue PMs (Count: 4) and Emergency Work Orders (Count: 1) . The supervisor clicks Emergency Work Orders . The table displays work order WO-10492 for asset Drive motor on filling line filler FL-02, generated by a condition monitoring high vibration action limit. Direct action: The supervisor clicks Assign , selects a mechanical technician certified in drive alignments, and updates the status to Approved, APPR . Next, the supervisor clicks Overdue PMs , reviews the four routine filter changes, and allocates them to the afternoon shift schedule. How to configure work queues in Work Queue Manager ¤ Select includes some work queues. Administrators can use them as they are, or create and manage their own for the operational dashboards. Step 1: Create the work queue definition ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Work Queue Manager and open it. Click New Work Queue . In the Work Queue field, enter a unique name, such as WQ-OVERDUE-PM . In the Description field, enter a descriptive label, such as Overdue Preventive Maintenance . In the Object Structure field, select the target object structure , such as MXAPIWODETAIL . In the Launch Application field, select WOTRACK or Work Orders . Step 2: Define the query and person group access ¤ In the Query field, select the saved public query that filters the records, such as OVERDUE_PMS . To restrict the queue to specific roles, add the target group in the Person Groups table, such as SUP_MAINT . If left blank, the queue is available across all dashboards with work queue cards. In the Status field, change the value to ACTIVE . Step 3: Add the work queue card to the operational dashboard ¤ Go to the target dashboard, such as Operational Dashboard : Supervisor . Click Edit Dashboard . Add the Work queues card, and select your work queue from the list. Verify that your active work queue is selected. Click Save Dashboard . If you added a person group to the work queue, the queue does not show on the Work queues card by default. People in that group can select the Work queues card, edit the dashboard, and select the queue on the Advanced tab of the card gallery. Alert and work queue checklist ¤ Use this checklist to confirm that dashboard alerting and work queues operate effectively for your team. Table 4: Alert and work queue verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] KPI thresholds configured Every displayed KPI has target, caution, and alert levels defined in KPI Manager [ ] Public visibility enabled KPIs and work queues are marked public or assigned to the correct security group [ ] Active queue status All required work queues in Work Queue Manager are set to Active [ ] Query accuracy Saved queries filter strictly on active, uncompleted records to prevent historical clutter [ ] Direct actions tested Supervisors can assign labor and approve work orders directly from the dashboard card Continue building your skills ¤ Detect developing equipment problems ¤ Condition monitoring feeds automated defect alerts into your emergency work queues. Learn how to configure gauge and characteristic measurement limits. How do I detect issues early? Prioritize incoming work requests ¤ Combine dashboard alerts with structured prioritization criteria based on asset criticality and safety requirements. How do I decide what work should be done? What to do next ¤ What metrics matter? : Understand the core metrics monitored on operational dashboards. How do I detect issues early? : Set up measurement points that generate alerts when equipment degrades. How do I schedule work? : Balance daily alerts with scheduled preventive maintenance . Related topics ¤ What metrics matter? How do I detect issues early? Supervisor: Assign and track work How do I plan recurring maintenance? How do I assign the correct people?

docs.text: How do I detect issues early? ¤ Equipment rarely breaks down without warning. Before a motor bearing seizes or a refrigeration compressor fails, assets show physical symptoms, such as elevated vibration, rising operating temperature, pressure drops, or degraded lubricant color. Condition monitoring allows you to track these physical indicators systematically. By defining acceptable limits for meter readings, Maximo Application Suite Select helps you identify developing defects and generate corrective maintenance before an unexpected breakdown halts operations. Looking to verify your condition monitoring setup right away? Skip to condition monitoring checklist ↓ In Maximo Application Suite Select, you enter meter readings manually. Select does not receive a continuous stream of readings from sensors or IoT devices. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Select the correct meter type before creating records. Gauge meters track numeric values that fluctuate; characteristic meters track qualitative observations; continuous meters track cumulative run hours. Remember that warning limits are informational only. The system does not automatically create work orders when a reading crosses a warning limit. Automated work order generation requires an action limit linked to an active job plan . Avoid setting action limits too close to normal operating variance. Tight thresholds trigger unnecessary work orders and cause alert fatigue for supervisors. Group related meters into meter groups when multiple assets share the same monitoring profile, such as standard drive motors. Choosing the correct meter type ¤ Every condition monitoring strategy begins in the Meters application. The system supports three distinct meter types, each designed for a specific maintenance purpose. Table 1: Meter types and maintenance applications ¤ Meter type How measurements behave Maintenance purpose Typical examples Where configured Gauge Numeric values that fluctuate up and down over time Track operating condition against acceptable upper and lower limits Operating temperature, vibration velocity, line pressure, oil level Condition Monitoring application Characteristic Qualitative observations chosen from a predefined list of values Record visual inspections and trigger work for specific degraded states Oil color, belt condition, leakage severity, corrosion level Condition Monitoring application Continuous Numeric values that accumulate and increase indefinitely Track usage intervals to trigger routine scheduled servicing Operating run hours, odometer mileage, production cycles Preventive Maintenance application Continuous meters track usage intervals, such as running a service every 500 hours, and do not use condition monitoring measurement points. Condition monitoring relies on gauge meters and characteristic meters . How measurement points work ¤ In the Condition Monitoring application, you create a point record that connects a specific meter to an asset or a location . Each point record applies to a single asset or a single location at your site . Table 2: Measurement points versus observation points ¤ Point type Meter type used Limit structure Work generation trigger Measurement point Gauge meter Upper and lower warning limits; upper and lower action limits Reading exceeds an upper action limit or falls below a lower action limit Observation point Characteristic meter Specific observation values mapped from a domain Reading matches an observation value that has an attached job plan or preventive maintenance record Understanding warning limits versus action limits ¤ A frequent point of confusion is the difference between warning limits and action limits on gauge measurement points. Table 3: Limit types on gauge measurement points ¤ Limit type Purpose System behavior Recommended use Warning limit Highlights that an asset is trending away from optimal condition Informational only; recorded in history and visible in reports, but generates no automated work Early warning for inspectors and supervisors during routine rounds Action limit Identifies that an asset has reached an unacceptable condition requiring intervention Triggers work order generation when combined with an active job plan or preventive maintenance record Immediate corrective maintenance to prevent equipment failure Every action limit must include an active job plan or a preventive maintenance record. If an action limit is populated without a job plan or preventive maintenance record, the system generates an error during work order processing. Real-world example: Ice cream plant monitoring ¤ Consider how condition monitoring applies across equipment and areas at the ice cream main plant. Example 1: Drive motor vibration on Filler FL-02 ¤ The drive motor on filling line filler FL-02 operates in the filling line room. Excessive vibration indicates bearing wear or misalignment: Application: Condition Monitoring Asset : Drive motor Meter : VIB-VEL with gauge type, measured in millimeters per second Normal operating range: 0 to 2.5 mm/s Upper warning limit: 2.8 mm/s, signaling early wear during inspection reviews Upper action limit: 4.2 mm/s, mapped to job plan JP-MTR-ALIGN to dispatch a technician for precision alignment and bearing inspection Example 2: Cold storage room ambient temperature ¤ The cold storage room must maintain strict sub-zero temperatures to protect finished product: Application: Condition Monitoring Location : Cold storage room Meter : ROOM-TEMP with gauge type, measured in degrees Celsius Normal operating range: -22°C to -18°C Lower action limit: -26°C, mapped to job plan JP-REF-LOW to check expansion valve settings Upper action limit: -14°C, mapped to job plan JP-REF-HIGH to inspect refrigeration compressors immediately Example 3: Gearbox lubricant inspection ¤ Technicians inspect gearbox oil condition during monthly rounds: Application: Condition Monitoring Asset : Drive motor gearbox Meter : OIL-COND with characteristic type, using values CLEAR , CLOUDY , DARK , and CONTAMINATED Normal values: CLEAR requires no follow-up action Trigger value: CONTAMINATED is mapped to job plan JP-OIL-FLUSH to schedule an immediate oil replacement and seal inspection Common setup mistakes to avoid ¤ Review these four common pitfalls when designing condition monitoring points: Table 4: Common condition monitoring mistakes and solutions ¤ Mistake Why it causes problems Recommended solution Using continuous meters in Condition Monitoring Continuous meters accumulate indefinitely and cannot evaluate upper or lower thresholds Use continuous meters in the Preventive Maintenance application to trigger usage-based maintenance Expecting warning limits to create work orders Warning limits carry no automated workflow triggers in the system Define action limits with attached job plans for conditions that require maintenance work Leaving job plan fields blank on action limits The system cannot determine what tasks or resources are needed when limits are breached Always assign an active job plan or preventive maintenance record to every populated action limit Setting limits without historical baselines Setting action thresholds too tight creates dozens of duplicate work orders for minor temperature spikes Establish baseline readings during normal operating conditions before defining action limits How to set up condition monitoring in desktop applications ¤ Setting up early issue detection follows four sequential steps across the desktop applications. Step 1: Create the meter ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Meter and open it. Click New Meter . In the Meter field, enter a unique identifier, such as VIB-VEL . In the Meter Type field, select GAUGE for variable numeric values or CHARACTERISTIC for qualitative observations. In the Reading Type field, select ACTUAL for raw values or DELTA for change increments. Click Save Meter . Step 2: Associate the meter with the asset or location ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Assets or Location and open it. Open the asset or location record, such as asset Drive motor . Open the Meters tab and click New Row . In the Meter field, select the meter you created in Step 1. Click Save Asset or Save Location . Step 3: Create the measurement point record ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Condition Monitoring and open it. Click New Measure Point . In the Point field, enter a unique point number or accept the system-generated value. Specify the Asset or Location to monitor. In the Meter field, select the associated gauge or characteristic meter . For gauge meters , enter your Upper Warning Limit , Upper Action Limit , Lower Warning Limit , or Lower Action Limit . In the Job Plan or PM field next to each action limit, select the active maintenance plan to execute when the limit is breached. Click Save Measure Point . Step 4: Generate work orders from condition breaches ¤ When technicians record meter readings during inspections, work orders can be generated in two ways: Manual generation: Open the Condition Monitoring record and select Generate Work Order from More Actions . Automated generation: Administrators configure background processing so that work orders generate automatically whenever a qualifying measurement is entered. Condition monitoring checklist ¤ Use this checklist to confirm that your condition monitoring point is properly configured and ready to protect equipment. Table 5: Condition monitoring verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Meter type alignment Gauge meter is used for fluctuating numbers; characteristic meter is used for observational codes [ ] Asset or location link The meter is added to the Meters tab of the target asset or location record [ ] Action limit job plans Every populated action limit has an active job plan or preventive maintenance record assigned [ ] Realistic thresholds Limits reflect true operational boundaries and avoid nuisance triggering during normal startup [ ] Work order priority The work order priority field on the point record is set to reflect the urgency of the condition Continue building your skills ¤ Respond to system alerts and work queues ¤ Once condition monitoring points detect abnormal readings, alerts appear on operational dashboards. Learn how supervisors review and process incoming alerts. How do I act on alerts? Track key performance metrics ¤ Connect condition monitoring data to plant-wide reliability metrics, including Mean Time Between Failures and preventive maintenance compliance. What metrics matter? What to do next ¤ How do I act on alerts? : Review and manage threshold breach alerts on your operational dashboard. What metrics matter? : Discover which metrics help measure the health of your maintenance program. How do I plan recurring maintenance? : Complement condition-based maintenance with structured preventive schedules. Related topics ¤ How do I act on alerts? What metrics matter? How do I track asset history? What happens when an asset fails? How do inspections work?

docs.text: What metrics matter? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select tracks maintenance performance through key performance indicators (KPIs). A KPI measures one specific variable over time, such as how many work orders were completed on schedule, or how long equipment typically runs before failing. Some KPIs are available when you first sign in. You can also create your own. The metrics that matter most depend on your role. A supervisor needs to know whether today's work is on track. An administrator needs to know whether the overall maintenance program is healthy. An inventory clerk needs to know whether parts are available when work demands them. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with three to five KPIs, not twenty. Too many metrics dilute focus and make it harder to act. Set thresholds for every KPI: a green target, a yellow caution level, and a red alert level. Without thresholds, a KPI is just a number. Review KPIs on a regular cadence that matches your role: daily for supervisors, weekly or monthly for managers and administrators. A KPI is only as reliable as the data behind it. If technicians are not closing work orders accurately, completion rate and MTTR figures will be wrong. What metrics matter to supervisors? ¤ Supervisors use KPIs to monitor daily work progress and respond to problems before they escalate. The Operational Dashboard for supervisors gives you a role-based view of the metrics most relevant to your team. Table 1: Supervisor metrics ¤ Metric What it tells you Where to find it Work order completion rate How many work orders were completed vs. scheduled in a given period. A low rate signals resource or planning problems. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor Overdue work orders Work that has passed its required finish date. Growing overdue counts mean scheduling or capacity issues. Operational Dashboard, Work Queues PM compliance The percentage of preventive maintenance work orders completed on schedule. Target is 85% or higher. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor Emergency work orders The count of unplanned, reactive work orders . High numbers indicate equipment is failing unexpectedly instead of being maintained proactively. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor Maintenance backlog The volume of outstanding work. A healthy backlog is 2 to 4 weeks of work. Above 6 weeks signals a resource problem. Work Queues Schedule compliance How often planned work is completed when it was scheduled. Targets above 90% indicate a well-run maintenance program. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor How supervisors use these metrics ¤ Review completion rate and overdue work orders daily. Use the Work Queues card on your Operational Dashboard to act on items directly. You can change status , assign work, or escalate without leaving the dashboard. What metrics matter to administrators? ¤ Administrators use KPIs to assess the health of the overall maintenance program and configure the system to support it. KPI Manager is where administrators create, configure, and manage KPIs for the organization. Table 2: Administrator metrics ¤ Metric What it tells you Where to find it Planned maintenance percentage (PMP) The ratio of planned maintenance hours to total hours. Above 80% means your program is proactive, not reactive. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Mean time between failures (MTBF) The average time equipment runs before failing. Rising MTBF means reliability is improving. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Mean time to repair (MTTR) The average time to repair an asset after failure. High MTTR indicates slow response or complex failures. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Asset availability The percentage of time an asset is operational. Critical for production equipment. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Reactive maintenance ratio Emergency work orders as a percentage of total work. World-class programs keep this below 10%. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer KPI threshold breaches KPIs that have crossed caution or alert thresholds. These require investigation or program adjustments. KPI Manager How administrators use these metrics ¤ Use KPI Manager to create KPIs with defined targets, caution levels, and alert thresholds. Make frequently reviewed KPIs public so they appear on role-specific Operational Dashboards. Review program-level metrics monthly and adjust PM schedules or resource allocation based on trends. Three configuration points that are easy to miss: Set thresholds on every KPI. A KPI without a green target, yellow caution, and red alert level is just a number. The traffic-light colour coding on the Operational Dashboard only activates when thresholds are configured. Without them, supervisors see data but no signal. Make KPIs public. A KPI configured in KPI Manager is private by default. It will not appear on anyone's Operational Dashboard until you explicitly make it public or assign it to a security group . Activate new work queues. In Maximo Application Suite Select, a newly created work queue defaults to inactive. If a work queue shows no results on the Operational Dashboard, check that it has been activated in Work Queue Manager. What metrics matter to inventory clerks? ¤ Inventory clerks use metrics to ensure parts are available when work demands them. Stock-related KPIs help prevent delays caused by missing parts. Table 3: Inventory clerk metrics ¤ Metric What it tells you Where to find it Stock-outs How often a required part was unavailable when needed. Frequent stock-outs delay work and increase downtime . Operational Dashboard, Inventory Clerk Inventory turnover How quickly stock is consumed and replenished. Low turnover may mean overstocking; high turnover may indicate understocking. Operational Dashboard, Inventory Clerk Parts requested vs. available The gap between what technicians need and what is in stock. Helps prioritize reordering. Operational Dashboard, Inventory Clerk Where to find KPIs in the product ¤ Table 4: KPI applications ¤ Application Who uses it What it does KPI Manager Administrators Create, configure, and manage KPIs. Set targets, thresholds, and security group access. KPI Viewer All roles View individual KPI values and trends. Read-only access to configured KPIs. KPI Templates Administrators Create reusable templates to generate multiple related KPIs efficiently. Operational Dashboard All roles Role-based dashboard showing KPI trend cards, work queue cards, and alert summaries. Work Queue Manager Administrators Create and manage work queues that surface actionable items on the Operational Dashboard. Continue building your skills ¤ Act on what the data tells you ¤ When a KPI breaches a threshold, the Operational Dashboard surfaces it as an alert. Learn how to respond directly from the dashboard without leaving the view. How do I act on alerts? Catch problems before they become failures ¤ Condition monitoring feeds asset health data into your metrics. Set it up so your KPIs reflect equipment state, not just work order counts. How do I detect issues early? What to do next ¤ How do I act on alerts? : Use your Operational Dashboard to take action when KPIs breach thresholds. How do I plan recurring maintenance? : Improving PM compliance starts with a well-configured maintenance schedule. How do I detect issues early? : Condition monitoring feeds asset health metrics on your dashboard. Related topics ¤ How do I detect issues early? How do I act on alerts? docs.text: How do I assign the correct people? ¤ Match the right technician or crew to a work order so the job goes to someone with the correct skills, availability, and access. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Set up crafts and labor records before assigning work. A labor record without a craft won't appear when you filter by skill. See How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? if your workforce isn't configured yet. Check availability before assigning. The system shows scheduled hours and availability based on the labor record's calendar and shift. Use crews when multiple people need to work on the same job at the same time. Assigning a crew takes one step instead of adding each person individually. Set a scheduled start date on every assignment. Without a date, the assignment won't surface in scheduling views at the correct time for planning or dispatch. Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Assignment methods ¤ Method Best for Work orders , Plans section Assigning an individual to a work order Crew assignment Assigning a whole team to a job in one step How to assign an individual to a work order ¤ What to do: Open the Work orders application. Search for and open the work order . Go to the Plans section. Under Assignment , click Edit assignments . In the Labor field, enter or select the person to assign. Enter the estimated hours in Time to complete . This is how the system calculates whether a person is over-allocated. Without it, the system shows unlimited availability for that slot and supervisors can unknowingly double-book people. Save the work order . Note Assignments filter by the default craft on the labor record. A person with the correct skill set as a secondary craft will not appear. If the list is empty or missing expected people, check that the correct craft is set as their default in the Labor application. How to assign a crew ¤ Use a crew when a group of people need to work together on the same job. What to do: Open the Work orders application. Search for and open the work order . Go to the Plans section. Under Assignment , click Edit assignments . In the Crew field, enter or select the crew name. The system adds all active crew members as individual assignments. Save the work order . Why isn't someone showing up as available? ¤ The most common reasons a technician doesn't appear in the Available Labor list: No craft assigned ¤ Available Labor filters by default craft only . A person with the correct skill as a secondary craft is excluded from the results. They exist in the system but the filter doesn't find them. What to do : Open the Labor application, find the person's record, and confirm the correct craft is set as their default, not just listed as a secondary craft . Calendar or shift mismatch ¤ Available Labor uses the calendar and shift on the labor record. If the scheduled start date falls outside the person's working hours, they may not appear or show as unavailable. What to do : Check that the calendar and shift on the labor record match the crew 's working schedule. Work order status doesn't allow assignment ¤ You can only assign labor to work orders in an approvable or approved status . Work orders in Waiting for Approval or Approved status accept assignments. What to do : Check the work order status and change it to APPR before assigning. Assigning the correct people consistently means work gets done faster and teams stop stepping on each other. Continue building your skills ¤ Understand why a technician can't see their assigned work ¤ After assigning work, verify it's visible to the correct people. Why can't technicians see their assigned work? Set up the workforce records behind assignments ¤ If assignments aren't working correctly, the issue is often in how crafts , calendars, and labor records are set up. How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Related topics ¤ How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Why can't technicians see their assigned work? How do I schedule work? docs.text: How do I customize dropdown values? ¤ Domains control the values users can pick from in dropdown lists and status fields across the application. As an administrator, you can add your own labels to existing status dropdowns to match your organization's terminology. Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Domain terminology ¤ Term What it means Domain A list of valid values attached to a field, such as the values available in a work order status dropdown Synonym domain A domain used for status fields. Lets you add your own labels that map to built-in system statuses Internal value The system status that drives business logic, such as WAPPR (Waiting for Approval) or COMP (Complete) Synonym value A custom label you add that maps to an internal value, such as "Needs sign-off" mapping to WAPPR What you can do in IBM Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Table 2: Domain customization tasks ¤ Task How Add a custom label to a status field Add a synonym value to an existing domain Use different terminology across your organization Set a synonym value at the organization level Find which domain controls a field Use Alt+F1 on the field, then look up the domain in Domains Why add synonym values? ¤ Synonym values let you use your organization's terminology without affecting how the system works underneath. For example, your team might call a work order status "Needs sign-off" rather than "Waiting for Approval." You can add "Needs sign-off" as a synonym that maps to the built-in WAPPR status . Users see your label. The system still processes work orders using the standard internal status . Common uses: Rename work order or asset statuses to match your organization's language Add organization-specific labels for a status Localize terminology for your team What you cannot change ¤ You can add synonym values, but you cannot add new internal values. The system's business logic, meaning what happens when a work order reaches APPR, COMP, or CLOSE, is hardwired to those internal values and cannot be modified. If you need a status that behaves differently from any existing internal value, that is not possible through domain configuration. How to add a synonym value ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Domains and open it. Search for the domain you want to update. For example, search for WOSTATUS to find the work order status domain . Open the domain record. In the Values table, click Add Row , the + button above the values list. Leave the Internal Value field set to the existing system status you want to map to. Enter your custom label in the Value field. Add a description to explain the value. If this value applies to a specific organization only, set the Organization field. An organization-level synonym is visible across all sites in that organization. A value with no organization set applies system-wide. Choosing the wrong scope can expose values to users who should not see them, or hide them from users who need them. To make this the default value for the field, select Default . Click OK . Save the domain record. Before you add synonym values after go-live ¤ Adding synonym values at the organization level after your system is live can cause issues with existing records. If you add synonyms with an organization specified, records that were created before the change may no longer match valid values. If you need to add organization-scoped synonyms after go-live, add a synonym for every existing internal value at the same scope before saving. If you are unsure about the impact, test the change in a non-production environment first, or contact IBM support. How to find the correct domain for a field ¤ To identify which domain controls a specific field: Place your cursor in the field. Press Alt+F1 to open field help. The field name and domain name appear in the field help panel. In the Find navigation item field, search for Domains and open it. Then search for that domain name. Continue building your skills ¤ Set up maps for your field teams ¤ Visual maps let technicians and supervisors see where assets and work orders are located. Set up a map after your dropdown values are in place. How do I set up maps? Automate your notifications ¤ Keep your team informed automatically. Set up email and push notifications so people know when work is assigned or updated. How do I automate communication? Related topics ¤ How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? : craft domains and labor status values How do I classify assets ? How do I schedule work?

docs.text: Why don't technicians see their assigned work? ¤ This is one of the most common issues. Work is assigned, but the technician can't see it in their queue. Looking to troubleshoot assignment visibility right away? Skip to work assignment visibility checklist ↓ Likely causes ¤ User permissions were updated but sessions weren't refreshed ¤ When permissions change, active sessions might not pick up the new access rights immediately. What to do : Have the technician log out of all sessions completely, then log back in. This forces the system to reload their current permissions. Clear all sessions Logging out of all sessions (including mobile devices and any open browser tabs) often resolves visibility issues immediately. Missing site or data access ¤ The technician might not have access to the site where the work order exists, or their data restrictions might prevent them from seeing certain work orders . What to check : Verify the technician has access to the correct site Check if data restrictions are limiting what they can see Confirm their security group includes the necessary permissions What to do : Contact your system administrator to review and update site access or data restrictions. Cached sessions not picking up new permissions ¤ Even after permissions are updated, cached session data might prevent the changes from taking effect. What to do : Have the technician: Log out completely from all devices Clear browser cache if using a web browser Close and reopen mobile apps Log back in Why can't I update assignment status ? ¤ You might see validation errors or the status doesn't save when you try to move from Assigned → Started → Complete. Status sequence skipped ¤ Some organizations require work orders to progress through specific statuses in order. You can't skip steps. Example : You can't go directly from "Assigned" to "Complete" without going through "In Progress" first. What to do : Follow the required status sequence for your organization. Date validation errors ¤ The system validates that dates make sense. Common issues: Finish date must be after start date Scheduled date must be after creation date Actual dates must align with planned dates What to do : Check all dates on the work order and correct any that are out of sequence. Updates not committing to the database ¤ Sometimes changes appear to save but don't actually commit to the database. What to do : Verify the change was saved by refreshing the screen Check for error messages that might have been missed Try the update again Contact your system administrator if the problem persists Why is it hard to track who is doing what? ¤ Supervisors often struggle with visibility into team workload and assignments. Known limitations ¤ Out-of-the-box views : Standard views don't easily show workload per technician Reporting complexity : Reports can include incorrect or excessive data Filtering behavior : Filters might not work as expected for assignment tracking What to do : Use custom queries or reports designed for your organization Ask your system administrator about available workload views Consider using dashboards that show team assignments Why do assignments disappear after work order completion? ¤ Assignments are typically removed when the work order is closed or completed. Impact ¤ No historical assignment tracking unless configured separately Reporting needs to rely on work order history instead of active assignments What to do : If you need historical assignment data, work with your system administrator to set up: Assignment history tracking Custom reports that capture assignment data before completion Archive processes that preserve assignment information Work assignment visibility checklist ¤ Use this checklist to diagnose and resolve missing work order assignments: Table 1: Work assignment visibility checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Active labor record Technician username is linked to an active Labor record in the Labor application [ ] Craft and skill match Labor record craft matches the craft required on the work order assignment [ ] Shift calendar active Calendar and shift assigned to the labor record cover the scheduled work date [ ] Assignment dates valid Labor assignment has an effective start date and no expired end date [ ] Work order status Work order is in APPR, WSCHED, or INPRG status , not WAPPR or CLOSE [ ] Site security access User security group grants permission to view records for the specific site [ ] Session refreshed Technician has signed out and signed back in after recent permission updates Continue building your skills ¤ Know what work matters ¤ Create job plans that standardize tasks, parts, and time estimates so every technician does the work the same way. How do I decide what work should be done? Plan recurring maintenance ¤ With your team seeing their work correctly, set up schedules that generate work orders automatically so you're not creating them one at a time. How do I plan recurring maintenance? Related topics ¤ How do I assign the correct people? Why can't I see new work in IBM Maximo Mobile? How do I find my work? How do I complete a job? Still stuck? ¤ If this page did not answer your question: Browse all Q&A: Get answers In the product: Click the help icon (?) in the top right For a specific field: Click the field name or press Alt+F1

docs.text: How do I decide what work should be done? ¤ Create job plans that list the steps, parts, and tools for common maintenance tasks. Job plans work like templates. They keep work consistent every time. You plan the work once. Then you reuse the plan. This saves time and reduces mistakes. Looking to validate a job plan right away? Skip to job plan verification checklist ↓ Figure 1 illustrates how a job plan template flows into an approved work order : Job plan template : defines sequential task steps, estimated labor and craft hours, required materials and quantities, special tools, and default work order priority. Application paths : attached to a recurring preventive maintenance schedule or applied directly to an on-demand corrective work order . Approved work order outcome : upon approval, the system automatically populates task checklists, schedules labor assignments, generates storeroom material reservations, and applies priority ratings. Figure 1: How job plans flow into work orders 💡 Tips: Best practices for job plans ¤ Start with common tasks Create plans for work you do most often. Keep it simple Use clear, short instructions. Add safety notes Include warnings for dangerous work. Update regularly Change plans based on worker feedback. Use for all scheduled work Every maintenance schedule should have a job plan . When to use job plans ¤ Use job plans for: Tasks you do regularly, such as monthly inspections Work with multiple steps Jobs that need specific parts or tools Tasks where safety matters Scheduled maintenance What goes in a job plan ¤ Include these items : Work description What you need to do and why. Task list Step-by-step instructions. Labor estimates How many people and hours you need. When this job plan is applied to a work order and the work order is approved, the system automatically creates assignment records for each labor entry. Without labor estimates, no assignments are created, so planners must add them manually every time. Required materials Parts and supplies you need. When a work order with planned materials is approved, the system automatically creates storeroom reservations. Without materials on the job plan , no reservations are made and parts may not be available when the technician arrives on site . Tools Special equipment or tools. Safety information Hazards and safety steps. How to create and use job plans ¤ Create the job plan ¤ Open the Job Plans application Add a clear name and description List all work tasks in order Add labor , materials, and tools Set the WO Priority field. This pre-fills priority on every work order generated from this plan. Without it, work orders default to null priority and sort to the bottom of every scheduling and assignment view, and urgent work becomes invisible to planners. Use with scheduled maintenance ¤ Attach job plans to your maintenance schedules. Work orders include the job plan automatically. Use with work orders ¤ Add job plans to individual work orders . Technicians see all steps and materials. Keep plans current ¤ Review completed work. Update job plans based on what actually happened. Add missing steps or materials. To change a job plan that is already active, select Revise Job Plan from More Actions first. BMXAA0024E JOBTASK action ADD is not allowed TODO: Add visual content A video showing how to create a simple job plan would be useful here. Job plan verification checklist ¤ Before activating a job plan or attaching it to preventive maintenance schedules, verify that all core planning fields, tasks, and resource estimates are complete. Check Item What to verify [ ] Task sequence All work steps are listed in sequential order with clear instructions and estimated durations. [ ] Labor estimates and crafts Craft , skill level, and estimated hours are specified for each task so automatic assignment records are generated upon work order approval. [ ] Material reservations Required item numbers, direct issue items , and quantities are entered with designated storerooms so inventory reservations generate automatically. [ ] Tool requirements Required tools and operational hour estimates are attached to tasks. [ ] Work order priority The WO Priority field is set so work orders generated from this plan sort correctly in dispatch and scheduling queues. [ ] Safety precautions and hazards Necessary safety steps, lockout or tagout precautions, and hazard warnings are documented on tasks. [ ] Status activation The job plan status is changed to Active so it is available for selection on work orders , preventive maintenance records, and routes. Why job plans help ¤ Everyone does the work the same way No confusion about steps or procedures. Work goes faster No time spent figuring out what to do. You get the correct parts All materials are listed upfront. Reservations are created automatically at approval, so no manual follow-up is needed. Training is easier New workers have clear instructions. Costs are predictable You know time and materials in advance. Assignments are created for you Labor entries on the job plan generate assignment records when the work order is approved. The correct people appear in the assignment queue without a planner having to add them manually. Continue building your skills ¤ Plan recurring maintenance ¤ With job plans in place, set up schedules that generate work orders automatically instead of creating them one at a time. How do I plan recurring maintenance? Schedule your team ¤ Set up calendars and routes so work is assigned when people are available and inspections run in sequence. How do I schedule work? Monitor performance ¤ Track whether work is being completed on time, how much backlog your team carries, and where to intervene. What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ How do I plan recurring maintenance? How do I schedule work? How do I complete a job? What is a work order ?

docs.text: How do I plan recurring maintenance? ¤ Create a schedule that automatically generates work orders . The system creates work orders for you based on time, such as every 30 days, or equipment use, such as every 500 hours. This helps you maintain equipment before it breaks. You set up the schedule once. The system does the rest. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with a small number of critical assets , such as 5 to 10, then expand once the process works reliably Always create job plans before setting up schedules. They ensure consistent work. Set lead times based on your actual parts procurement time plus a buffer, typically 7 to 14 days Review completed work orders monthly and adjust schedules based on actual equipment performance Activate schedules gradually to avoid overwhelming your team with work orders When to use this ¤ Use recurring maintenance when you need to: Inspect or service equipment regularly Maintain equipment based on how much it runs Follow manufacturer maintenance schedules Prevent equipment breakdowns Keep consistent maintenance records How to set it up ¤ Step 1: Create a job plan (recommended) ¤ A job plan lists the work steps, parts needed, and time required. It keeps the work consistent every time. You can skip this step, but job plans make maintenance easier. Table 1: Job plan contents and when each is required ¤ Include in job plan Required when Task list The work has multiple steps that technicians must follow in order Labor entries You want assignment records created automatically at work order approval Material entries You want storeroom reservations created automatically at work order approval WO Priority This work must appear correctly sorted in scheduling views Step 2: Create the maintenance record ¤ Open the Preventive Maintenance application Choose the equipment or location Describe the maintenance work clearly Step 3: Set the schedule ¤ Choose how often to do the work: Time-based schedule Every 30 days Every 2 weeks Every 6 months Usage-based schedule Every 500 operating hours Every 1000 cycles Every 200 miles Combined schedule Every 6 months OR 300 hours, whichever comes first Every year OR 1000 hours, whichever comes first Fixed vs. floating: choose carefully ¤ This setting controls when the next work order is generated. Fixed schedule : The next work order is created on the calendar interval regardless of whether the previous one was completed. A monthly PM generates every 30 days, every time. Floating schedule : The next work order is not created until the previous one reaches a completed, closed, or cancelled status . If a work order is never closed, the PM stops generating entirely, with no warning. One missed closure can silently halt maintenance on an asset indefinitely. Use a fixed schedule for most time-based PMs. Use floating only when the next maintenance interval should genuinely depend on when the last job was finished, such as usage-based or condition-driven work. Step 4: Set lead time (optional but recommended) ¤ Lead time tells the system when to create the work order before it's due. Example: Set 7 days lead time. The system creates the work order a week early. This gives you time to get parts and schedule workers. If lead time is too short, parts and labor won't be ready when the work order is generated. If it's left at zero, the work order appears on its due date, leaving no time to prepare. A lead time shorter than your parts procurement time virtually guarantees a delayed job. Step 5: Add the job plan ¤ Link your job plan to the schedule. Each work order will include the same steps and parts list. To change a job plan that is already active, select Revise Job Plan first. For details, see Keep plans current . In practice Organizations often create overly complex schedules at the start, which are hard to maintain Schedules are frequently set up but never activated, so no work orders are generated Lead times are often too short, causing parts shortages and rushed work Teams sometimes create schedules without job plans , leading to inconsistent maintenance What happens next ¤ After you activate the schedule: The system creates work orders automatically Each work order includes your job plan steps Technicians complete the work The system calculates the next due date The system creates the next work order The cycle repeats until you stop it. Common mistakes ¤ Creating too many schedules at once instead of starting with critical equipment Setting unrealistic frequencies, either too often or not often enough Not linking job plans , so technicians don't know what to do Forgetting to activate schedules after creating them Setting lead times that are too short for parts procurement What good looks like ¤ Poor setup Create 50 Preventive Maintenance (PM) schedules for all equipment at once. No job plans . Activate all immediately. Good setup Start with 5-10 critical assets . Create detailed job plans first. Test one schedule. Adjust based on results. Gradually add more equipment. Decision support: Choosing schedule type ¤ Use time-based when: Equipment runs continuously or predictably Manufacturer recommends calendar-based maintenance You need simple, easy-to-manage schedules Use usage-based when: Equipment usage varies significantly Meters are reliable and regularly updated Maintenance depends on actual wear, measured in hours, cycles, or miles Use combined when: You want maintenance to happen even if equipment sits idle Usage is unpredictable You need a safety net for both scenarios Why proper planning matters ¤ If schedules are not set up correctly, equipment fails unexpectedly instead of being maintained proactively If lead times are too short, technicians wait for parts and work gets delayed If job plans are missing, maintenance quality varies and problems are missed Poor scheduling leads to either too much work, which overwhelms teams, or too little, which causes equipment failures If a floating schedule is used and a work order is never closed, no further work orders are generated for that asset , so maintenance stops without any alert A schedule left inactive after setup generates no work orders , ever. The first sign is typically an unexpected equipment failure Once your PMs are running, the system takes care of the scheduling. You focus on the work, not the calendar. Continue building your skills ¤ Know what work matters ¤ Create job plans that standardize tasks, parts, and time estimates, then link them to your schedules so technicians always know what to do. How do I decide what work should be done? Schedule your team ¤ Set up calendars and routes so work is assigned when people are available and inspections are grouped efficiently. How do I schedule work? Related topics ¤ Why isn't my PM generating work orders ? How do I decide what work should be done? How do I schedule work? How do I manage more assets ? docs.text: How do I schedule work? ¤ Use calendars to set working hours. Use routes to group inspection points. This helps you plan when work happens and organize inspections efficiently. Calendars track when your team works. Routes let you create inspection work orders for multiple items at once. Looking to verify your work schedule right away? Skip to work scheduling and calendar readiness checklist ↓ 💡 Tips: Best practices for calendars and routes ¤ For calendars: Start simple. Match your standard work week. Add holidays as you go. Update calendars when shifts change. For routes: Group equipment that is close together. Keep routes focused. Do not mix unrelated items . Update routes when equipment changes. Use clear names. Calendars: Set working time ¤ Calendars show when work can happen. They include: Working days and hours Shifts, such as 7 AM to 3 PM and 3 PM to 11 PM Holidays and shutdowns Days off Figure 1 shows how calendars connect to labor , equipment, and work scheduling across three areas: Calendar definition : establishes shift patterns for working hours, standard work weeks for working days, and non-working time for holidays and shutdowns. Assigned records : attaches calendars to labor records for individual worker availability, crew records for crew group availability, and locations or assets for shutdown windows. Work scheduling : validates worker availability against open shifts to assign target start and finish dates. Figure 1: How calendars connect to labor, equipment, and work scheduling When to use calendars ¤ Use calendars to: Set standard work shifts Track holidays and shutdowns Schedule work during available hours Assign work when people are working Calculate realistic finish times How to set up calendars ¤ Step 1: Create shifts Define a shift pattern that sets the working days, such as Monday to Friday Set start and end times, such as 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM Enter total work hours per day Step 2: Create the calendar Make a calendar for your organization Apply shifts to show the work schedule Mark holidays, shutdowns, and days off as non-working time Select includes some calendars, such as a day shift and an evening shift. You can use them as they are or duplicate them to make your own. [SME confirmation required: Confirm which calendars Select includes and that you can duplicate them.] Step 3: Assign calendars Apply calendars to your team members Apply to locations or equipment if needed System uses calendars to schedule work Table 1: Where to assign a calendar ¤ Assign calendar to Required when Labor records Assigning work to individuals so the system can calculate availability correctly Crews Assigning work to a crew as a group Locations or assets Only when the system needs to calculate scheduled work based on when a location or asset is available, such as for planned shutdowns Routes: Group inspection points ¤ Routes are lists of items that need regular inspection. Create one route. Generate work orders for all items at once. Figure 2 illustrates how a multi-stop route generates work across inspection points: Multi-stop route : defines sequential stops, such as Stop 1 ( Filler FL-02 ), Stop 2 ( Spiral Freezer SF-01 ), and Stop 3 ( Batch Mixer MX-01 ). Option A (Separate work orders per stop) : generates individual child work orders ( WO 101 , WO 102 , WO 103 ) so each machine retains independent maintenance history and cost tracking. Option B (One work order with multiple tasks) : generates a single consolidated work order containing sequential tasks ( Task 10 , Task 20 , Task 30 ) with unified completion at the route level. Figure 2: How routes generate work orders across multiple inspection stops When to use routes ¤ Use routes for: Regular inspection rounds, such as daily equipment checks Safety inspections at multiple locations Maintenance on similar equipment Any work that follows a set path How to set up routes ¤ Step 1: Create the route 1. Open the Routes application 2. Add a clear name, such as "Daily Production Line Inspection" 3. List all items to inspect, called "stops" Step 2: Use the route Add the route to a work order System creates work orders for each stop Add to a maintenance schedule for automatic use Choose: separate work orders or one work order with multiple tasks Table 2: Work order options for routes and when to use each ¤ Option Use when Separate work orders per stop Each stop needs to be tracked, costed, and closed independently, for example daily checks on Filler FL-02, Spiral Freezer SF-01, and Batch Mixer MX-01 where each job has its own history One work order with multiple tasks All stops are part of a single job and cost tracking at the route level is sufficient Step 3: Complete the work Technicians follow the route They complete inspections at each stop All work tracks under the main work order TODO: Add visual content A video showing how to create a simple inspection route would be useful here. Work scheduling and calendar readiness checklist ¤ Before assigning work orders or activating multi-stop routes, verify that working calendars, shift patterns, and route configurations are properly established. Check Item What to verify [ ] Standard shift definition Working days, start and end times, and shift hours are defined in the Calendar application. [ ] Non-working time Holidays, planned plant shutdowns, and non-working days are marked on the calendar. [ ] Labor calendar association Each technician and worker has their primary calendar and shift assigned on their Labor record so availability displays accurately. [ ] Crew calendar assignment Assigned crews have active calendars reflecting crew shift patterns. [ ] Asset and location shutdown calendar Equipment requiring shutdown windows has calendar constraints defined if scheduling calculations must enforce operating downtime . [ ] Route stop sequence Route stops list all inspection assets or locations in logical physical travel order. [ ] Route generation type Route options specify whether to generate child work orders per stop for separate asset history or multiple tasks on a single work order . Continue building your skills ¤ Monitor performance ¤ With scheduling in place, track whether work is being completed on time, how much backlog your team carries, and where to intervene. What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ How do I plan recurring maintenance? How do I decide what work should be done? How do I complete a job? How do I assign the correct people?

docs.text: Why isn't my PM generating work orders ? ¤ You set up a preventive maintenance record, called a PM, but the work order you expected is not there. Or you try to generate a work order and see a message such as "is not due yet". Looking to troubleshoot right away? Skip to the PM generation checklist ↓ Common causes ¤ The PM is not active ¤ A PM generates work orders only when its status is Active. A PM that is still a draft, or one that was set to inactive, is skipped. What to do : Open the PM and check its status . If it is not Active, activate it. The asset or location is not operating ¤ The asset or location on the PM must have a status of Operating. If it has a different status , such as Not Ready, the system does not generate the work order . You might see a message such as "The asset or location associated with PM 1038 has a status of NOT READY. Change the status to an Active status to generate work orders ." What to do : Check the status of the asset or location on the PM. Change it to Operating if the equipment is in service. A floating schedule is waiting for the last work order ¤ A floating schedule does not create the next work order until the previous one is completed, closed, or cancelled. While the previous work order is still open, you might see a message such as "PM IC-11460 is not due yet, or it does not fall within the active season." What to do : Find the open work order from the previous cycle and finish or close it. If the next work order should not depend on the last one, change the PM to a fixed schedule. For the difference, see Fixed vs. floating: choose carefully . The PM is not due yet ¤ By default, the system checks the frequency of each PM and generates work orders only for PMs that are due. If you generate work orders by hand before the due date, nothing is created. What to do : Check the next due date on the PM. If you need the work order now, clear Use Frequency Criteria in the Generate Work Orders dialog. The system then generates a work order for the selected parent PM regardless of its due date. You tried to generate from a child PM ¤ Work orders can be generated only from the top level PM in a PM hierarchy. If you try it from a child PM, you might see a message such as "PM 1039 is not a top-level PM and cannot generate work orders ." What to do : Open the PM Hierarchy tab, find the parent PM, and generate from there. Why did only some work orders generate? ¤ A parent PM can trigger work orders for its whole PM hierarchy. If one PM in the hierarchy has an asset or location that is not Operating, the system skips that PM and the PMs below it. The rest of the hierarchy can still generate. What to do : Check the asset or location status for every PM in the hierarchy. When you change the status of a parent location or asset , you can roll the status down the hierarchy so the children stay consistent. Why hasn't the work order appeared yet, even though the PM is active? ¤ The system does not create work orders the moment you activate a PM. Generation runs on a schedule in the background. [SME confirmation required: Confirm how often work order generation runs in Select, and whether it runs overnight. The source describing a once a day, overnight run is a video transcript for Maximo Manage.] What to do : Check again after the next generation run. If you need the work order now, generate it by hand with the Generate Work Orders action. PM generation checklist ¤ Use this checklist to find out why a PM is not creating work orders : Table 1: PM generation checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] PM status The PM status is Active, not draft or inactive [ ] Asset or location status The asset or location on the PM has a status of Operating [ ] Schedule type If the schedule is floating, the previous work order is completed, closed, or cancelled [ ] Due date The PM is due, or Use Frequency Criteria is cleared for a manual generate [ ] PM hierarchy You generate from the top level PM, and every asset or location in the hierarchy is Operating [ ] Generation timing Enough time has passed for the next background generation run 💡 Tip: Close work orders promptly on floating schedules ¤ A floating schedule stops generating when one work order is left open. Close or cancel finished work orders so the next one can generate. Related topics ¤ How do I plan recurring maintenance? How do I plan my preventive maintenance strategy? How do I decide what work should be done? How do I schedule work? docs.text: How do I add users? ¤ Before people can work in IBM Maximo Application Suite Select, they need a user account with the correct security group assigned. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Use consistent naming conventions for user IDs Follow principle of least privilege, that is, minimum access needed Keep security group assignments organized What to do ¤ Add a user ¤ Open the Users application. Click Create user . Specify a login email . Specify a user ID . Optionally, add a note in the memo . Example: Temporary access for contractor at ice cream plant A Provide a display name . This is the full name of the user or a recognizable preferred name. Click Select groups and add the user to at least one security group . An email is sent to the login email address. Table 1: Security groups ¤ A security group is a collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. A role determines what a person can see and do in Maximo Application Suite Select. Assign each user to the security group that matches their role: Security group What they can do System admin Manages system configuration and user access. System administrators can configure domains , communication templates , AI settings, create users, and set up security groups , but typically do not perform day-to-day operational work. Example tasks: Set up notification templates, manage user roles, set up security groups , configure system settings, and maintain data structures. Supervisor Oversees operations and team activities. Supervisors can plan and approve work, review technician work, monitor assets and performance, and access analytics to track progress. Example tasks: Assign and approve work orders , review KPIs, review inspection results, manage job plans , and monitor asset condition and maintenance schedules. Technician Performs maintenance and operational work. Technicians can view and update assigned work, complete inspections, record labor hours, report materials used, and record asset data such as meter readings and condition details. Example tasks: Complete work orders , enter inspection results, update asset condition, record labor hours, report materials used, and report meter readings. Requester Submits and tracks service requests. Requesters have limited access and cannot perform operational or administrative tasks. This role is focused on initiating and monitoring work requests. Example tasks: Create a service request for a broken asset and track its status until it is resolved. Inventory clerk Manages inventory and storeroom operations. Inventory clerks can maintain stock, process item movements, adjust inventory balances, and ensure accurate inventory records. Example tasks: Receive items into inventory , issue materials to work orders , perform inventory counts, adjust inventory balances, and manage storerooms. Note You must assign at least one security group . The user cannot access applications until a security group is assigned. User preferences ¤ Users update their preferences in their profile. They open the profile menu from the top right of the header and can select preferences, such as a default application , storeroom, locale, and language. Continue building your skills ¤ Set up your workforce ¤ After adding users, create the craft and labor records that let you assign work to the correct people. How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Customize your dropdown values ¤ Add your organization's terminology to status fields and dropdowns so the system speaks your team's language. How do I customize dropdown values? Related topics ¤ How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? How do I assign the correct people? How do I customize dropdown values?

docs.text: How do I automate communication? ¤ Communication templates let you send automatic emails when things happen in the system, such as when a work order changes status or a task is assigned. Push notifications send real-time alerts to mobile devices so field technicians know about new or updated work without having to check the app. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Set the status of a communication template to Active before trying to use it. Inactive templates will not send. Do not edit the built-in system templates. Duplicate an existing template and modify the copy instead. Use roles as recipients rather than hardcoding individual email addresses. Roles resolve dynamically, so notifications reach the correct person even when team membership changes. Test your template by triggering the relevant action on a test record before rolling it out. Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Communication terminology ¤ Term What it means Communication template A reusable email template that can be triggered automatically or manually from a record Accessible from Controls where the template can be used: Applications or All Role A dynamic recipient definition that resolves to a person or group at the time the email is sent Substitution variable A placeholder in the template body that pulls live data from the record, such as the work order number Push notification A real-time alert sent to the IBM Maximo Mobile app on a user's mobile device Communication templates ¤ Communication templates automate outbound email for work order assignments, status changes, approvals, and other events. You create a template once, then attach it to an escalation , a workflow, or trigger it manually from a record. How to create a communication template ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Communication Templates and open it. Click New Communication Template . Enter a unique Template ID and a clear description. Set Accessible From to the context where this template will be used, such as APPS or ALL . Enter a Send From email address. This is the address recipients will see as the sender. Enter a Subject line. Use substitution variables to include record data, for example: Work order :wonum has been assigned to you Enter the message body. You can use substitution variables here too, for example :description to include the work order description. Go to the Recipients tab. Add recipients using one or more of the following: Roles : recommended. The role resolves to the correct person at send time. Person groups : sends to group members based on availability. Persons : sends to a specific named person. Email addresses : sends to a fixed address. For each recipient, select To , cc , or bcc . Save the template. Use Change Status to set the template status to Active . Send an email about a KPI ¤ When a KPI reaches its caution or alert level, you can email the people who need to act. From the KPI, use the Create Communication action and choose a communication template to fill in the subject and message. The email is recorded in the KPI's log. [SME confirmation required: Confirm that the Create Communication action is available for KPIs in Select, and whether an administrator can set up these emails to send automatically when a KPI reaches a threshold.] Push notifications ¤ Push notifications send real-time alerts to the IBM Maximo Mobile app on iOS and Android devices. Users receive a notification on their device when an event occurs, such as a work order being assigned to them, without needing to have the app open. Setting up push notifications is a two-step process: generate an API key from the IBM push notification portal, then configure it in MAS. Step 1: Generate an API key ¤ Open https://pushnotification.suite.maximo.com in a browser. Sign in with your IBMid. Enter a meaningful name for the API key, for example MAS-PROD-PushNotif . Click Generate API Key . Copy the API key immediately. It will not be shown again once you leave the page. Store it securely. Step 2: Configure push notifications in MAS ¤ In MAS, click the Administration icon and go to Configurations . In the Users and Identity section, click Push Notifications . In the Bundle Identifier field, enter: com.ibm.iot.maximo.mobile In the URL field, enter: https://pushnotification.suite.maximo.com/pushnotification/sendMessage In the API Key field, paste the key you generated in Step 1. Save the configuration. To confirm the setup is working, ask a user to log in via the IBM Maximo Mobile app and trigger a relevant event such as a workflow assignment. The notification should arrive on their device within a few seconds. When users receive push notifications ¤ A user receives push notifications only when all of the following are true: The user has an active session in IBM Maximo Mobile. The user has not signed out of the app. The app has not been reset. If a user's session expires, notifications stop until the user signs in again. The network on the device must also allow connections to the Apple and Google push notification services. Continue building your skills ¤ Configure Maximo Mobile for field teams ¤ Let technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks use a mobile app to access their work from anywhere. How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? Load your existing data ¤ Now that your configuration is in place, bring in your locations , assets , and inventory from existing records. How do I prepare data for import? Related topics ¤ How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? How do I set up maps? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? Administrator: Add users
