docs.text: Why does my data look wrong? ¤ When dashboard reports display unexpected figures, asset counts look inflated, inventory balances show negative numbers, or assets seem disconnected from their physical rooms, data anomalies are almost always the cause. Inaccurate data undermines trust in your maintenance system and distorts performance metrics. In Maximo Application Suite Select, identifying the symptom and tracing it to the underlying configuration allows administrators to correct existing records and prevent recurring errors. Looking to verify data integrity right away? Skip to data quality verification checklist ↓ 💡 Tips for success ¤ Check for duplicate asset records before modifying maintenance history. Duplicates frequently occur when identical machines are imported twice with slightly different naming conventions. Verify parent location links when assets do not appear in hierarchy drill-downs. An operating location without a parent is treated as an isolated top-level site record. Reconcile physical inventory with Count Books when stock balances show negative numbers. Issuing parts before recording purchase receipts creates temporary negative balance discrepancies. Establish standardized classification attributes so that all assets in the same category display consistent technical specifications. Diagnosing common data anomalies ¤ Review this diagnostic guide to match your observed symptom with its root cause and corrective action. Table 1: Common data quality symptoms and corrective actions ¤ Observed symptom Primary root cause Where to investigate Corrective action Asset count is doubled or inflated Duplicate asset records created during manual entry or CSV imports Assets Decommission or merge duplicate asset records, redirecting work history to the primary asset Asset missing from location hierarchy Location record has no parent location specified Location Open the location record and populate the Parent Location field Inventory balance is negative Parts were issued from the storeroom before receipt transactions were processed Inventory Perform a physical count in Count Books and adjust the balance to match physical reality Technical attributes are missing on asset Asset is not linked to a classification structure Classifications Assign the correct classification class to the asset on the Specifications tab Work order shows zero labor cost Assigned labor record has no craft hourly rate defined Labor Open the Labor record and define standard hourly billing rates for the craft Fixing orphan locations and broken hierarchies ¤ When a technician or supervisor cannot locate equipment in the hierarchy tree, the location record is usually missing its parent link. How to reconnect an orphan location ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Location and open it. Search for the affected location , such as Packaging zone . In the Location details view, check the Parent field. If the field is empty, click the detail menu next to Parent and select the parent area, such as Production building . Open the Location Hierarchy tab to verify that the location now sits under the correct plant building. Click Save Location . Resolving duplicate asset records ¤ Duplicate assets distort maintenance histories by splitting work orders and costs across multiple records for the same physical machine. How to remediate duplicate assets ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Assets and open it. Filter by asset description or serial number to identify the duplicate records, such as MTR-101 and MTR-DRIVE-01 . Determine which record holds the primary maintenance history and active preventive maintenance schedule. For the redundant duplicate record: Check for open work orders on the Work tab and reassign them to the primary asset . Update the status of the redundant asset to DECOMMISSIONED or INACTIVE . Add a cross-reference note in the long description directing users to the primary asset ID. Click Save Asset . Correcting inventory balance discrepancies ¤ Negative balances occur when emergency repairs consume parts faster than receiving paperwork is entered. How to reconcile stock balances ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Inventory and open it. Find the item in the target storeroom, such as Main storeroom . In the Inventory Balances table, enter the actual physical count verified on the shelf. Compare the Current Balance with the Physical Count . Save the record, then check that the Reconciled? checkbox is selected on the balance row. Real-world example: Resolving data errors at the ice cream plant ¤ Consider how the system administrator corrected data anomalies affecting the cold storage room and filler FL-02 drive motor. Scenario: Broken reporting metrics ¤ Symptom 1: The supervisor reported that the cold storage room did not appear on the plant hierarchy navigation card. Fix: The administrator opened the Location application, found Cold storage room , and added Ice cream main plant into the Parent field. The room immediately appeared in the site drilldown. Symptom 2: The motor for filler FL-02 showed zero historical maintenance costs despite multiple recent repairs. Fix: The administrator opened the Labor application and found that the mechanical technician labor record lacked an hourly rate on craft MECH-01 . Adding the standard rate immediately corrected labor cost calculations on all future work orders . Data quality verification checklist ¤ Use this checklist to maintain high data accuracy across assets , locations , and inventory . Table 2: Data quality verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Hierarchy completeness Every operating room and zone has a valid parent location linking to the main site [ ] No duplicate serials Asset serial numbers are unique across operating equipment records [ ] Positive inventory Storeroom balances show zero or positive quantities across all active bins [ ] Labor rates defined Every active Labor record has an associated craft hourly rate configured [ ] Classifications applied Operating production assets have technical specifications populated Continue building your skills ¤ Establish permanent data governance ¤ Preventing data quality issues before they start is easier than fixing broken records. Learn how to standardize dropdown values and enforce data entry rules. How do I make data reliable? Standardize dropdown lists and domains ¤ Customizing system domains ensures that technicians and clerks select consistent terminology during data entry. How do I customize dropdown values? docs.text: How do I make data reliable? ¤ Reliable data enables accurate maintenance forecasting, automated work order generation, and dependable inventory planning. When data entries contain typos, inconsistent naming conventions, or missing attributes, reports produce misleading results and scheduled maintenance fails to trigger. To make operational data reliable across your organization, replace free text entry with controlled vocabularies, enforce mandatory fields, structure asset classifications, and conduct routine data health audits. Looking to verify data reliability right away? Skip to data reliability checklist ↓ Core principles of reliable data ¤ Reliable maintenance data rests on four structural pillars: Controlled vocabularies: Restrict data entry to defined picklists using the Domains application instead of free-form text fields. Standardized hierarchies: Organize assets , locations , and failure records into structured parent and child relationships. Consistent attribute capture: Apply classifications to categorize equipment specifications, such as motor horsepower or refrigeration refrigerant types. Regular validation audits: Review data exceptions on a recurring schedule to catch orphaned records, duplicate entries, or missing rates before they impact reporting. Table 1: Data standardization mechanisms in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Standardization mechanism Application Operational purpose Example implementation ALN domains Domains Provides a fixed list of text values for selection fields Standard work order priority reasons or inspection condition grades Synonym domains Domains Extends internal system statuses with custom business sub-statuses Adding WAITING_PERMIT under internal status WAPPR Numeric and range domains Domains Enforces numeric validation and boundary limits Restricting allowable temperature entries between -30 and 50 degrees Celsius Classifications Classifications Applies uniform attribute templates across equipment families Requiring voltage, frame size, and RPM attributes on all drive motors Failure hierarchies Failure Codes Standardizes failure reporting across Problem, Cause, and Remedy tiers Linking mechanical seal leak failure paths to Filler FL-02 Replacing free text with Domains ¤ Free text entry is the primary cause of data degradation in maintenance management systems. When technicians and planners type freehand notes into categorisation fields, slight variations such as Pump Leak , PMP LK , and Leaking pump prevent automated reporting from aggregating failure history. ALN domains for standard picklists ¤ ALN alphanumeric domains present users with a controlled drop-down list. By attaching ALN domains to user-defined fields, you eliminate spelling discrepancies and enable precise filtering. Creating an ALN domain in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Domains and open it. Click Add New Domain and select Add New ALN Domain . In the Domain field, enter a unique identifier, such as IC_FAIL_REASON . In the Description field, enter a descriptive title, such as Ice Cream Plant Failure Reason Codes . In the ALN Values table, click New Row to add each allowable option: In the Value field, enter the code, such as BEARING_WEAR . In the Description field, enter the full label, such as Mechanical bearing wear or fatigue . Repeat step 5 for all required values. Click OK , then click Save . Synonym domains for status workflows ¤ Synonym domains allow organizations to define business-specific terms that map directly to core system statuses. The internal system logic operates on the base status , while users interact with the familiar synonym value. For example, if the Ice Cream plant requires a specific sub-state for work orders awaiting food safety sign-off before work starts, add a synonym value WFOODSAFE mapped to the system base status Waiting on Approval, WAPPR . Figure 1: Synonym domain mapping to system base status As shown in Figure 1, the core system base status WAPPR branches into multiple user-facing display statuses: Standard Base Status : Waiting on Approval, WAPPR , for general maintenance work orders . Synonym Value WFOODSAFE : Waiting on Food Safety Sign-off for hygiene and sanitation hold points. Synonym Value WENVPERMIT : Waiting on Environmental Permit for environmental compliance hold points. 💡 Tip: Keep domain lists concise and mutually exclusive ¤ Do not overload domains with dozens of overlapping choices. If a picklist exceeds fifteen options, users often pick the first available entry rather than scrolling to find the correct code. Review domain lists quarterly and deactivate obsolete values. Enforcing standardized classifications ¤ Classifications ensure that all assets of the same type store identical technical specifications. Without classifications, one technician records motor power in kilowatts in the description field, while another records horsepower in the remarks section. In the Classifications application, build an equipment hierarchy: Figure 2: Hierarchical asset classification and specification structure As shown in Figure 2, asset classifications organize specifications down a four-level hierarchy: Level 1 ( PRODUCTION ) : Encompasses all plant machinery. Level 2 ( ROTATING ) : Groups dynamic equipment families. Level 3 ( MOTORS ) : Defines electric drive units. Level 4 (Attributes) : Captures standardized technical specifications, including Horsepower or Kilowatts, Voltage or Phase, NEMA Frame, Rated RPM, and Bearing Type. When you classify the drive motor for Filler FL-02 under MOTORS , Maximo Application Suite Select prompts for each defined attribute. This structured capture enables engineers to search for all 50 HP motors across the Ice Cream Main Plant when planning standardized spares. Establishing a data governance cadence ¤ Data quality is not a one-time cleanup project; it requires regular monitoring. Establish a tiered audit cadence to catch anomalies early. Table 2: Recommended data governance schedule ¤ Frequency Responsible role Focus area Action required Daily Maintenance Supervisor Open Work Orders Review newly created work orders to ensure asset , location , and work type fields are populated correctly Weekly Inventory Clerk Storeroom Balances Reconcile negative balances and investigate unrecorded material receipts Monthly Reliability Engineer Failure Reporting & PM Compliance Identify work orders closed without failure codes or completed with unlinked assets Quarterly System Administrator Domains & Classifications Audit unused domain values, archive obsolete codes, and review orphan location records Data reliability checklist ¤ Use this checklist to verify that data standards are active across your plant. Table 3: Data reliability verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Mandatory failure codes Work types requiring failure tracking cannot be completed without Problem, Cause, and Remedy selection [ ] Controlled picklists Key operational fields use ALN or Synonym domains rather than free text entry [ ] Asset classification coverage All critical production assets have an assigned classification and populated specification attributes [ ] Active meter associations Rotating assets requiring usage-based maintenance have active continuous or gauge meters linked [ ] Location hierarchy integrity All child locations connect to valid parent locations with no orphan records [ ] Craft and labor rates Every active craft has standard loaded labor billing rates configured Related topics ¤ How do I fix data that looks wrong? docs.text: How do I improve completion rates? ¤ A low work order completion rate is a warning signal that operational friction is slowing down your maintenance team. When work orders linger for weeks in unapproved, waiting, or in progress statuses, the maintenance backlog inflates, overdue counts rise, and critical preventive maintenance gets missed. Improving completion rates requires identifying and eliminating the specific bottlenecks that prevent technicians from finishing jobs on time. In Maximo Application Suite Select, this means aligning material readiness, craft qualifications, job plan clarity, and status lifecycle discipline. Looking to verify completion workflows right away? Skip to work order completion checklist ↓ 💡 Tips for success ¤ Review work orders in Waiting on Material status daily. A work order should not be approved or scheduled until all required parts are verified in stock. Match work orders to technician crafts before assigning. Assigning an electrical repair to a general mechanic leads to delays, rework, and incomplete tasks. Attach standardized job plans to recurring work. Work orders with defined step-by-step tasks and estimated hours are completed 40% faster than vague single-line requests. Train technicians to complete work orders on mobile devices before leaving the job site . Delaying data entry until the end of the week creates administrative backlogs and inaccurate actual labor hours. The four major completion blockers ¤ When work orders stall, the cause usually falls into one of four operational categories. Table 1: Common completion blockers and solutions ¤ Blocker System symptom Operational root cause Remediation strategy Material availability Work order stuck in WMATL status Required spare parts are out of stock or not reserved in advance Use the Storerooms application to check balances and reserve parts before approving work Craft mismatch Long duration in INPRG status Technician lacks the specialized certification or tools for the task Check craft and skill requirements in Labor and match assignments accordingly Unclear scope Task marked incomplete or rejected Work order description lacks specific instructions or safety procedures Attach a standardized Job Plan with documented task steps and safety requirements Approval delay Accumulation of WAPPR records Supervisors lack a consolidated daily review routine Use the Work queues card on the supervisor Operational Dashboard to approve work in batches Managing the work order lifecycle ¤ Maintaining disciplined status progression prevents work orders from getting lost between shifts or departments. Table 2: Standard work order status lifecycle ¤ Status Code Meaning Who manages it Waiting on Approval WAPPR Work order created; pending review and resource verification Supervisor Approved APPR Work order approved; ready for scheduling and resource allocation Supervisor Waiting on Material WMATL Work approved but waiting for required inventory parts Inventory Clerk Waiting on Plant Condition WPCOND Work approved but requires equipment shutdown or line clearance Supervisor In Progress INPRG Technician is actively performing the physical work Technician Completed COMP Physical work finished; actual hours, materials, and notes recorded Technician Closed CLOSE Financial and operational review completed; record locked Administrator Pre-job staging: Eliminating parts delays ¤ The single largest cause of stalled work orders in manufacturing and facilities operations is the lack of replacement parts when the technician arrives at the asset . How to verify and reserve parts before work begins ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Work Orders and open it. Open the planned work order and open the Plans tab. Open the Materials subtab and verify that required parts and quantities are listed. Review the Direct Issue and Line Status indicators. If items show insufficient stock, update the status to WMATL and notify the inventory clerk. Once the inventory clerk confirms stock availability in the storeroom, update the status to APPR for assignment. Real-world example: Clearing stalled work on the filling line ¤ Consider how the maintenance supervisor at the ice cream main plant cleared a backlog of overdue work orders on filling line filler FL-02. Scenario: Stalled preventive maintenance ¤ The Problem: Three consecutive monthly PM work orders for filler FL-02 remained in INPRG for over four weeks. The overall plant completion rate had dropped to 62%. Diagnosis: The supervisor opened Operational Dashboard : Supervisor and reviewed the work orders . Two work orders were stalled because the sanitization seal kit was on backorder ( WMATL ). The third was stalled because the assigned technician was an apprentice mechanic who needed a certified electrician to complete the motor drive calibration task. Corrective Action: The supervisor reconfigured the job plan for filler FL-02 into two separate tasks: Task 10 for mechanical seal replacement, and Task 20 for electrical motor calibration. The supervisor worked with the inventory clerk to establish a dedicated kit item in Item Master for filler FL-02 monthly maintenance. The supervisor updated shift assignments so that mechanical and electrical tasks were assigned to the appropriate crafts simultaneously during the planned Tuesday sanitation shutdown. The Outcome: The backlog was cleared in a single shift, and monthly PM completion rates on the packaging line rose to 94%. Daily supervisor completion routine ¤ Supervisors who follow a consistent 15-minute daily triage routine maintain significantly higher completion rates across their teams. Table 3: Daily completion triage workflow ¤ Time Action Application Focus Shift start (10 min) Review WAPPR and WMATL queues Operational Dashboard Approve verified work and allocate to technicians based on craft availability Mid-shift (5 min) Check long-running INPRG records Work Orders Identify technicians who encounter unexpected blockers or scope changes Shift end (10 min) Review COMP work orders Work Orders Verify actual labor hours, materials used, and failure codes before closing Work order completion checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure that your organization maintains high work order completion rates. Table 4: Work order completion verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Daily queue review Supervisor checks the WAPPR work queue on the dashboard at the start of every shift [ ] Materials confirmed No work order is released to INPRG without confirmed parts availability in Storerooms [ ] Craft alignment Assigned labor craft matches the skill requirements listed on the job plan [ ] Mobile completion Technicians log labor actuals, materials used, and failure codes directly on mobile [ ] Status hygiene Work orders are advanced from COMP to CLOSE within standard accounting timeframes Continue building your skills ¤ Reduce unplanned asset downtime ¤ High completion rates on preventive maintenance directly reduce unscheduled breakdowns. Learn how to structure maintenance programs for maximum reliability. How do I reduce downtime ? Assign the correct people to work ¤ Ensure work orders are directed to technicians with the right skills, certifications, and shift availability. How do I assign the correct people? How do I schedule work? : Build balanced weekly schedules that prevent resource bottlenecks. How do I assign the correct people? : Configure crafts , crews , and calendars. docs.text: How do I reduce downtime ? ¤ Unplanned equipment downtime is one of the most costly disruptions in industrial and facilities operations. When critical machinery stops unexpectedly, production halts, maintenance costs surge, and emergency repairs replace planned work. Reducing downtime requires shifting your maintenance operation from reactive emergency response to proactive defect prevention. In Maximo Application Suite Select, this transformation rests on four core pillars: structured preventive maintenance , standardized failure reporting, condition monitoring, and critical spare parts availability. Looking to verify your downtime reduction program right away? Skip to downtime reduction checklist ↓ 💡 Tips for success ¤ Maintain a preventive maintenance compliance rate of 85% or higher. When PMs are deferred, equipment failure rates increase dramatically within 30 to 60 days. Implement structured failure codes with Problem, Cause, and Remedy levels. Without standardized failure data, reliability teams cannot identify repeat root causes. Report actual downtime hours on every corrective work order . Recording when the breakdown started and ended allows the system to calculate accurate Mean Time to Repair and Mean Time Between Failures. Ensure critical spare parts are linked directly to asset records on the Spare Parts tab. Technicians should never lose hours searching storerooms for routine wear components. The four pillars of downtime reduction ¤ World-class maintenance programs keep unplanned downtime below 10% of total operating hours. Maximo Application Suite Select supports this goal through four integrated capabilities. Table 1: Core capabilities for downtime reduction ¤ Capability What it does Operational impact Where configured Preventive Maintenance (PM) Generates recurring inspections and servicing before equipment degrades Prevents up to 70% of mechanical and electrical wear failures PM Condition Monitoring Triggers corrective work orders when meter readings breach action limits Detects impending failures days or weeks before catastrophic breakdown Condition Monitoring Failure Code Hierarchies Captures structured Problem, Cause, and Remedy data on work orders Reveals recurring defect trends across equipment classes Failure Codes Storeroom Reorder Points Automates reorder notifications when stock falls below safety levels Eliminates repair delays caused by missing replacement parts Storerooms Structuring failure codes to identify root causes ¤ When technicians record failure details in free-form notes, analyzing defect trends is difficult. Structured failure codes convert maintenance history into actionable reliability data. A failure hierarchy follows a three-level parent-child structure headed by a failure class: Failure Class: Identifies the broad asset type, such as PUMP or MOTOR . Problem: Describes the observed symptom, such as HIGH-TEMP or VIBRATION . Cause: Identifies why the problem occurred, such as BEARING-WEAR or LUBRICATION-LOSS . Remedy: Describes the corrective action taken, such as REPLACE-BEARING or GREASE-UNIT . Table 2: Example failure hierarchy for electric drive motors ¤ Level Code Description Operational meaning Failure class MTR-ELEC Electric Motor Top category assigned to all motor asset records Problem OVERHEAT Operating temperature above limit Observed symptom during production Cause FAN-BLOCK Cooling fan blocked with debris Root cause identified upon inspection Remedy CLEAN-FAN Cleaned fan cowl and housing Corrective action executed by technician Tracking asset downtime on work orders ¤ To measure whether downtime is decreasing, maintenance teams must record downtime accurately on corrective work orders . How to report downtime in the Work Orders application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Work Orders and open it. Open the completed corrective work order . Select Report Downtime from the common actions menu. Specify whether the downtime occurred during operational or non-operational production hours. In the Downtime Code field, select the reason code, such as BRKDWN for unscheduled breakdown. In the Start Date and End Date fields, enter the exact timestamps when the asset stopped and returned to service. Click OK to save the downtime record. Real-world example: Eliminating recurring downtime on Filler FL-02 ¤ Consider how the maintenance supervisor at the ice cream main plant used failure data to eliminate repeated stoppages on filling line filler FL-02. Scenario: Chronic packaging line stops ¤ The Problem: Filler FL-02 in the filling line room suffered four unscheduled stops over six weeks, totaling 18 hours of lost ice cream packaging time. Data Analysis: The supervisor reviewed KPI Viewer and filtered work orders by asset Filler FL-02 . The failure reporting tab showed that all four work orders shared the problem code JAM and cause code SEAL-LEAK . Root Cause: Product leakage from worn nozzle seals was contaminating the drive belt track, causing drive slip and safety stops. Corrective Action: The supervisor updated the preventive maintenance schedule for filler FL-02, changing the nozzle seal replacement interval from 90 days to 45 days. The supervisor set up a characteristic condition monitoring point to inspect seal integrity during weekly sanitization rounds. The inventory clerk increased the safety stock level for nozzle seal kits from 2 to 6 units in the main storeroom. The Outcome: Unscheduled downtime on filler FL-02 dropped to zero hours over the following quarter. Downtime reduction roadmap ¤ Follow this progressive roadmap to systematically reduce downtime across your facility. Table 3: Progressive steps to reduce equipment downtime ¤ Stage Focus area Key milestone Target metric Stage 1: Basic control Achieve 85%+ PM compliance All critical production assets have active PM schedules generated on time PM Compliance > 85% Stage 2: Failure tracking Enforce failure code entry Technicians select Problem, Cause, and Remedy on 100% of emergency work Failure Code Capture > 90% Stage 3: Parts alignment Secure critical spare parts All high-risk failure components have active reorder points in Storerooms Stock-Out Rate < 2% Stage 4: Early detection Implement condition monitoring Critical drives and compressors use gauge meters to detect early wear Reactive Work Ratio < 15% Downtime reduction checklist ¤ Use this checklist to confirm that your downtime reduction processes are operating effectively. Table 4: Downtime reduction verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] PM compliance tracking Supervisor Operational Dashboard displays monthly PM compliance above 85% [ ] Failure hierarchy assigned All operating production assets have a valid Failure Class on their record [ ] Mandatory failure reporting Technicians enter Problem, Cause, and Remedy before closing emergency work [ ] Downtime hours logged Downtime start and end timestamps are recorded on all unscheduled work orders [ ] Critical spares identified Critical wear components are listed on the Spare Parts tab of critical assets Continue building your skills ¤ Complete maintenance on schedule ¤ High work order completion rates ensure preventive maintenance is finished before breakdowns occur. Learn how to eliminate work order bottlenecks. How do I improve completion rates? Catch equipment defects early ¤ Condition monitoring detects temperature, vibration, and pressure anomalies before they turn into emergency downtime events. How do I detect issues early? What metrics matter? : Track MTBF, MTTR, and planned maintenance percentages. How do I plan recurring maintenance? : Configure effective PM schedules and routes. docs.text: What is Maximo Application Suite Select? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select is a ready-to-use Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution for tracking equipment, managing work, and keeping operations running smoothly. No installation. No configuration. No customization needed. Just log in and start working: Track assets Create and complete work orders Schedule preventive maintenance Manage parts inventory Monitor performance Who is this for? ¤ Technicians can find and complete work orders , for example, complete work on Filler FL-02. Supervisors can plan, assign, and track maintenance work, for example, assign preventive maintenance for Spiral freezer SF-01. Inventory clerks can manage parts and supplies, for example, issue parts from Main storeroom. Administrators can load data and set up users, for example, load users for Ice cream plant A. To see what you can do in your role, go to What can I do in my role? About these examples ¤ To make onboarding easier to follow, the examples in this help center use one consistent scenario: an ice-cream manufacturing operation. You'll see the same site , locations , assets , and work, so you can focus on how the workflow fits together. What problems does it solve? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select helps you move from reactive "run-to-fail" maintenance to organized, preventive maintenance : Stop losing track of work: all work orders in one system, not scattered across spreadsheets or paper Prevent equipment failures: schedule maintenance before problems happen Know what you have: track all your assets and their maintenance history Control parts inventory : see what's in stock and what's been used Make better decisions: use data to understand what's working and what needs attention Take your work mobile ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile lets technicians view assets , manage work orders , and update work from their phone or tablet, wherever work happens. To install the app and sign in, go to Get IBM Maximo Mobile . What to do next ¤ What can I do in my role? What are the basic concepts? docs.text: How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? ¤ Understanding how locations , assets , and work orders connect helps you work more efficiently in Maximo Application Suite Select. Example scenario ¤ Top-level location : Ice cream main plant Location : Filling Line 2 Asset : Filler FL-02 Work order : Inspect filler nozzles Type : Inspection Parts : Food-grade seal kit Figure 1: How a location, an asset, and a work order connect Locations , assets , and work orders each answer a different question. A location tells you where work happens. An asset tells you what equipment is maintained. A work order tells you what work was done. In this example, Filler FL-02 is installed at Filling Line 2 in Ice cream main plant. The work order Inspect filler nozzles records the maintenance done on that equipment, including the inspection work type and the food-grade seal kit parts used. The diagram also shows that both locations and assets can use parent-child hierarchies, which helps you organize work and track maintenance at the correct operational level. docs.text: How do inspections work? ¤ An inspection is a set of questions that you answer about an asset or a location . Inspections use two apps: Inspection Forms . Use it to define the forms that inspections use. Inspections . Use it to conduct inspections and record the results. To open either app, use the Find navigation item field and search for its name. Inspections is also in IBM Maximo Mobile, so you can inspect an asset or location where it is. The app has the same name on the desktop and in IBM Maximo Mobile. [SME confirmation required: Confirm that the inspection behavior in this topic applies to MAS Select. The source is the Maximo Manage documentation. Confirm that Inspection Forms and Inspections are the app names and locations in Select.] How inspections fit together ¤ A form defines the questions for an inspection. When the form is activated, an inspection appears in the Inspections app. An inspector answers the questions and completes the inspection. The results are saved with the asset or location that was inspected. [SME confirmation required: Confirm how inspections are scheduled or generated from a form in Select, and where the results appear for the asset or location.] What you can do in Inspections ¤ Filter your inspections by pending, in progress, and completed. Conduct several inspections at the same time, as a batch. Create an unscheduled inspection when you find something that is not on your schedule, including for several assets or locations at once. Show only the required questions, or only the questions that you have not answered. Review your answers in a summary before you complete the inspection. View the results of completed inspections. Attach photos to an inspection. Create follow-up work from an inspection. The app saves your answers automatically as you go. Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Inspection apps ¤ App Use it to Inspection Forms Define the forms that inspections use. Inspections Conduct inspections and review results. Who can use inspections? ¤ The apps you see depend on your security group . In general: Technicians complete inspections. Supervisors review inspection results. For the security groups , see How do I add users? What to do next ¤ Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? : See how Inspections relates to the other apps. docs.text: What keyboard shortcuts can I use? ¤ You can use keyboard shortcuts to work faster in Maximo Application Suite Select without switching between your keyboard and mouse. Everyday actions ¤ Use these shortcuts throughout the application for saving, navigating records, and changing status . Table 1: Keyboard shortcuts for everyday actions ¤ Action Keyboard shortcut Insert new record Ctrl+Alt+I Save record Ctrl+Alt+S Clear changes Ctrl+Alt+C Previous record Ctrl+Alt+P Next record Ctrl+Alt+N Change status Ctrl+Alt+A Put record in edit mode, or release record from edit mode Ctrl+Alt+L Navigating the page ¤ Use these shortcuts to move through fields, select controls, and get contextual help. Table 2: Keyboard shortcuts for page navigation ¤ Action Keyboard shortcut Move to the next field or control Tab Select a button, link, or menu option Enter Select or clear a check box Spacebar Show a description of the selected field Alt+F1 Mac users On a Mac, press Option+Fn+F1 to show a description of the selected field. Working in tables ¤ Use these shortcuts when you are entering data in a table, such as adding job plan tasks or labor assignments. Table 3: Keyboard shortcuts for tables ¤ Action Keyboard shortcut Move to the next row Ctrl+Down arrow Move to the previous row Ctrl+Up arrow Create a new row Enter Submit a value Tab Open or close the table filter Ctrl+Z Move to the next page Ctrl+Right arrow Move to the previous page Ctrl+Left arrow Working with dates ¤ Use these shortcuts when entering or adjusting dates in date fields. Table 4: Keyboard shortcuts for dates ¤ Action Keyboard shortcut Insert today's date Ctrl+Shift+7 Move forward one day Alt+Up arrow Move back one day Alt+Down arrow Move forward one month Ctrl+Shift+0 Move back one month Ctrl+Shift+9 Move forward one year Ctrl+Shift+Up arrow Move back one year Ctrl+Shift+Down arrow Global navigation ¤ Use these shortcuts to return from lookup windows. Table 5: Keyboard shortcuts for global navigation ¤ Action Keyboard shortcut Return Alt+R Return with value Alt+W Non-standard behaviour ¤ Two keyboard shortcuts behave differently in Maximo Application Suite Select from the standard browser expectation. docs.text: What apps are in IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile provides role-based applications on your mobile device or tablet. You can complete work orders , conduct inspections, manage storeroom inventory , approve work, review reported hours, and update asset and location records while in the field. The apps you see on your home screen depend on your role and the security groups assigned by your administrator. If an app you need is missing, contact your administrator. Note IBM Maximo Mobile is also used with IBM Maximo Manage. If you see references to Maximo Manage, you can ignore them. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Use the search bar or app tiles on your home screen to find the app you need. Work offline when you lose connectivity. Your updates save locally and sync automatically when your device reconnects. If an app is missing from your home screen, ask your administrator to verify your security group permissions. Work execution and supervisor apps ¤ Technician ¤ Use the Technician app to review and complete your assigned work orders . You can view work on a map, follow job plans , log labor , tools, and materials, report failure codes , attach photos, and record meter readings. To get started with completing work orders , see Technician: Complete your first work order . Inspections ¤ Use Inspections to complete inspection forms for assets and locations . You can answer required questions, record measurements, attach photos, and generate follow-up work orders . To learn more about how inspection forms and checklists operate, see How do inspections work? . Approvals ¤ Use Approvals to review, approve, and monitor work orders awaiting supervisor authorization. When notifications are enabled, you receive alerts on your device when a work order requires approval. To learn more about supervisor workflows, see Supervisor: Assign and track work . Service Requests ¤ Use Service Requests to report issues or log maintenance requests directly from your device, and to monitor the status of requests you submitted earlier. Inventory management apps ¤ Issues and Transfers ¤ Use Issues and Transfers to issue parts and tools to work orders , issue items without a reservation, and transfer stock between storerooms. To get started with issuing inventory , see Inventory clerk: Issue a part . Inventory Counting ¤ Use Inventory Counting to perform physical stock counts and cycle counts in storerooms using count books or ad hoc counts. To learn more about stock counts and count books, see What happens if stock is incorrect? . Material Request ¤ Use Material Request to request parts, tools, or services for a work order from the field, and to track previous requests. People and team apps ¤ Timesheet ¤ Use Timesheet to review your personal reported labor transactions. You can check labor entries recorded for today or earlier, including the associated work order , asset , location , and total hours. Crew Manager ¤ Use Crew Manager to manage work orders assigned to a crew . A crew leader or supervisor can start and stop timers for the entire crew , recording labor for all active crew members simultaneously. To set up crews , see How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? . Asset and location management apps ¤ Locations ¤ Use Locations to view, create, and update location records in the field. You can navigate location hierarchies, view locations on a map, and record location meter readings. To learn more about location structures, see How do I plan my location hierarchy? . Assets ¤ Use Assets , also known as Asset Manager, to look up equipment details, specifications, and meter readings, view asset locations on maps, and register new assets found in the field. To learn more about asset structures, see How do I plan my asset hierarchy? . Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Apps in IBM Maximo Mobile ¤ App Primary use Technician View and complete assigned work orders , report labor , materials, tools, and record meter readings. Inspections Conduct scheduled and unscheduled inspections, complete checklists, and log results. Approvals Review and approve work orders requiring supervisor sign-off. Service Requests Create service requests to report issues and track request status . Issues and Transfers Issue reserved or non-reserved parts to work orders and transfer items between storerooms. Inventory Counting Perform physical stock counts and cycle counts. Material Request Request parts, tools, or services for a work order from the field. Timesheet Review reported labor entries and hours. Crew Manager Track work and log collective labor hours for crew -assigned work orders . Locations Review location hierarchies, update location records, and log location meters . Assets Search equipment, view specifications and meters , and register new assets . To find an app on the desktop, use the Find navigation item field at the top of the menu and search for the app name. To return to the desktop applications after you open one of these apps on your computer, see How do I get back to the desktop applications? What to do next ¤ How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? : Install the app and sign in. What happens when I'm offline in IBM Maximo Mobile? : Learn how the apps operate without a network connection. Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? : Understand the relationship between mobile apps and desktop applications. How do I add users? : Assign the security groups that control app access. Related topics ¤ What is an asset ? What is a location ? What is a work order ?

docs.text: What happens when I'm offline in IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile keeps working when your device loses its connection. The app stores your data on the device, so you can keep working and sync your changes later. How online and offline work ¤ Online: The app is connected to the server. It saves the data it retrieves to your device and keeps that data in sync with the server. You can also sync manually. Offline: The app is not connected to the server. It uses the data that is stored on your device. When the connection returns, the app syncs your changes automatically. When is my device offline? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile treats your device as offline when any of these conditions apply: The device is in airplane mode. The network adapter of the device is turned off. The network bandwidth is low. The server cannot be reached from the device. Your sign-in session has expired. Signing in and staying signed in ¤ First sign-in: You need a network connection the first time you sign in. You use the same credentials that you use on the desktop. The app then creates a local data store on your device. Opening the app: Each time you open the app, it asks for your device's security credentials before it opens your local data. Session expiry: After your session expires, the app asks you to sign in again. If you do not sign in, you work offline until you do. By default, access expires after 30 minutes and the session can be renewed for up to 12 hours. Signing in again: To sign in at any time, select the cloud icon on the app screen. Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Online and offline ¤ Online Offline Data source The server and the data stored on your device The data stored on your device Syncing Automatic. You can also sync manually. Automatic when the connection returns What to do next ¤ How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? : Download the app and sign in. How do I complete a work order ? : See what you can do offline while you complete work. Related topics ¤ Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? How do I find my work? docs.text: Qu'est-ce qu'un actif ? ¤ Un actif est tout équipement, toute machine ou toute infrastructure que votre organisation entretient. Les actifs sont les éléments physiques sur lesquels vous travaillez. Exemples d'actifs ¤ Équipements de production : Batch Mixer MX-01, Filler FL-02, Conveyor CV-02, Spiral Freezer SF-01 Équipements de procédé : pompes, moteurs, compresseurs, échangeurs de chaleur, refroidisseurs Installations : systèmes de chauffage, ventilation et climatisation, unités de réfrigération, systèmes d'éclairage Véhicules : camions, chariots élévateurs, transpalettes Stockage : cuves, silos, chambres froides Pourquoi les actifs sont importants ¤ Suivre l'historique de maintenance de chaque équipement Planifier la maintenance préventive Surveiller l'état et les performances des actifs Planifier les remplacements et les mises à niveau Calculer le coût total de possession Hiérarchie des actifs ¤ Figure 1 : exemple de hiérarchie des actifs pour un fabricant de crèmes glacées Un actif est un équipement physique que vous entretenez. Vous pouvez organiser les actifs selon une hiérarchie parent-enfant afin de montrer comment les équipements sont reliés et de suivre la maintenance au bon niveau. Dans la figure 1, Batch Mixer MX-01, Filler FL-02, Conveyor CV-02 et Spiral Freezer SF-01 sont des actifs parents. Les actifs parents peuvent inclure des actifs enfants. Par exemple, Batch Mixer MX-01 comprend l'Agitator motor et le Seal. Les actifs sont installés dans des emplacements, qui indiquent où l'équipement fonctionne. L'utilisation de hiérarchies d'actifs présente de nombreux avantages : Comprendre comment les équipements sont reliés Suivre la maintenance d'un système complet ou d'un composant précis Voir à la fois ce qu'est l'équipement et où il est installé Vous souhaitez voir comment cela s'articule avec les emplacements et les ordres de travail ? Consultez Comment les emplacements, les actifs et les ordres de travail fonctionnent-ils ensemble ? Nommer les actifs ¤ ✓ À faire Utilisez un numéro d'actif alphanumérique court Rédigez une description claire et précise Utilisez un format de description cohérent Identifiez l'actif parent lorsque c'est pertinent ✗ À éviter N'utilisez pas de descriptions vagues telles que PUMP Ne surchargez pas le numéro d'actif avec trop de détails Exemples d'actifs : Batch Mixer MX-01, Filler FL-02, Conveyor CV-02, Spiral Freezer SF-01. Exemples de descriptions : Filler FL-02, poste de remplissage de cornets ; Batch Mixer MX-01, préparation du mélange vanille. Rubriques connexes ¤ Quels sont les concepts de base ? Qu'est-ce qu'un ordre de travail ? Qu'est-ce qu'un emplacement ? Comment les emplacements, les actifs et les ordres de travail fonctionnent-ils ensemble ? Comment suivre l'historique d'un actif ?

docs.text: What is a location ? ¤ A location is a physical place where work is performed or assets are installed. Locations help you organize and find equipment. Types of locations ¤ Operating locations : Where assets are installed and running Storerooms : Where parts and materials are kept Service locations : Customer sites or service areas Staging areas : Temporary locations for work preparation Why locations matter ¤ Find equipment quickly Organize maintenance by area Assign work by location Track costs by facility or department Plan work routes efficiently Manage access and safety Location hierarchy ¤ Figure 1: Sample location hierarchy for an ice cream manufacturer A location is a place where work happens or where assets are installed. You can organize locations in a parent-child hierarchy to show how areas in a facility connect and to track work in the correct place. In Figure 1, the top-level location is Ice cream main plant, which branches into three main areas: Production building : A parent location containing child locations Mixing room, Filling line room, and Packaging zone. Cold storage : A dedicated refrigerated facility directly under Ice cream main plant. Main storeroom : The primary parts inventory warehouse directly under Ice cream main plant. Want to see how this connects to assets and work orders ? See How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? To plan your own hierarchy, see How do I plan my location hierarchy? Naming locations ¤ ✓ Do Use a unique location identifier Name locations so they make sense in the hierarchy Use location names for places, not equipment ✗ Don't Don't use the location name to represent the asset Don't mix place names and equipment names at the same hierarchy level without a clear reason Example names : Ice Cream Plant A, Production Building, Mixing Room, Filling Line 2, Packaging Zone, Cold Storage, Main Storeroom. Location vs. asset ¤ Location : The place, such as Filling Line 2 Asset : The equipment, such as Filler FL-02 Relationship : Asset is installed at location Some work orders are for locations , such as Clean production floor, rather than specific assets . Locations vs service addresses ¤ Locations and service addresses work together but serve different purposes. A location represents an operational place. A service address provides the physical or geographic details needed to find it. Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Location terminology ¤ Term What it is Location An operational place where assets are used, stored, or repaired Service address The physical or geographic details needed to find that place or its associated assets Table 2: Detailed comparison of locations vs service addresses ¤ Aspect Location Service address Primary purpose Represents a place where assets are operated, stored, or repaired Provides detailed physical or geographic information that helps people find an asset or location Role in the data model Supports asset tracking, work management, purchasing, and the history of asset movements and performance at particular sites Provides another way to search for assets and locations and helps direct field crews to where work must be performed Structure Can belong to one or more location systems, which organize locations into logical parent-child hierarchies. See Can I organize the same locations more than one way? Can participate in an address system that establishes address ancestry and determines how addresses apply to child records Information stored Can include location type, status , associated assets , parent and child locations , and an associated service address Can include an address code, street information, coordinates, directions, landmarks, and other detailed location information Relationship to assets Assets can be installed at or associated with the location One service address can represent the position of one or more assets or physical locations Use on work records A location can identify where work is associated operationally When work is created for an asset or location , its service address can be copied to the service request or work order Example ¤ Consider an ice-cream manufacturing plant: Location : Packaging Line 2 : This record represents the operational place where equipment is installed and work is managed. It might be a child of the Packaging Area in the primary location hierarchy. Service address: Building B, south entrance, second floor, coordinates X/Y : This record provides the physical details that help a technician find Packaging Line 2. The service address does not replace the location . It supplements the location with address, navigation, or geographic information. How they work together ¤ A location can have an associated service address. You can add service addresses to assets , locations , work orders , and service requests. When work is created for an asset or location , the service address can be copied to the work order or service request. If an asset or location does not have its own service address, the system can use the address of the closest ancestor in the address hierarchy. A service address provides an additional way to find individual assets and locations , or groups of them. Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is an asset ? What is a work order ? How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? How do I decide: location , asset , or spare part? How do I plan my location hierarchy?

docs.text: What is a work order ? ¤ A work order is a request or instruction to perform maintenance work. It's the central document that tracks everything about a maintenance job. Types of work orders ¤ Corrective maintenance : Fix something that broke Preventive maintenance : Scheduled routine maintenance Predictive maintenance : Work based on condition monitoring Project work : Installations, upgrades, modifications Inspections : Regular checks and assessments Why work orders matter ¤ Assign work to the correct people Track what work was done Record labor hours and costs Document parts used Maintain history of all maintenance Measure performance and productivity Work order lifecycle ¤ A work order progresses through six sequential stages from initial creation to final historical closeout: Created : The requester or the system creates the work order . It captures what needs to be done, where the work happens, how urgent it is, and any instructions the technician needs later. Approved : A supervisor reviews and approves the work. Approval confirms that the job can move ahead, reserves planned items , and records planned cost and rate information. Assigned : A supervisor or planner assigns the work to a technician. Before work starts, the planner checks that the assigned person has the schedule, instructions, parts, and tools needed. In Progress : The technician starts the job and records updates. Labor , materials, services, and tools are recorded as physical work happens so the record stays accurate. Completed : The technician documents labor , parts, and notes upon finishing the physical work. The record can still undergo final review or closeout. Closed : A supervisor or planner reviews completion and closes the work order . Closing finalizes the record, removes unused item reservations, and archives the job into maintenance history. Figure 1: The lifecycle of a work order in Maximo Application Suite Select A work order records maintenance work. It tells you what needs to be done, where the work happens, and which asset the work applies to. In this example, the work order Inspect filler nozzles is linked to Filler FL-02 at Filling Line 2. It also shows the work type and the parts used. This helps you track maintenance clearly and keep a useful history of the work performed. Want to see how this connects to locations and assets ? See How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? Creating a work order ¤ You create a work order when work needs to be done. Start with a clear description of the work. Then add details such as the work type, the priority, and the asset and location . For example, you might create a work order for Inspect filler nozzles and link it to Filler FL-02. Technicians can also create a work order from the field with the add button in the Technician app, for example when they find a problem on site . [SME confirmation required: Confirm the details you can add when you create a work order in Select.] Naming work orders ¤ ✓ Do Let Maximo Application Suite Select create the work order number automatically Write the description as a clear, action-oriented summary ✗ Don't Don't use vague descriptions such as Broken or Need fix Don't treat the description and work type as the same thing Example names : Inspect filler nozzles; Replace seal on Batch Mixer MX-01; Quarterly inspection, Spiral Freezer SF-01. Work order vs. work request ¤ Work request : Someone reports a problem or need Work order : Approved request with assigned resources Not all requests become work orders . Some may be rejected, combined, or deferred. Ready to work with work orders ? See How do I complete a job? for step-by-step guidance.

docs.text: Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? ¤ You can work with work orders in three places: The Work Orders application. The Technician app on the desktop, in your web browser. The Technician app in IBM Maximo Mobile, on your phone or tablet. All three work with the same work orders . This happens because Maximo Application Suite Select includes two kinds of apps: Desktop applications , such as Work Orders, Assets , and Inventory . These are the full applications that match the rest of the interface. Mobile apps , such as Technician, Inspections, and Asset Manager. Each is one application with two versions: a web version that runs in your browser next to the desktop applications, and a mobile version that runs in IBM Maximo Mobile on your phone or tablet. The two versions work the same way. Only the mobile version works offline. The two kinds of apps do not match one for one. For example, Technician combines parts of several desktop applications into one app for completing work. Most of the menu is desktop applications. To tell the two kinds apart, look at the name in the menu: The web version of a mobile app has a label in parentheses after its name, such as Timesheet (Mobile) or My Schedule (Mobile) . In a narrow menu, the label is cut off, as in Inventory Counting (M... . A desktop application has no label, such as Work Orders or Count Books . Some mobile apps are grouped under a name such as Technician or Asset Manager. The group has no label, but the apps inside it do. Which one should I use? ¤ There is no fixed rule. Use the one that suits how you work: If you use IBM Maximo Mobile often, use the web version of apps such as Technician on the desktop too. The app works the same way in both places. If you rarely use IBM Maximo Mobile, you might prefer desktop applications such as Work Orders. They are more consistent with the rest of the interface. How do I get back to the desktop applications? ¤ The web version of a mobile app, such as Technician or Inspections, opens without the desktop menu. To go back to the desktop applications, select the application menu icon at the bottom right of the screen, then select Start Center or Operational Dashboard in the navigator. Quick reference ¤ Table 1: Mobile apps and what they do ¤ App Use it to Technician Complete assigned work. Inspections Complete inspections. Inspection Forms Work with inspection forms. Asset Manager Look up and manage assets . Issues and Transfers Issue and transfer inventory . Inventory Counting Count inventory . Service Requests Create and track service requests. To find any app, use the Find navigation item field at the top of the menu and search for the app name. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the purpose of each app in the "Use it to" column.] Which apps can I see? ¤ The apps you see depend on the security group that your administrator assigned to you. For the security groups , see How do I add users? Note Technician is both a security group and an app. The Technician security group is a role that you assign to a user. The Technician app is one of the apps that role can use. What to do next ¤ Technician: Complete your first work order : Complete a work order . How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? : Get the app that contains Technician, Inspections, and the other apps in Table 1. How do I add users? : Assign the security group that gives a user access to apps. What apps are in IBM Maximo Mobile? : Overview of all the apps in IBM Maximo Mobile. Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is a work order ? What can I do in my role?

docs.text: Why do some terms differ from what I'm used to? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select uses a consistent set of terms to describe assets , locations , work, and inventory . These might differ from the terms you use today or in other systems. If you're not sure what a term means, click any underlined term in this help center to see its definition and related terms. This list brings those definitions and common alternatives together in one place. Assets and equipment ¤ Asset ¤ Any piece of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure that your organization maintains. You might know this as: equipment, machine, or unit Want to know more? What is an asset ? · How do I classify assets ? · How do I track asset history? Work and maintenance ¤ Work order ¤ A request or instruction to perform maintenance work. It records what needs to be done, where, who did it, what parts were used, and how long it took. This record stays with the asset as part of its maintenance history. You might know this as: maintenance order, job, ticket , or work request Want to know more? What is a work order ? · How do I complete a work order ? Plan tab ¤ The Plan section of a work order is where you record what is expected before work starts: the tasks to perform, materials to request, and labor needed. When actual work happens, those details are recorded separately in the Actuals section. Comparing plan to actuals lets you see whether jobs came in on time and on budget. You might know this as: planned work, work plan, or expected materials Work log ¤ A record of notes and updates added directly inside a work order . Use the work log to describe what you found, what you did, and anything else the next person needs to know. Entries are time-stamped and show who wrote them. You might know this as: job notes, maintenance notes, or technician notes Communications log ¤ A record of emails, notifications, and messages sent or received in connection with a work order . The communications log captures the conversation around the work, such as approval requests, status updates, and alerts. It is separate from the work log, which is for internal notes. You might know this as: message history, notification log, or email log Preventive maintenance ¤ Scheduled routine maintenance performed to prevent equipment failures. You might know this as: maintenance plan, planned maintenance, or PM Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance? Corrective maintenance ¤ Maintenance performed to fix equipment that has broken down. You might know this as: breakdown maintenance, repair work, or reactive maintenance Want to know more? How do I decide what work should be done? · What happens when an asset fails? Job plan ¤ A template that defines standard tasks, materials, and labor for recurring maintenance work. You might know this as: standard job, task template, or maintenance procedure Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance? Status ¤ The lifecycle state of a work order or record. You might know this as: lifecycle state, order state, or workflow stage Want to know more? How do I complete a work order ? Locations and sites ¤ Location ¤ A functional location or operating area where assets are installed or work is performed. You might know this as: functional location , area, or site area Want to know more? What is a location ? Site ¤ A data partitioning concept that represents a plant, facility, or business unit. You might know this as: plant, facility, or business unit Want to know more? What are the basic concepts? People, roles, and access ¤ Person and role ¤ A person record holds an individual's contact details and is used across the system to identify who owns, supervises, or reports on work. A role, also called a security group , determines what applications and actions that person can access. When you add a user, you assign them to a security group . The security group defines the role. The person record and the user account are separate, though they are linked. You might know this as: user type, access level, or permission group Want to know more? How do I add users? · How do I assign the correct people? Security group ¤ A collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. You might know this as: permission group, access group, user group, or role Want to know more? How do I add users? Authorized users ¤ The number of authorized users defines how many people are entitled to access the product under your subscription. When you add a new user account, it counts against this limit. If you reach the limit, you cannot add more users until entitlement is increased. Contact your IBM account representative to adjust your authorized user count. You might know this as: licensed users, named users, or seat count People and skills ¤ Labor ¤ Work time and effort assigned to a work order . You might know this as: technician time, work hours, or crew time Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Craft ¤ A trade or skill type required for maintenance work. You might know this as: trade, skill type, or discipline Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people? Inventory and materials ¤ Inventory ¤ Materials and spare parts stored for maintenance work. You might know this as: stock, stores, or warehouse Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job? Item and material ¤ An item is the master record for a part or material in the catalog, such as a filter or a seal. Material is the same thing in the context of a work order : materials are items requested or used for a specific job. The word changes depending on where you are in the system, but they refer to the same physical thing. You might know this as: spare part, stock item , or consumable Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job? Material request, reservation, and issue ¤ These three terms describe the sequence of getting parts to a job: Material request : You ask for the parts, tools, or services that a job needs. A request can be linked to a work order or made without one. Reservation : When materials are specified on an approved work order or task, the system can reserve the items in the storeroom automatically. A submitted material request can also create a reservation. A reservation holds the stock so it is not allocated to another job before yours. Issue : When you physically take the parts and use them, you issue them against the work order . This deducts the quantity from inventory and records the cost. You might know this as: pick list, parts request, stock allocation, or materials withdrawal Rotating item ¤ A repairable spare part that can be tracked individually by serial number. You might know this as: repairable spare, rotable, or serialized spare Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? Tracking and monitoring ¤ Meter ¤ A counter that tracks equipment usage, such as hours, cycles, or miles. You might know this as: counter, runtime meter , or odometer Want to know more? How do I detect issues early? Failure code ¤ A standardized code used to categorize and track equipment failures. You might know this as: failure classification, breakdown code, or fault code Want to know more? What happens when an asset fails? Downtime ¤ The period when equipment is not operational or available for use. You might know this as: outage, production loss, or equipment unavailable Want to know more? How do I reduce downtime ? · How do I detect issues early? Service requests ¤ Ticket ¤ A service request or incident report. You might know this as: service request, incident, or request Want to know more? What are the basic concepts? Configuration and data ¤ Object structure ¤ Defines the records and related fields that are available for importing, exporting, or exchanging data. You might know this as: data structure, import template, or record definition Want to know more? Which object structure do I use for each data type? · How do I get data into the system? Domain ¤ A list of valid values attached to a field that controls what users can select in a dropdown. You might know this as: value list, lookup list, or picklist Want to know more? How do I customize dropdown values? Communication template ¤ A reusable email template that can be triggered automatically by a workflow or escalation , or manually from a record. You might know this as: email template, notification template, or message template Want to know more? How do I automate communication? Escalation ¤ An automated rule that monitors the system for a condition and performs an action or sends a notification when that condition is met. You might know this as: alert rule, automated notification, or trigger Want to know more? How do I automate communication? · How do I act on alerts? People and teams ¤ Crew ¤ A named group of workers assembled to complete a job together, assigned as a team to a work order . You might know this as: work crew , team, or work gang Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people? Data sync ¤ The process of transferring record, lookup, and map data between the server and a mobile device. You might know this as: synchronization, offline sync, or data refresh Want to know more? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? User interface ¤ Default application ¤ The application that opens when a user logs in. Users can set their own default application in their profile preferences. Administrators can also set defaults for a security group . Choosing the correct default means users land on the most relevant application for their role without extra navigation. You might know this as: home screen, landing page, or startup application Start Workflow ¤ A workflow is an automated sequence of steps that routes a record through an approval or review process. "Start Workflow" is the action that begins this process for a specific record. Once started, the record follows a defined path, such as routing a work order to a supervisor for approval, and the system handles the routing automatically. You might know this as: submit for approval, begin approval process, or route for review Share with admin ¤ The "Share with admin" action sends a copy of information or a report to a system administrator. Administrators receive the information and can act on it, such as reviewing a configuration issue or adjusting access. The exact content and outcome depends on where in the system you use the action. You might know this as: send to admin, notify administrator, or escalate to admin API calls ¤ An API call is a request your system makes to Maximo Application Suite Select to exchange data automatically. For example, sending a new work order from an external system counts as one API call. Subscription plans include a defined number of API calls per period. If you integrate other systems with Maximo Application Suite Select, each data exchange uses some of this allowance. You might know this as: system integrations, data requests, or integration transactions Upgrade ¤ In Maximo Application Suite Select, Upgrade refers to moving to a higher subscription tier or adding capacity to your account. This gives you access to additional features, more users, or higher usage limits. You might know this as: subscription upgrade, plan upgrade, or adding capacity Basemap ¤ The background map layer that shows geography, streets, or satellite imagery. You might know this as: background map, base layer, or map tile Want to know more? How do I set up maps? Operational dashboard ¤ A landing page to monitor KPIs, manage upcoming assignments, complete tasks, or access related applications. You might know this as: command center, control panel, or operations console Want to know more? What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is an asset ? What is a work order ? What is a location ?

docs.text: Administrateur : ajouter des utilisateurs ¤ Démarrez rapidement avec une tâche conçue pour les administrateurs comme vous. Apprenez les notions de base tout en accomplissant quelque chose d'utile. Ajoutez un nouvel utilisateur au système et accordez-lui les accès appropriés, par exemple ajoutez des utilisateurs pour Ice cream plant A. 💡 Conseils pour réussir ¤ Utilisez des conventions de nommage cohérentes pour les ID utilisateur Appliquez le principe du moindre privilège, c'est-à-dire l'accès minimal nécessaire Gardez les affectations de groupes de sécurité organisées Marche à suivre ¤ Ajouter un utilisateur ¤ Ouvrez l'application Users. Cliquez sur Create user . Indiquez une adresse e-mail de connexion . Indiquez un ID utilisateur . Si vous le souhaitez, ajoutez une note dans le champ mémo . Exemple : accès temporaire pour un sous-traitant de l'usine de crèmes glacées A Indiquez un nom d'affichage . Il s'agit du nom complet de l'utilisateur ou d'un nom d'usage facilement reconnaissable. Cliquez sur Select groups et ajoutez l'utilisateur à au moins un groupe de sécurité. Un e-mail est envoyé à l'adresse e-mail de connexion. Tableau 1. Groupes de sécurité ¤ Un groupe de sécurité est un ensemble d'utilisateurs qui disposent des mêmes accès. Les droits d'un groupe de sécurité déterminent les applications, les actions et les données auxquelles ses membres peuvent accéder. Un rôle détermine ce qu'une personne peut voir et faire dans Maximo Application Suite Select. Affectez chaque utilisateur au groupe de sécurité qui correspond à son rôle : Groupe de sécurité Ce qu'ils peuvent faire System admin Gère la configuration du système et les accès des utilisateurs. Les administrateurs système peuvent configurer les domaines, les modèles de communication et les paramètres d'IA, créer des utilisateurs et définir des groupes de sécurité, mais ils n'effectuent généralement pas de travail opérationnel au quotidien. Exemples de tâches : configurer des modèles de notification, gérer les rôles des utilisateurs, définir des groupes de sécurité, configurer les paramètres système et gérer les structures de données. Supervisor Supervise les opérations et les activités de l'équipe. Les superviseurs peuvent planifier et approuver le travail, examiner le travail des techniciens, surveiller les actifs et les performances, et accéder aux analyses pour suivre l'avancement. Exemples de tâches : affecter et approuver des ordres de travail, examiner les indicateurs clés de performance, examiner les résultats d'inspection, gérer les plans de travail, et surveiller l'état des actifs et les calendriers de maintenance. Technician Effectue le travail de maintenance et le travail opérationnel. Les techniciens peuvent consulter et mettre à jour le travail qui leur est affecté, effectuer des inspections, enregistrer les heures de main-d'œuvre, déclarer les matériaux utilisés et enregistrer des données sur les actifs, comme les relevés de compteur et les détails sur l'état. Exemples de tâches : terminer des ordres de travail, saisir les résultats d'inspection, mettre à jour l'état des actifs, enregistrer les heures de main-d'œuvre, déclarer les matériaux utilisés et saisir les relevés de compteur. Requester Soumet et suit des demandes de service. Les demandeurs disposent d'un accès limité et ne peuvent pas effectuer de tâches opérationnelles ou administratives. Ce rôle consiste à lancer et à suivre des demandes de travail. Exemples de tâches : créer une demande de service pour un actif en panne et suivre son statut jusqu'à sa résolution. Inventory clerk Gère l'inventaire et les opérations du magasin. Les magasiniers peuvent tenir à jour les stocks, traiter les mouvements d'articles, ajuster les soldes d'inventaire et garantir l'exactitude des enregistrements d'inventaire. Exemples de tâches : réceptionner des articles en stock, sortir des matériaux pour des ordres de travail, effectuer des comptages d'inventaire, ajuster les soldes d'inventaire et gérer les magasins. Note Vous devez affecter au moins un groupe de sécurité. L'utilisateur ne peut pas accéder aux applications tant qu'aucun groupe de sécurité n'est affecté. Préférences utilisateur ¤ Les utilisateurs mettent à jour leurs préférences dans leur profil. Ils ouvrent le menu du profil en haut à droite de l'en-tête et peuvent sélectionner des préférences, comme une application par défaut , un magasin, des paramètres régionaux et une langue. À quoi ressemble la réussite ¤ Vous avez ajouté votre premier utilisateur avec succès lorsque : L'utilisateur peut se connecter L'utilisateur voit les applications et les menus appropriés Les droits du groupe de sécurité fonctionnent comme prévu L'utilisateur peut effectuer les tâches correspondant à son rôle Aucun message d'erreur ni problème d'accès Vous saurez que vous êtes prêt à passer à la suite lorsque vous pouvez créer des utilisateurs efficacement, attribuer les droits appropriés et résoudre seul les problèmes d'accès. Et ensuite ? ¤ Après avoir créé votre premier utilisateur, essayez de : Configurer les notifications par e-mail Définir des groupes de sécurité supplémentaires Besoin d'aide ? ¤ Si vous êtes bloqué sur votre première tâche : Consultez Pour commencer pour obtenir des réponses aux questions courantes Revoyez les notions de base dans Quels sont les concepts de base ? Une fois votre premier utilisateur ajouté, la configuration du reste de votre équipe suit les mêmes étapes, simplement répétées à plus grande échelle. Continuer à développer vos compétences ¤ Configurer vos effectifs ¤ Après avoir ajouté des utilisateurs, créez les enregistrements de métiers et de main-d'œuvre qui vous permettent d'affecter le travail aux bonnes personnes. Comment configurer la main-d'œuvre, les métiers et les équipes ? Personnaliser vos valeurs de liste déroulante ¤ Ajoutez la terminologie de votre organisation aux zones de statut et aux listes déroulantes pour que le système parle le langage de votre équipe. Comment personnaliser les valeurs de liste déroulante ?
