docs.text: How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile lets you view assigned work, complete work orders , assign and approve work, issue parts, and update records from your phone or tablet. Technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks all use IBM Maximo Mobile. Note IBM Maximo Mobile is also used with IBM Maximo Manage. If you see references to Maximo Manage, you can ignore them. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Download the app before your first shift, not during it. Sign in with the same credentials you use on the desktop. Sync your work list after signing in so your assignments are available on the device. What you need before you start ¤ A mobile device or tablet running iOS, Android, or Windows. Your Maximo Application Suite Select login credentials. Your administrator must have configured IBM Maximo Mobile for your team. If the app is not yet available, contact your administrator. Download the app ¤ On your device, open the App Store on iOS, Google Play on Android, or the Microsoft Store on Windows. Search for IBM Maximo Mobile . Download and install the app. Sign in ¤ Your first sign-in needs a network connection. The app creates a local data store on your device, which it uses when you work offline. Open IBM Maximo Mobile on your device. If the app asks for a server URL, enter your Maximo Application Suite Select server URL. Your administrator can also set the URL for you, in which case the app does not ask. Enter your username and password. Tap Sign in . [SME confirmation required: Confirm the exact sign-in screens in Select, including single sign-on prompts.] Sync your work ¤ While your device is online, the app syncs your work automatically. You can also sync manually at any time. If your device is offline, the app uses the data stored on the device and syncs when it reconnects. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the name and location of the manual sync control in Select.] What to do next ¤ Technician: Complete a work order : Complete your first work order using the app or desktop. What happens when I'm offline in IBM Maximo Mobile? : Learn how the app works without a connection. Why can't I see new work in IBM Maximo Mobile? : Fix missing work on your device. How do I find my work? : Find and filter your assigned work queue. What apps are in IBM Maximo Mobile? : Overview of all role-based mobile applications. How do I complete a work order ? : Walk through the full work order completion workflow. Related topics ¤ Technician: Complete a work order How do I find my work? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team?
docs.title: Obtenir Maximo Mobile

docs.text: Inventory clerk: Issue a part ¤ Get started quickly with a task designed for inventory clerks like you. Learn the basics while accomplishing something useful. Issue a part from the storeroom to a work order , for example, issue parts from Main storeroom. Guided steps available: Prefer to learn in the application? Log in and open your Operational dashboard to follow guided steps for issuing a part. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Always verify item numbers before issuing Keep storeroom organized and labeled Issue parts promptly to avoid work delays Record transactions immediately Check for reorder needs after issuing What to do ¤ Check for work orders needing parts. Review the parts list. Note the work order number. Go to Inventory application. Search by item number or description. Check the storeroom location . Verify quantity available. Go to the storeroom. Find the correct bin location . Verify the item number matches. Check the part condition. In Maximo, open the inventory record. Click Issue Current Item . Enter the work order number. Specify quantity to issue. Confirm the transaction. Check that inventory balance decreased. Verify work order shows the material. Confirm cost was recorded. Hand over the physical part to technician. What success looks like ¤ You've successfully issued your first part when: Inventory balance decreased by the correct quantity Work order shows the material issued with cost Transaction recorded with work order number Physical part delivered to technician Storeroom bin location updated if needed System and physical inventory match No errors or warnings in the transaction You'll know you're ready to move on when you can issue parts quickly and accurately, verify inventory balances, and handle multiple requests efficiently. Check what needs attention ¤ Your Operational Dashboard shows work queues for inventory . For example, you can see parts needed today, low stock, stagnant inventory , open material requests, and cycle counts that are due. Use them to decide what to work on first. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the work queues that the inventory clerk Operational Dashboard shows in Select.] Get IBM Maximo Mobile ¤ Take your work with you. IBM Maximo Mobile lets you issue parts and transfer items between storerooms from your phone or tablet. How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? Every part you issue accurately means one less discrepancy to chase down later. Good habits here make inventory reliable for everyone. Continue building your skills ¤ When an issue fails ¤ The most common early blocker. Learn what to check when the system won't let you issue a part to a work order . Why can't I issue materials to a work order ? Know what you have ¤ Move beyond reacting to requests. Learn to monitor stock levels so you can see what's running low before it causes a delay. How do I track stock levels? Fix a discrepancy ¤ When the system and the shelf don't match, learn how to investigate and correct it before it causes a parts shortage. docs.text: How can AI improve maintenance? ¤ Artificial intelligence features in maintenance management accelerate work order processing, assist with failure classification, and generate executive summaries of historical equipment performance. By extracting patterns from historical maintenance records, AI reduces manual administrative tasks and helps teams identify recurring failure modes. In Maximo Application Suite Select, AI capabilities focus on data enrichment, intelligent classification, and automated work summaries configured through the AI Configuration application. Looking to verify your AI readiness right away? Skip to AI configuration checklist ↓ AI maintenance capabilities ¤ Integrating AI models with maintenance workflows provides several key operational improvements: Automated work order summarization: Summarize extensive technician logs, status changes, and repair remarks into concise executive digests for shift handovers. Failure mode recommendations: Suggest relevant Problem, Cause, and Remedy failure codes based on free-form technician text entered on work orders . Asset classification assistance: Analyze asset specification attributes and recommend standardized classification hierarchies. Job plan step extraction: Draft preventive maintenance checklists and material requirements by extracting steps from digital equipment manuals. Table 1: AI capabilities and administrative configuration in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ AI capability Operational function Data requirements Configuration point Work order summarization Generates concise work summaries for closed or long-running work orders Historical work logs, actual labor hours, and technician remarks AI Configuration Failure code suggestion Matches technician descriptions to the three-tier failure hierarchy Standardized Failure Codes and historic closed work orders AI Configuration Attribute classification Recommends asset classification attributes for newly registered equipment Asset specifications, manufacturer data sheets, and Classifications Classifications, AI Configuration Predictive threshold analysis Analyzes continuous meter trends to forecast when upper action limits will breach Condition Monitoring meter history and run-hour readings Condition Monitoring Figure 1: AI configuration service and maintenance workflow integration As shown in Figure 1, the AI integration workflow ingests technician logs and routes them through a central AI service to generate three operational outputs: Input : A technician records free-form work log text and actual repair notes on a work order . AI Configuration gateway : The system routes the text securely to the configured AI model endpoint, such as a watsonx service. AI Outputs : The model returns three distinct operational enhancements: Failure code suggestions : Analyzes unstructured repair descriptions to match and suggest standardized Problem, Cause, and Remedy codes. Work order summarization : Synthesizes lengthy maintenance histories into concise summaries for shift handoffs and management digests. Attribute recommendations : Evaluates manufacturer specifications to suggest classification attribute values for newly onboarded assets . Configuring AI integration in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ System administrators configure AI model endpoints, credentials, and feature prompts in the AI Configuration application. Connecting an AI model provider in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for AI Configuration and open it. Click New AI Configuration . In the Configuration Name field, enter a unique identifier, such as WATSONX_MAINT_AI . In the Provider field, select your AI service provider. In the Model Endpoint field, specify the secure API endpoint URL. Enter the authorized API Key or authentication secret. In the Feature Toggles section, select the maintenance features to enable: Check Work Order Summaries to activate automated text synthesis on closed tickets . Check Failure Classification Recommendations to assist technicians with failure code selection. Click Test Connection to verify endpoint availability and response latency. Change the configuration status to Active , then click Save . 💡 Tip: Standardize historical data before enabling AI classification ¤ AI failure recommendations depend directly on the quality of your historical records. If past work orders contain unstandardized free text, the AI model will suggest inaccurate failure paths. Enforce clean Failure Codes on new work orders to establish a dependable training baseline. Real-world scenario: Failure code assistance at the Ice Cream Plant ¤ When a technician services Filler FL-02 for a mechanical seal failure, they might enter Replaced worn seal on filler pump due to product leakage . Instead of requiring the technician to search through hundreds of failure code records: The AI model analyzes the work text. It suggests the Failure Class PUMPS , Problem code LEAK , Cause code SEAL_WEAR , and Remedy code REPLACED . The technician verifies the suggestion with a single tap, ensuring failure data remains consistent for reliability reporting. AI configuration checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure AI features are properly integrated and governed. Table 2: AI readiness and configuration checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Secure model endpoint The AI endpoint URL is configured with valid HTTPS certificates and encrypted API keys [ ] Feature toggle validation Enabled AI capabilities match the operational workflows of your plant [ ] Active failure hierarchies Standard Problem, Cause, and Remedy failure trees are populated in Failure Codes [ ] Role access permissions Technicians and supervisors have security permissions to view AI-generated recommendations [ ] Audit monitoring Administrators review AI suggestion acceptance rates quarterly to ensure accuracy Related topics ¤ What can I automate? docs.text: What can I automate? ¤ Automating routine maintenance workflows eliminates repetitive manual scheduling, ensures preventive maintenance triggers on time, and delivers instant notifications when critical equipment anomalies occur. Instead of relying on planners to generate work orders or send status updates manually, automated background tasks handle routine administration. In Maximo Application Suite Select, automation is driven by scheduled background tasks in Cron Task lite, condition monitoring triggers, communication templates , and mobile push notifications. Looking to verify your automation readiness right away? Skip to automation readiness checklist ↓ Key automation capabilities in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Automation in Maximo Application Suite Select addresses four major operational maintenance areas: Preventive maintenance generation: Automatically creates scheduled work orders ahead of due dates based on elapsed calendar time or accumulated run hours. Condition-based work triggers: Generates corrective work orders when the gauge readings that you enter exceed defined action thresholds. Automated inventory reordering: Flags storeroom parts that drop below their minimum reorder point and creates restock requests. Instant stakeholder alerts: Dispatches email and push notifications when work orders are approved, delayed, or completed. Table 1: Automation mechanisms and operational applications ¤ Automation type Primary application How it works Operational example Scheduled PM generation Cron Task lite, PM Background process scans active PM schedules and generates work orders within a defined look-ahead window Generating weekly lubrication work orders 3 days before their due date for Filler FL-02 Condition-based triggers Condition Monitoring, Cron Task lite Monitors gauge readings and automatically issues corrective work orders upon action limit breaches Generating an urgent inspection work order when drive motor bearing temperature exceeds 80 degrees Celsius Inventory reorder calculation Inventory , Cron Task lite Calculates current balances against minimum thresholds and economic order quantities Creating restock requisitions when food-grade lubricant stock drops below 5 drums Mobile push alerts Push Notifications Administration Dispatches immediate notifications directly to technician mobile devices Alerting on-call technicians to emergency breakdowns in the Cold Storage Room Figure 1: Automated background processing architecture in Cron Task lite As shown in Figure 1, the Cron Task lite background engine automates maintenance scheduling and inventory replenishment across three core tasks and two operational dispatch channels: Background Engine (Cron Task lite) : Executes automated background processing on configured schedules without manual user intervention. Automated tasks : PMWOGENCRONTASK : Evaluates active preventive maintenance intervals and automatically generates scheduled PM work orders within configured lead times. MEASUREPOINTWOGENCRONTASK : Evaluates condition monitoring meter logs and triggers corrective work orders when action limits are breached. REORDERCRONTASK : Scans current storeroom balances and automatically creates restock requisitions for low-stock items . Dispatch outcomes : Work dispatch : Routes generated PM and condition-based work orders directly to technician mobile push alerts and supervisor Work Queue cards. Inventory dispatch : Routes generated material requisitions directly to the storeroom restock queue. Scheduled background tasks in Cron Task lite ¤ Cron tasks run on configured background schedules without requiring user intervention. System administrators manage execution intervals and parameters in the desktop application. Table 2: Essential background tasks in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Task name Frequency Function PMWoGenCronTask Nightly Evaluates preventive maintenance frequencies and generates open work orders MeasurePointWoGenCronTask Every 15 minutes Evaluates condition monitoring meter points against defined action limits ReorderCronTask Daily Analyzes storeroom balances and initiates replenishment for low-stock items Configuring PM work order generation in Cron Task lite ¤ To ensure work orders generate automatically before their maintenance due date, configure the automated generation schedule: In the Find navigation item field, search for Cron Task Setup and open it. In the Cron Task field, search for PMWOGENCRONTASK . In the Cron Task Instances table, select the active instance for your site . In the Schedule field, verify the execution frequency, such as running daily at 01:00 AM. In the Parameters table, set the LEADTIME value to 3 to generate work orders three days ahead of target start dates. Check the Active box to ensure the background task is running. In the Select Action menu, click Save Properties , then click Reload Request . 💡 Tip: Use lead time to prevent last-minute scheduling chaos ¤ Always configure a lead time on your PM generation cron task. Generating work orders 3 to 7 days before their scheduled date gives maintenance supervisors time to pre-assign technicians, confirm parts availability in the storeroom, and coordinate equipment downtime with production managers. Mobile push notifications for urgent work ¤ When equipment breaks down unexpectedly, supervisors must alert field technicians immediately. The Push Notifications Administration application routes urgent work alerts directly to technician tablets and mobile devices. Enabling mobile push alerts for emergency work ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Push Notifications Administration and open it. Select the notification event configuration for Emergency Work Orders . Verify that the trigger condition is mapped to work orders with Priority 1 or Emergency work types. Set the recipient rule to target the assigned technician and maintenance lead for the active shift. Set status to Active and click Save . Automation readiness checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure automated processes run smoothly and reliably. Table 3: Automation verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] PM generation task active PMWoGenCronTask is active and generates work orders on schedule [ ] Condition monitoring task active MeasurePointWoGenCronTask executes periodically and converts breached limits into work [ ] Inventory reorder task active ReorderCronTask flags low-stock items for procurement [ ] Communication templates mapped Automated email templates are linked to key work order status changes [ ] Push notifications configured High-priority and emergency work orders deliver instant mobile alerts Related topics ¤ How can AI improve maintenance? docs.text: How do I turn data into decisions? ¤ Collecting thousands of work orders , meter logs, and parts transactions provides no operational value unless maintenance leaders can synthesize that information into strategic decisions. Without structured reporting, management reacts to emergencies rather than proactively addressing chronic failures. Turning maintenance data into actionable decisions in Maximo Application Suite Select involves monitoring performance indicators in KPI Manager and KPI Viewer, analyzing equipment failure trends, and leveraging role-based operational dashboards. Looking to verify your decision analytics right away? Skip to decision-making analytics checklist ↓ Framework for data-driven maintenance decisions ¤ To transition from reactive firefighting to strategic asset management, connect operational metrics directly to business outcomes. Table 1: Strategic maintenance decisions and supporting metrics ¤ Decision category Core question to answer Key metrics Analytics tool Repair versus replace Has the cumulative repair cost of an asset exceeded its economic replacement value? Total Maintenance Cost, Year-to-Date Cost vs Replacement Value Assets , KPI Viewer PM optimization Are preventive maintenance routines preventing breakdowns or causing intrusive infant mortality? PM Compliance Rate, Emergency Work Ratio, MTBF KPI Manager, PM Staffing & craft planning Do we have sufficient mechanical and electrical staffing to handle the scheduled backlog? Labor Utilization, Overdue Backlog Hours by Craft Work Queue Manager, Supervisor Operational Dashboard Inventory stocking Are we holding excess capital in slow-moving stock while stocking out of critical spares? Inventory Turnover Ratio, Stockout Incidence Rate Inventory , Inventory Clerk Operational Dashboard Figure 1: Maintenance data aggregation and decision pipeline As shown in Figure 1, operational maintenance data moves through a four-stage decision pipeline from raw logging to strategic actions: Data ingestion : Field technicians and clerks log raw work logs, labor hours, and parts actuals. Aggregation engines : Data feeds in parallel into two core analytical modules: KPI Manager : Calculates compliance rates and measures performance against targets. Failure Codes : Tracks chronic root causes and failure trends. Dashboards : Operational dashboards aggregate these analytical streams into unified review screens. Strategic actions : Specific performance thresholds trigger targeted operational decisions: PM Compliance below 85 percent : Reallocate craft labor to clear maintenance backlogs. Chronic failures : Refine job plan instructions and maintenance tasks. Repair cost exceeding 60 percent of asset value : Initiate capital replacement planning. Monitoring metrics with KPI Manager and KPI Viewer ¤ KPI Manager allows reliability managers to configure mathematical metrics, set performance targets, and define Green, Yellow, and Red alert thresholds. Key performance indicator benchmarks ¤ Targeting established industry benchmarks ensures your maintenance strategy drives plant profitability. Table 2: Recommended operational KPI target thresholds ¤ Key performance indicator Benchmark target Warning threshold Critical action threshold PM Compliance Rate with 10 percent grace rule Greater than 90 percent 80 to 89 percent Below 80 percent Emergency Work Ratio Below 10 percent of total labor hours 11 to 20 percent Above 20 percent Mean Time Between Failures, MTBF Increasing month-over-month Flat Declining trend Schedule Compliance Greater than 85 percent 70 to 84 percent Below 70 percent Creating a KPI in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for KPI Manager and open it. Click New KPI . In the KPI field, enter a unique code, such as KPI_PM_COMPLIANCE . In the Description field, enter Preventive Maintenance Compliance Rate . In the Calculation field, enter the SQL select statement calculating completed PMs within allowable grace windows against total scheduled PMs. In the Target field, enter 90.00 . In the Caution at field, enter 85.00 to establish the yellow warning boundary. In the Alert at field, enter 80.00 to establish the red critical boundary. Click Save , then click Run KPI to calculate the initial value. 💡 Tip: Review KPI trends weekly rather than single-day spikes ¤ A single day drop in PM compliance often reflects a scheduled plant-wide cleaning or minor power outage. Look for four-week rolling trends in KPI Viewer before making permanent adjustments to craft staffing or job plans . Real-world decision: Filler FL-02 repair versus replace analysis ¤ At the Ice Cream Main Plant, Filler FL-02 experienced four mechanical seal failures over six months. By analyzing the asset history: Total Maintenance Cost: The Assets application showed $42,000 in combined parts and overtime labor over the trailing twelve months. Replacement Cost: A new modular filling station costs $65,000. Failure Trend: Failure Codes indicated all four breakdowns originated from drive shaft misalignment causing seal wear. Decision: Rather than approving a fifth seal replacement or spending $65,000 on a complete machine replacement, engineering scheduled a targeted drive shaft realignment and bearing housing overhaul for $6,500, permanently resolving the root cause. Decision-making analytics checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure your reporting framework supports sound management decisions. Table 3: Decision-making analytics verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Core KPI activation PM compliance, emergency work ratio, and backlog hours are active in KPI Manager [ ] Role dashboard deployment Supervisors and inventory clerks review their respective Operational Dashboards daily [ ] Failure data capture Over 90 percent of corrective work orders have Problem, Cause, and Remedy codes populated [ ] Asset cost tracking Labor hours, storeroom parts, and contractor invoices are tracked against asset records [ ] Monthly review cadence Reliability leaders meet monthly to review KPI trends and adjust maintenance frequencies Related topics ¤ How do I optimize performance? How do I act on alerts? How do I reduce equipment downtime ?

docs.text: How do I optimize performance? ¤ Continuous maintenance optimization transforms a routine preventive maintenance program into a high-efficiency reliability strategy. Over time, maintenance programs accumulate outdated tasks, excessive inspection frequencies, and inaccurate time estimates that consume valuable craft labor without preventing breakdowns. Optimizing maintenance performance in Maximo Application Suite Select involves conducting PM optimization reviews, fine-tuning condition monitoring limits, refining job plan labor estimates, and eliminating chronic failure modes. Looking to verify your optimization program right away? Skip to performance optimization checklist ↓ The continuous optimization cycle ¤ Effective maintenance programs follow a closed-loop refinement cycle: Figure 1: Continuous maintenance performance optimization cycle As shown in Figure 1, continuous maintenance optimization operates as a closed-loop cycle across four progressive steps and an ongoing refinement loop: Step 1: Execute work : Technicians perform preventive, corrective, and inspection tasks in the field. Step 2: Log actuals : Technicians record accurate actual labor hours, materials used, and failure codes . Step 3: Analyze KPIs : Reliability engineers and supervisors evaluate key performance metrics, such as PM compliance and equipment availability. Step 4: Identify changes : The maintenance team pinpoints operational bottlenecks and formulates targeted process revisions. Refinement actions : Adjustments such as extending PM intervals, refining job plan torque specifications, and pre-staging replacement parts feed directly back into Step 1 for ongoing execution. Table 1: Maintenance optimization stages and techniques ¤ Optimization stage Operational focus Data analyzed Desired outcome PM frequency tuning Adjusting service intervals based on actual operating run hours Continuous meter history, PM generation counts, historical failure dates Eliminating unnecessary PMs on idle equipment Condition threshold calibration Setting realistic warning and action limits Gauge meter readings, historical reading logs Preventing alarm fatigue while ensuring early anomaly detection Job plan refinement Comparing estimated labor and parts against actual logged values Work order actuals, wrench time delays, parts issue logs Reducing job duration and eliminating missing parts delays Failure elimination Identifying chronic root causes across equipment families Failure Codes Problem, Cause, and Remedy trends Modifying operating parameters to design out recurring failures Identifying candidates for PM optimization ¤ Not all preventive maintenance tasks deliver equal value. Reviewing maintenance records often reveals tasks that can be streamlined or eliminated entirely. Table 2: Indicators that a PM routine requires optimization ¤ Observed symptom Operational diagnosis Optimization action Zero failures found over 20 consecutive PM cycles The inspection frequency is too tight or the asset operates in low-stress conditions Extend the PM frequency interval or switch to a usage-based meter trigger Failures occur immediately after scheduled PM service Intrusive teardown inspections are introducing human assembly errors Replace intrusive mechanical inspections with non-destructive condition monitoring Actual hours consistently exceed estimated hours by 50 percent Job plan instructions are missing setup steps or required tooling Revise the Job Plan to reflect realistic task durations and stage specialized tools PM work orders closed without completing tasks Technicians face time constraints or perceive the task as non-value-added Simplify the checklist in Inspection Forms to focus only on critical failure modes Refining PM intervals in the desktop application ¤ When an asset runs intermittently, calendar-based maintenance schedules generate premature work orders . Converting calendar PMs to meter -based schedules ensures servicing occurs only after true operating wear. Updating a PM schedule to usage-based triggers ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for PM and open it. Open the preventive maintenance record for the target asset , such as PM_FILLER02_SVC . In the Frequency tab, navigate to the Meter Based Frequency sub-tab. Click New Row to link a continuous meter : In the Meter field, select the run-hour meter , such as RUNHOURS . In the Frequency field, enter the operating interval, such as 500 hours. In the Estimated Run Hours per Day field, enter expected operating rates to calculate projected due dates. In the Time Based Frequency tab, clear the fixed calendar interval if the schedule should rely solely on operating hours. Click Save . 💡 Tip: Eliminate invasive PMs on sealed components ¤ Avoid scheduled tear-down inspections on sealed gearboxes, bearings, and hydraulic assemblies unless mandated by regulatory codes. Opening sealed housings introduces particulate contamination and moisture. Use oil condition monitoring and vibration analysis to dictate rebuilds. Calibrating Condition Monitoring limits ¤ Condition monitoring thresholds that are set too tight cause alarm fatigue, leading supervisors to ignore alerts. Thresholds set too loose fail to generate corrective work orders before catastrophic failure. Adjusting Action Limits in Condition Monitoring ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Condition Monitoring and open it. Open the point record, such as CP_FILLER02_MOTOR_VIB . In the Action Limits table, review historical readings captured on recent work orders . Update the Upper Action Limit to reflect the true ISO vibration velocity ceiling. Verify that the Job Plan attached to the action limit contains specific diagnostic procedures. Click Save . Performance optimization checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure your maintenance optimization processes are active and effective. Table 3: Performance optimization verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Usage-based PM conversion High-duty rotating machinery uses meter run-hour triggers rather than arbitrary calendar dates [ ] Non-invasive inspection adoption Teardown inspections are replaced with condition monitoring where technically feasible [ ] Job plan labor accuracy Estimated craft hours on job plans match actual logged labor within 15 percent variance [ ] Condition limit calibration Action limits in Condition Monitoring reflect manufacturer tolerances without false alarms [ ] Failure review cadence Engineering conducts quarterly reviews of chronic Problem and Cause codes Related topics ¤ How do I turn data into decisions? docs.text: How do I manage more assets ? ¤ As manufacturing plants expand and new production lines are commissioned, maintenance teams must manage hundreds of additional pieces of equipment. Trying to manage growing asset registries using individual, disconnected preventive maintenance records creates administrative overload and leads to missed service intervals. Scaling maintenance operations efficiently in Maximo Application Suite Select relies on Master PM templates, multi- asset Routes, parent and child equipment hierarchies, and bulk data onboarding via Data Management. Looking to verify your scaling readiness right away? Skip to scaling verification checklist ↓ Core tools for scaling asset management ¤ To scale equipment coverage without increasing administrative headcount, use four core features: Master PM templates: Maintain a single master maintenance schedule that automatically updates individual PM records across hundreds of identical machines. Multi-stop routes: Combine repetitive inspections across multiple assets or locations into a single consolidated work order . Asset hierarchies: Organize equipment into parent and child relationships to track sub-assemblies. Data Management tool: Bulk load newly commissioned assets , locations , and initial meter configurations using validated spreadsheet templates. Table 1: Scaling mechanisms and operational applications ¤ Scaling mechanism Application Operational function Plant scaling example Master PM Master PM Centralizes maintenance intervals, job plans , and seasonal triggers across equipment models Managing identical 500-hour service schedules for 30 homogenizer pumps Routes Routes Bundles multiple physical assets or locations into a single sequential work order Inspecting 45 cold storage temperature valves on a single daily shift route Parent-child trees Assets Establishes sub-assembly structures for components that move between machines Tracking drive motors and gearboxes installed on Filler FL-02 Bulk onboarding Data Management Ingests large asset registries with classifications and specifications in batches Commissioning 200 new assets for the Ice Cream Plant expansion Figure 1: Operational scaling through Master PMs and multi-stop routes As shown in Figure 1, operational scaling relies on two complementary consolidation mechanisms: Master PM cascading : A single master template, such as the 50 HP Motor Template, links to and automatically updates individual maintenance schedules across the plant, including PM 1001 for Filler FL-01 Drive Motor, PM 1002 for Filler FL-02 Drive Motor, and PM 1003 for Filler FL-03 Drive Motor. Route consolidation : A single route definition, such as the Cold Storage Daily Route, bundles multiple physical inspections into one unified work order with sequential stops, covering Stop 1: Production Room Compressor Valve, Stop 2: Cold Storage Evaporator Valve, and Stop 3: Filling Line Room Bypass Valve. Standardizing schedules with Master PMs ¤ When your facility operates dozens of identical assets , such as motors, pumps, or conveyors, creating separate PM schedules for each machine causes maintenance drift. If the manufacturer updates the recommended lubrication interval, updating each PM manually is time-consuming and error-prone. A Master PM establishes the master frequency and attached Job Plan. When you modify the Master PM, Maximo Application Suite Select cascades the update to all linked individual asset PM records. Creating a Master PM in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Master PM and open it. Click New Master PM . In the Master PM field, enter a unique identifier, such as MPM_50HP_MOTOR . In the Description field, enter Standard 50 HP Motor Quarterly Service . In the Frequency tab, set the maintenance interval, such as every 90 days or every 1,500 run hours. In the Job Plan field, select the standardized maintenance procedure. In the Select Action menu, click Create Associated PMs to link existing equipment records that match this equipment model. Click Save . Consolidating repetitive tasks with Routes ¤ Creating individual work orders for every light fixture, fire extinguisher, or conveyor bearing generates overwhelming work order volume that clutters technician task lists. The Routes application groups multiple assets or locations into a single route. When Maximo Application Suite Select generates work from a routed PM, it creates one parent work order with child tasks or multiple entries on the Multi Asset and Location table. Table 2: Comparing individual PMs versus routed maintenance ¤ Metric Individual PM approach Routed maintenance approach Work order volume 50 separate work orders generated weekly 1 consolidated work order with 50 asset stops Technician time logging Technician opens and closes 50 individual records Technician logs time once on the parent route work order Scheduling overhead Supervisor assigns 50 distinct work orders Supervisor assigns 1 route work order to the shift team Audit trail Fragmented across dozens of disconnected records Consolidated in one chronological route history Creating an asset route in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Routes and open it. Click New Route . In the Route field, enter an identifier, such as RT_COLD_INSPECT . In the Description field, enter Cold Storage Daily Temperature and Valve Inspection . In the Route Stops table, click New Row to add equipment locations in sequential walking order: In the Location field, enter COLD_ROOM_A . In the Asset field, enter the specific refrigeration valve or sensor. Repeat step 5 for all remaining stops along the inspection path. Click Save . 💡 Tip: Order route stops by physical layout ¤ When building routes, list stops in the exact physical sequence a technician walks through the facility. Sequencing stops by floor and room eliminates backtrack travel time and ensures inspectors do not overlook remote equipment. Scaling verification checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure your asset management practices are optimized for scale. Table 3: Asset scaling verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Master PM adoption Standard equipment types are linked to Master PMs rather than standalone PM records [ ] Route consolidation Minor recurring inspections and lubrication tasks are grouped into multi-stop routes [ ] Asset hierarchy depth Complex machinery like Filler FL-02 is broken down into sub-assemblies for accurate failure tracking [ ] Uniform classifications All assets within the same equipment family share identical specification attributes [ ] Bulk onboarding validation Newly imported assets pass data validation before activation Related topics ¤ How do I standardize across teams? docs.text: How do I standardize across teams? ¤ When different maintenance shifts or plant areas follow disparate procedures, equipment reliability varies widely. One shift might lubricate pump bearings using detailed manufacturer steps while another applies grease without cleaning grease fittings or checking seals. Standardizing maintenance across teams ensures uniform safety compliance, predictable job durations, consistent failure analysis, and accurate labor cost tracking. In Maximo Application Suite Select, standardization is achieved through shared Job Plans, uniform Craft definitions, standardized Failure Codes, and structured Inspection Forms. Looking to verify standardization readiness right away? Skip to cross-team standardization checklist ↓ Core standardization pillars in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ To establish consistent operational practices across all shifts and plant zones, standardize four primary elements: Standard Job Plans: Provide unambiguous, numbered task instructions, safety lockout requirements, estimated labor hours, and required spare parts. Uniform Craft and Labor structures: Define enterprise-wide craft codes, skill levels, and hourly billing rates. Structured Failure Hierarchies: Enforce a common three-tier Problem, Cause, and Remedy taxonomy across all equipment classes. Digital Inspection Forms: Replace informal walk-through checklists with version-controlled inspection templates. Table 1: Cross-team standardization pillars in Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Standardization pillar Application Operational purpose Cross-team benefit Standard procedures Job Plans Specifies exact mechanical steps and required tools Eliminates variation between day, night, and weekend shift execution Craft definitions Crafts Standardizes skill levels, certifications, and loaded hourly rates Ensures accurate labor cost estimation across departments Failure classification Failure Codes Defines uniform Problem, Cause, and Remedy failure paths Enables plant-wide reliability engineering and root cause comparison Digital inspections Inspection Forms Standardizes quality, sanitation, and safety audit sheets Guarantees compliance records match regulatory audit requirements Figure 1: Cross-shift standardization structure and unified reporting As shown in Figure 1, the cross-shift standardization architecture connects central standards to operational execution and executive reporting: Enterprise Standards : Central definitions establish baseline consistency: Standard Crafts : Enforce uniform labor billing rates and skill progressions. Standard Job Plans : Mandate identical procedural steps, safety controls, and required parts. Standard Failure Codes : Define uniform Problem, Cause, and Remedy failure options. Shift Execution : Both Day Maintenance and Night Maintenance follow the identical procedures and log data using the same failure codes . Unified Reporting : Operational execution feeds clean, structured data into KPI Viewer, enabling true benchmark comparisons across shifts and departments. Creating standardized Job Plans ¤ A well-constructed Job Plan removes guesswork for technicians. When a work order generates for Filler FL-02, the attached job plan details exact torque specifications, required seal replacement kits, and food safety sanitation steps. Creating a Job Plan in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Job Plans and open it. Click New Job Plan . In the Job Plan field, enter an identifier, such as JP_FILLER_SEAL_SVC . In the Description field, enter Filler FL-02 Mechanical Seal Service and Inspection . In the Tasks table, click New Row to add numbered operational steps: Task 10: Isolate power and apply lockout and tagout locks to main disconnect. Task 20: Drain product lines and flush pump housing with clean water. Task 30: Remove mechanical seal housing and inspect drive shaft for pitting. Task 40: Install new food-grade mechanical seal kit and torque bolts to 25 Nm. Task 50: Remove lockout tags, restore power, and conduct 15-minute leak check. In the Labor tab, add required craft hours, such as 2 hours of Mechanical Technician, MECH . In the Materials tab, specify required storeroom items , such as the replacement seal kit and food-grade lubricant. In the Select Action menu, change status to Active , then click Save . 💡 Tip: Version job plans rather than overwriting active procedures ¤ When updating standard operating procedures, use the Revision feature in Job Plans. Revising a job plan preserves historical records on completed work orders while ensuring new work orders automatically adopt the latest approved safety standards. Configuring uniform Crafts and Labor rates ¤ Standardizing craft codes ensures that work plans accurately predict job costs regardless of which specific technician is assigned. Table 2: Example craft hierarchy for manufacturing facilities ¤ Craft code Description Skill levels Standard hourly rate MECH Mechanical Technician Apprentice, Journeyman, Master $45.00 to $65.00 ELEC Electrical Technician Journeyman, Master $55.00 to $75.00 HVAC Refrigeration Specialist Journeyman, Master $60.00 to $80.00 LUBE Lubrication Technician Standard $35.00 to $45.00 Creating a Craft in the desktop application ¤ In the Find navigation item field, search for Crafts and open it. Click New Craft . In the Craft field, enter the code, such as MECH . In the Description field, enter Mechanical Maintenance Technician . In the Standard Rate field, enter the default loaded hourly labor cost. In the Skill Levels table, click New Row to define progression levels, such as JOURNEY and MASTER . Change status to Active and click Save . Cross-team standardization checklist ¤ Use this checklist to ensure all maintenance teams operate under unified standards. Table 3: Cross-team standardization verification checklist ¤ Check Item What to verify [ ] Universal job plan coverage Recurring preventive maintenance work orders have active, standardized Job Plans linked [ ] Craft rate accuracy All active crafts have current loaded hourly rates populated in Crafts [ ] Standard failure codes Technicians across all shifts select from the identical Problem, Cause, and Remedy tree [ ] Digital inspection templates Paper check sheets are replaced with active digital forms in Inspection Forms [ ] Shift calendar synchronization Team working hours and on-call schedules are updated in Calendar Related topics ¤ How do I manage more assets ?
